title: Alpha Omega Chardonnay Napa Valley

paras.text: Our Chardonnay is as low-impact as they come in the cellar, naturally fermented, unfined, unfiltered and barely touched during its evolution. Six different clones add their own unique flavor harmonies, and we achieve further precision and balance by an 18-month sur-lie aging process in French oak. The result is an elegant yet opulent Chardonnay that calls to mind a classic Meursault with a California suntan.

title: Alpha Omega II Chardonnay

paras.text: II is the culmination of the two worlds, the Alpha and the Omega, the Old World and the New World. Winemakers, Jean Hoefliger and Michel Rolland worked to create a wine that is not only opulent, fruit forward and generous, but also has the backbone of European acidity and elegance. A reflection of both worlds, II is a wine that
On the nose: explosion of bubble gum, pear, dark chocolate and granite with touches of citrus
On the palate: soft candy-like entrance evolving on a sweet acidity with touches of lemon candy, mango and pears lingering on grape- fruit and guava

title: Alpha Omega ERA

paras.text: ERA, Alpha Omega’s flagship wine, represents the highest level of dedication to handcrafting a wine which serves as the confluence of Old World traditions and New World techniques. Our Consulting Winemakers, Jean Hoefliger and Michel Rolland, work together to blend a wine which highlights the exceptional diversity of Napa Valley terroir. ERA is a blend of Cabernet Sauvignon from eight award winning and historic vineyards in Napa Valley and is handcrafted, barrel-fermented with its natural wild yeast, and is not fined or filtered. Alpha Omega’s unique style of blending Cabernet Sauvignons from various terroirs crafts a wine with the perfect balance of depth, intensity and elegance.

title: Alpha Omega II Red Wine Napa Valley

paras.text: II is the culmination of the two worlds, the Alpha and the Omega, the Old World and the New World. Our two winemakers, Jean Hoefliger and Michel Rolland, worked to create a wine that is not only opulent, fruit-forward and generous, but also has the backbone of European acidity and elegance. A reflection of both worlds, II is a wine that is built to be approachable, both in taste and price, and consumed early.
Blend: 52% Cabernet Sauvignon, 23% Petit Verdot, 18% Merlot, 4% Malbec, 3% Cabernet Franc.

title: Alpha Omega Proprietary Red Napa Valley

paras.text: This Cabernet-dominant wine was designed to be a Bordeaux blend with pure Napa Valley pedigree. Utilizing vineyards such as Sunshine Valley Vineyard, we created a dense wine that has more diversity in its profile. We consider our Proprietary Red the intellectual offering of our current releases.
On the nose: strong dark chocolate with rose candy lingering on cinnamon, nutmeg and granite
On the palate: velvety, silky entrance with soft ripe strawberry and mango with hints of juicy blueberries and ripe plums lingering on cassis and wisteria

title: Alpha Omega Cabernet Sauvignon Napa Valley

paras.text: When our winemaking team has complete control over our vineyard blocks, magic happens in the cellar. Blending for ripeness and structure, four properties lent a hand to the cause here. Just enough cooler-climate fruit adds sophistication and style to our Napa Cabernet bombshell. Black fruits, blueberries, allspice, subtle oak toast and a long, luxurious finish define one of our signature bottlings.
On the nose: beautiful, elegant cedar with touches of thyme, sawdust, locorice, pine needles, plum, tapenade, sour cherry and lemon meringue pie
On the palate: soft, velvety entrance evolving on beautiful fruit and fine tannins, lingering on boysenberries, darkcherries, mandarin orange, star fruit and wild raspberry

title: Altocedro Ano Cero Cabernet Sauvignon

paras.text: A dark and dense color along with ripe, mossy aromas of herbal black fruits and grilled meat create interest and confidence prior to a full but sappy and drying palate that's more jammy than fit. Spicy oak and herbal black fruit flavors hold their own on a weighty finish.

title: Altocedro Ano Cero Cabernet Sauvignon La Consulta Mendoza

paras.text: We strive for a La Consulta-terroir driven Cabernet Sauvignon that is fresh, fruit-forward, and easy-to-drink. Altocedro means “tall cedar,” and represents both winemaker and owner Karim Mussi Saffie's Lebanese-Argentine heritage, and a cedar tree which towers over the winery.Total Production: 750 cases
Vineyards: La Consulta, Valle de Uco, MendozaSoil: Alluvial, sandy loam, rocky bottom

title: Altocedro Ano Cero Malbec La Consulta Mendoza

paras.text: We strive for a La Consulta-terroir driven Malbec that is fresh, fruit-forward, and easy-to-drink. Altocedro means “tall cedar,” and represents both winemaker and owner Karim Mussi Saffie's Lebanese-Argentine heritage, and a cedar tree which towers over the winery.

title: Altocedro Ano Cero Malbec

paras.text: A blend of Malbec, Cabernet, Tempranillo and Syrah: Full medium ruby. Extremely ripe aromas of cassis, blackberry, dark chocolate and graphite. Fat, plush, silky and sweet, with thick blackberry and chocolatey oak flavors given shape by just enough acidity. This lush blend delivers and impressive wave of fruit and finishes with palate-saturating length.
“Fermented with indigenous yeasts in concrete vats… some floral aromas… very good varietal characteristics… great freshness… the palate is juicy, fresh and tasty… delicious.”

title: Altocedro Ano Cero Tempranillo

paras.text: We strive for a La Consulta-terroir driven Tempranillo that is fresh, fruit-forward, and easy-to-drink.
Label Notes: Altocedro means “tall cedar,” and represents both winemaker and owner Karim Mussi Saffie's Lebanese-Argentine heritage, and a cedar tree which towers over the winery.
Fermentation and Maceration: Entire berry fermentation with indigenous yeasts in small concrete tank; gravity-fed. 7 days at 27C.
Winemaking: 10% bleed-off, four pump-overs per day; two total delestages; no filtering; natural cold stabilization

title: Altocedro Malbec Reserva

paras.text: We strive for a La Consulta-terroir driven Malbec that is complex and concentrated. Big and rich-tasting, with concentrated flavors of dark plum, dried blackberry and dark currant, flanked by luscious Asian spice notes. Very creamy as well, offering a plush, open-textured finish of dark chocolate and mocha.

“Big and rich-tasting, with concentrated flavors of dark plum, dried blackberry and dark currant, flanked by luscious Asian spice notes. Very creamy as well, offering a plush, open-textured finish of dark chocolate and mocha.”

title: Altocedro Malbec Gran Reserva

paras.text: We strive for a La Consulta-terroir driven Malbec that is elegant with great depth. Very dark, but juicy and driven, with a mouthwatering streak of briar and anise that pushes the muscular core of raspberry, fig and boysenberry fruit. Graphite and black tea notes flash in the background. The finish is long and structured.

"Very dark, but juicy and driven, with a mouthwatering streak of briar and anise that pushes the muscular core of raspberry, fig ad boysenberry fruit. Graphite and black tea notes flash in the background. The finish is long and structured."

title: Arnaud Lambert Samur Blanc Clos David

paras.text: Terroir: Northeast-facing, 70 cm lightly silty sandy soil on softer Turonian limestone bedrock
and 50% in barrel (15% new oak). Aged for 12 months in barrel, an additional 6 months blending and aging in tank.

title: Arnaud Lambert Saumur Blanc Clos de la Rue

paras.text: Vinification: Indigenous yeast fermentation in oak barrels (35% new). Aged for 24 months in barrel, additional 6 months blending and aging in tank.

title: Arnaud Lambert Saumur Rouge Clos du Tue-Loup

paras.text: Vinification: 100% de-stemmed, 10-15 days maceration, indigenous yeast fermentation: ½ in 2 to 3-year-old barrels and ½ in raw concrete tanks for 8 months. They are then assembled and aged for 6 months in stainless steel tanks before bottling where they are aged for 6-12 months in bottle before release (35mg/L total SO

title: Arnaud Lambert Saumur Blanc Clos de Midi

paras.text: Terroir: Facing southeast, 70 cm of silty/ sandy clay soil on softer Turonian limestone rock
Vinification: Indigenous yeast fermentation, 50% in stainless steel tanks, 50% in older Burgundian barrels. Aged for 12 months.

title: Arnaud Lambert Saumur Rouge Clos Mazurique

paras.text: Vinification: 100% de-stemmed, indigenous yeast fermentation in concrete tanks, no pump-overs. Aged for 5 months in concrete tank (15mg/L total SO

title: Babylon's Peak Chenin Blanc

paras.text: Babylon's Peak winery, situated on the highest weathered granite slopes of the Paardeberg Mountain, is privately owned by the Basson family who has passed down the tradition, passion and art of winemaking over four generations.

The Chenin Blanc grapes were picked from very old dryland bushvine vineyards. The vineyard grows on weathered granite soils, contributing to the flavor of the grapes and mineral character of the wine. Production is limited to 5 tons/ha.

Vinification: The grapes were harvested by hand at 22.1°B. The grapes were destalked and lightly crushed. Only the first 450 liters free-run juice per ton were fermented in stainless steel tanks at a cold temperature (10-12°C) for 21 days. The wines was left on the fermentation lees until bottling.
Pairings: Salads, seafood, chicken and other light dishes. The perfect wine for every occasion.

title: Babylon's Peak Paardeberg Shiraz

paras.text: Babylon's Peak winery, situated on the highest weathered granite slopes of the Paardeberg Mountain, is privately owned by the Basson family who has passed down the tradition, passion and art of winemaking over four generations. Predominantly low-yield dryland bushvines are selected to produce these excellent wines with distinctive character.
A classic Shiraz with dark fruit, violets and white pepper. An elegant wine with ripe tannins and a lingering aftertaste.

Vinification: The grapes were harvested by hand. The grapes were destalked only, no crushing was done. Cold maceration was done before fermentation started in open fermenters. The grapes fermented between 24-26°C for 5-7 days, after which the wine was taken to barrels where it went through malolactic fermentation. After malolactic fermentation was completed, the wine spent 14 months in 225 litre French oak barrels until bottling.

title: Leda Pucci Rosso di Toscana Sangiovese

paras.text: PRODUCTION TECHNIQUES: Harvest at the end of the month of September, classic vinification with 2 daily pumpings over at a controlled temperature of 28°C and 10 days of maceration. After racking and subsequent malolactic fermentation, the wine is prepared for bottling, which takes place 10-12 months after harvesting.
SERVING SUGGESTIONS: It easily pairs with appetizers, first courses and non-spicy second courses.

title: Domaine La Bastide Blanche Bandol Rose

paras.text: The rosé, produced about 80,000 bottles a year, is composed of Cinsault and Grenache Mourvedre. It is obtained by direct pressing of Mourvèdre and maceration of 24 hours of Grenache and Cinsault. Malolactic fermentation will be based varieties. The wines will be raised from 4 to 10 months in tank before placing on the market.

Every January, this cuvée is assembled by Peter Weygandt at the domaine with Stéphane Bourret (wine-maker) and the Bronzo family so every year the blend is a little different, but the quality and signature "Bastide Blanche Bandol rosé" character never strays. Dominant Mourvèdre with about equal parts Cinsault and Grenache from hand-harvested grapes on clay-limestone soil with cailloux, yielding only about 36hL/ha. About 1100 cases produced

title: Domaine La Bastide Blanche Bandol Rouge

paras.text: A stunning value from Bandol - hand-harvested at low yields of 36hL/ha. Entirely destemmed, 22 day fermentation on indigenous yeasts with occasional pigeage in foudre. Aged in large foudre.

title: Benjamin Leroux Batard-Montrachet Grand Cru

paras.text: Terroir: The Chassagne side of the appellation, just across the road from the DRC's vines
Vinification: Directly pressed, light settling before transfer to barrel (15% new), indigenous yeast fermentation. Aged for 16 months, fined, unfiltered.

title: Benjamin Leroux Bourgogne Aligoté

paras.text: Terroir: The older half of vines are gobelet-pruned and located in Bouzeron, the other younger half are near Meursault
Vinification: Directly pressed, settling before transfer to older oak barrels for indigenous yeast fermentation. Aged for 12 months, fined and/or filtered if necessary.
Benjamin first made this wine in 2016, using exclusively old Aligoté Doré vines from Bouzeron. The following year he included Aligoté from a newly-acquired vineyard worked by the Leroux team.

title: Benjamin Leroux Bourgogne Côte d'Or

paras.text: Terroir: Blend of parcels from the Hautes-Côtes de Nuits, Santenay, Beaune, Ladoix, Savigny-lès-Beaune, and/or Fixin, depending on the vintage
Vinification: 100% de-stemmed, 10 days maceration, indigenous yeast fermentation. Aged for 12 months in older oak barrels, unfined, unfiltered.

title: Benjamin Leroux Chambertin Grand Cru
Benjamin Leroux Clos de la Roche Grand Cru

paras.text: Vinification: ⅓ whole-cluster, indigenous yeast fermentation, 15 days maceration. Aged for 18 months in oak barrel (33% new), unfined, unfiltered.

title: Benjamin Leroux Clos Saint-Denis Grand Cru

paras.text: A notably spicy nose exhibits equally elegant and cool aromas of plum, dark currant and Asian style tea nuances. There is fine intensity to the refined medium weight flavors that possess a subtle minerality on the punchy and muscular finish that is an exercise in harmony and balance.
Vinification: Mostly de-stemmed, indigenous yeast fermentation. Aged for 18 months in barrel (up to 50% new oak), unfined, unfiltered.

title: Benjamin Leroux Gevrey-Chambertin Aux Etelois

paras.text: Vinification: 80-100% de-stemmed, indigenous yeasts, 18 months aging in barrel (20% new oak), unfined, unfiltered.

title: Benjamin Leroux Meursault Les Vireuils

paras.text: Terroir: High altitude, just below the forest at top of hill, facing east/southeast,
Vinification: Whole-cluster pressing, light settling before transfer to 300L barrels (15% new oak), indigenous yeast fermentation. Aged for 18 months, fined and/or filtered only if necessary.

title: Benjamin Leroux Meursault Premier Cru Genevrières Dessous

paras.text: Terroir: Two parcels in the lower part of the appellation with gravelly limestone soils
Vinification: Directly pressed, light settling, transfer to barrels (15-20% new oak), indigenous yeast fermentation. Aged for 16 months, fined and/or filtered if necessary.

title: Benjamin Leroux Nuits-Saint-Georges Premier Cru Aux Boudots

paras.text: Terroir: Upper slope, rocky soil, particularly small bunches of Pinot Fin typical of neighboring Vosne
Vinification: About 60% whole-cluster, indigenous yeast fermentation. Aged in barrel (⅓ new).

title: Benjamin Leroux Vosne-Romanée Premier Cru Au Dessus des Malconsorts

paras.text: Vinification: About 80% whole-cluster, indigenous yeast fermentation, 15 days maceration in tank. Aged for 18 months in barrel, no new oak.
As Ben makes very little of this cuvée (just one barrel in 2016), he chooses not to age it in new oak, but rather in a barrel that he has already used for one or two vintages.

, under 600 square meters in total, with just a couple owners including Grivot and Ben's source. In 2016, when neighboring Echezeaux was badly hit by frost, this parcel was spared. In the middle of the parcel are four very particular vines. The current owner's father brought them from Algeria when he returned to Burgundy after his military service, and harvested them separately for simple table grapes.

title: Benjamin Leroux Volnay Premier Cru Les Caillerets

paras.text: Vinification: 2/3 whole-cluster, indigenous yeast fermentation. Aged for 12 months in barrel (25-30% new oak depending on the year).

title: Benjamin Leroux Savigny-les-Beaune Premier Cru Les Hauts Jarrons

paras.text: Vinification: 85-90% de-stemmed, 15 days in tank, 18 months aging in 300-l barrels (10% new oak), unfined, unfiltered.

title: Bernard Fouquet, Domaine des Aubuisières Vouvray Cuvée Sur Silex

paras.text: A sec (dry) Vouvray from 2 flint soil parcels. Entirely hand-harvested and only indigenous yeasts used. Fermented and matured in stainless steel thermo-regulated vats.

title: Bernard Fouquet, Domaine des Aubuisières Vouvray Les Girardières

paras.text: Food suggestions: Aperitif, cold and cured meat, fish, shellfish, white meat, cheese persillée. Best time for drinking this wine: Now, can be aged for 10 years.

title: Birgit Eichinger Grüner Veltliner "Hasel"

paras.text: The name for this site is derived from the the hazel bush, which thrives in the Kamptal region under the same moist conditions as the vines.
A wonderful nose of light spice, with underlying yellow fruit aromas, and delicate white pepper. Succulent and mouthfilling, glides really easily across the palate, with a nice echo.

title: Black Cabra Malbec Mendoza

paras.text: We strive to achieve a great value Malbec with lush flavors of plums, strawberries, cherries and a hint of vanilla with a fresh and balanced mouthfeel.
Label Notes: Our wines, like the Black Cabra (goat), come from the Argentine Andes.
Winery: Fincas Patagonicas (Tapiz & Zolo) Vineyards: Estate Mendoza vineyardsVarietal: 100% Malbec

Winemaking: A cold pre-maceration takes place (5o- 8oC) for 3 days to extract color and aromas. Fermented in stainless steel tanks for approx 10 to 14 days at 27oC in contact with French innerstaves. Malolactic Fermentation: 100%

title: Black Cabra Cabernet Sauvignon Mendoza

paras.text: We strive to achieve a great value, varietally-correct Cabernet Sauvignon with flavors of cassis, berry jam, and a hint of pepper with a long and creamy finish.
Label Notes: Our wines, like the Black Cabra (goat), come from the Argentine Andes.
Vineyards: Estate Mendoza vineyardsVarietal: 100% Cabernet SauvignonSustainably Farmed: 100%

Winemaking: A cold pre-maceration takes place (5o- 8oC) for 3 days to extract color and aromas. Fermented in stainless steel tanks for approx 10 to 14 days at 27oC in contact with French innerstaves.Malolactic Fermentation: 100%

title: Bodegas Riojanas Canchales Rioja Joven Tinta

paras.text: Classical vinification with destalked, crushed grapes using the most advanced techniques and with whole grapes in winegrowers' fermentation pools using carbonic maceration.
Cherry-red with violet hues, brillant. Fragant primary aromas. Fresh, fruity varietal. Smooth and balanced in the mouth. Slight tannis. Wide, long retronasal sensations with elegant fruity notes.

title: Bodegas Riojanas Pregón Verdejo

paras.text: Made with the variety verdejo coming from grapes selected from vineyards between 10 and 20 years. Night grape harvest.
Straw yellow color with green ishirises. Clean and bright. Aroma to white fruits with an herbal and aniseed background. In the mouth it is tasty, fresh and balanced. Soft and persistent finish.

title: Bodegas Riojanas Veiga Naum Albarino

paras.text: Light, yellow straw color in the glass with green-gold nuances.Nicely combines fruit and floral notes on the nose with good aromatic intensity. A lovely example of the varietal Albariño. The attack is fresh and fruit driven and the wine remains enjoyable and aromatic along the length of the palate.Complete with very pleasant finish that is fragrant and persistent.

title: Bodegas Riojanas Vina Albina Crianza

paras.text: Grapes were harvested with great care using classical elaboration, then destemmed and lightly crushed, utilizing the latest techniques to control fermentation, followed by an extended maceration.
Aging: Aged 18 months in American oak barrels for optimal tannin integration, including an additional 6 months in the bottle prior to release for optimum maturity.

Tasting Notes: Bright cherry red color with Fresh fruit and licorice aromas along with pronounce notes of spice and toasty flavours stemming from the new oak. Soft in the mouth with pleasant and velvety tannins on a nice long harmonious finish. As a result this wine with its structure and complexity could have been classified as a Rioja Reserve with additional oak aging.

title: Bonneau du Martray Corton-Charlemagne Grand Cru

paras.text: Bonneau du Martray’s Corton-Charlemagne is a difficult wine to describe. This is particularly true when it is young. It can take a decade before it will say something more than “Stony. Wait.” But even with age, it does not bloom in the same manner as the Montrachets do. In a way, it tastes like theoretical astronomy: we know that black matter exists. We can sense it, but we have no manifest proof of it. It’s a very beautiful agony.
Terroir: 15 contiguous west-facing parcels in En Charlemagne and Le Charlemagne. There is almost no clay in the topsoil which is made of silt and sand, it lays over white marl. Up to 30% grade.
Vinification: Alcoholic fermentation with indigenous yeasts. Lee-stirring as needed. Aging initially in oak barrels (30% new), racking to tank with fine lees over winter.

title: Bret Brothers & La Soufrandière Pouilly-Fuissé En Carementrant

paras.text: Terroir: Below the Roche de Vergisson, 350-meters elevation, facing south, clay soil with high limestone content
Viticulture: As of 2019, exclusively from grapes that are certified organic or in the process of certification
Vinification: Whole-cluster pressing, indigenous yeast fermentation. Aged for 11 months in 228L barrels (older oak). 5-6 months blending in stainless steel tanks.

The Brets’ domaine, La Soufrandière, has been certified biodynamic since its early days. For the wines made from purchased grapes, not only have the brothers been unimpeachably transparent as to what was organic/biodynamic or not, but, like the menu in a farm to table restaurant, they have always, and without solicitation, named the farmer.
Their honesty and extremely high standards have led the brothers to make most of their negociant wines from verifiably organic fruit for quite a few years (the proportion was 80% organic in 2018.)
And we are very proud to announce that as of the 2019 vintage, all the fruit for every Bret Brothers wine is now either certified organic or in the process of certification.

title: Bret Brothers & La Soufrandière Pouilly-Fuisse Terres de Fuisse

paras.text: Soil: Clay and limestone. The older plot lies on particularly white limestone. The other East-facing up the hill on shallow pebbly soil
Vinification & Ageing : Hand-picked grapes, whole berries pressing, 100% vinified and aged in oak barrel (of 228 liters each) for 11 months

title: Bret Brothers & La Soufrandière Pouilly-Vinzelles

paras.text: Vinification: Whole-cluster pressing, indigenous yeast fermentation. Aged for 11 months, 80% in tank, 20% in 228L barrels (older oak).
The appellation of Pouilly-Vinzelles is only 52 hectares (128.5 acres) large, in comparison to neighboring Pouilly-Fuissé, which is 750 hectares (1,850 acres).

title: Bret Brothers & La Soufrandière Saint Veran La Côte Rotie

paras.text: Vinification & Ageing : Hand-picked grapes, whole berries pressing, 100% vinified and aged in oak barrel (of 228 liters each) for 11 months.

Geographically opposite to our Saint-Véran « En Combe » compared to the Pouilly-Fuissé area (see Map of Bret Brothers), this terroir « La Côte Rôtie » lies at the foot of the Roche de Vergisson, around the village of Davayé. Its name comes from its very steep slope (over 40%) facing full South. The soil is calcarous but, as one may guess, it is a very solar wine, both rich and fruity. 2007 is once more an explosive wine!

title: Giacomo Brezza Langhe Rosato

paras.text: This wine presents important primary aromas (floral, rose, and peach), it is less dense and less tannic on the palate than the Langhe Nebbiolo. Ready to dink, is great as an aperitif, with fish, or a nice summer menu.

This Rosato wine has been produced since the end of the 70’s thanks to my father Oreste. This wine is the result of vinification of red grapes, where after one night in contact with the skins about 2% of the juice is taken off to finish its fermentation alone with a temperature of 20 °C / 68 °F. After the alcoholic fermentation is complete we will maintain the wine at a lower temperature because we do not want it to go through malolactic fermentation, helping to maintain the typical grape acidity. Unlike the French Rosé which are similar to a white wine, Italian Rosato are much closer to a red wine: they are in fact more colorful and fuller bodied.

title: Giacomo Brezza Barolo Sarmassa

paras.text: In ancient times, this area was called Salmassa, a name that probably originates from a source of brackish water welling up in its vicinity.

The soil of this vineyard, as is in the towns of Barolo and La Morra is made mostly from SANT’AGATA FOSSIL MARNE (TOV). The wines produced here are of grater quality in dry years: in fact, the highest percentage of clay and silt ensures a larger water retention, resulting in less stress on the vines that dwell in this land.

The winemaking system is one very close to the traditional method for Nebbiolo from Barolo, with a difference in the length of maceration which in this case is generally higher because the grapes have usually softer tannins.

Barolo coming from this vineyard is much more elegant resulting in an earlier readiness for consumption. The usual combination suggest the game and read meat but given its elegance, goes well also for the whole meal. This Barolo produced by the family only in great vintages with an indication of the MEGA (Additional Mention of the Geographic) in about 9/10 years after the harvest you will have a great wine for conversation and therefore only recommended in very good company.

title: Domaine Brusset Cotes du Rhone

paras.text: The Côtes du Rhône has superb purity and freshness in its dark cherry, graphite, leather and dried spice-driven bouquet. Tasting like a mini-Gigondas, with medium-bodied richness and depth, and a focused, masculine feel on the palate, drink it over the coming 3-5 years.
Vinification : Destalking, fermentation between 8 to 10 days at 28°C. with regular "délestages". Each grape variety is vinified separately then blended after malolactic fermentation.

title: Domaine Brusset Ventoux Les Boudalles

paras.text: Winemaking: De-stemming, fermenting 8 days at 26 ° C with daily pumping, two power cuts.

title: Domaine Brusset Gigondas Le Grand Montmirail

paras.text: Grape varieties: Grenache, Mourvèdre, Syrah. Vineyards established on small terraces.
Harvest : Hand-picked and strictly selected according to a variety of ripeness checks.

Vinification : Crushing, destalking, cold prefermentation. Separate fermentation for each grape variety during 30 days, « pigeage », temperature control. Maturing: 50% in french oak-casks (part of new) according to the vintage.

Appearance : A very deep, dark crimson robe. Aroma : A rich, fruity, spicy and complex aroma. Taste : Very round and powerful, long-lasting flavour. Consistent tannins, pleasantly woody with a deeper flavour of blackberry and chocolate.

title: Camille Giroud Chambertin Grand Cru

paras.text: Vinification: 100% de-stemmed, cold maceration, 18 days' fermentation in open wood tank. 18 months' aging on lees in oak barrels (50% new oak), racked once, 3 months' settling in stainless steel tank.

title: Camille Giroud Bourgogne Rouge

paras.text: Long Bois, Mon Poulain), Gevrey-Chambertin, Côte Chalonnaise (Moroges), all clay-limestone soils
Vinification: 100% de-stemmed, 1 year aging on fine lees in oak barrels, 3 months' settling in stainless steel tank.

title: Camille Giroud Chassagne-Montrachet Les Vergers Premier Cru

paras.text: Vinification: Direct pressing, indigenous yeast fermentation. Aged in barrel (20% new). Blending in stainless steel tanks.

title: Camille Giroud Chambolle-Musigny Les Borniques Premier Cru

paras.text: This vineyard sits next to Musigny. The quality of the site is evidenced by the first sniff of the glass, with a seductive perfume of violets, redcurrants and a dash of white pepper. Classically Chambolle, with a touch of extra roundness and flesh courtesy of the vintage, there are just two barrels in 2018.

title: Camille Giroud Chassagne-Montrachet Tonton Marcel Premier Cru

paras.text: of Grande Montagne, a small island of vines high up among bare hillside which is too rocky to be planted. The minerality of this wine, just two barrels of which have been made, is evident from the gunflint-infused nose. Chewy with real grip and spice, this is a wine of remarkable weight and density.
Vinification: Direct pressing, indigenous yeast fermentation. Aged in barrel (20% new). Blending in stainless steel tanks.

title: Camille Giroud Clos De La Roche Grand Cru

paras.text: (facing northeast, Dijon Corton limestone subsoil with layer of marl and fossils)
Vinification: Directly pressed, indigenous yeast fermentation in 228L and 600L oak barrels.

title: Camille Giroud Ladoix Les Chaillots

paras.text: Terroir: Lower on the northeast side of the hill of Corton, south/southeast-facing, limestone scree and silt soil with a lot of siliceous stones
Vinification: 100% de-stemmed, 5-6 days' cold maceration in wood tank. 15 months' aging on lees in oak barrels (10% new) without racking.

title: Camille Giroud Gevrey-Chambertin Lavaut Saint Jacques Premier Cru
Camille Giroud Corton-Charlemagne Grand Cru

paras.text: Terroir: From Rognet et Corton (at 320m altitude, limestone soil with Callovian marls) and Le Charlemagne (clay-limestone soils with Pernand white marls)
Vinification: Pressing, 24 hours' settling, alcoholic fermentation and 1 year aging in older oak barrels (no bâtonnage). Racked to stainless steel tank 3 months before bottling.

title: Camille Giroud Mercurey

paras.text: Maison Camille Giroud ranks among the most venerable as well as the most dynamic of the boutique négociants in Burgundy. Founded in 1865, Giroud earned an impeccable reputation over the last 150 years as a specialist in traditional vins de garde. Their principal business model was to acquire wines from the top vineyards and after aging them in seasoned barrels, selling the fully mature wines.

In 2001, Giroud was acquired by a group of investment bankers led by wine collector Joe Wender and his wife, Napa cult vintner Ann Colgin. They hired wunderkind David Croix not only to manage the distinguished cellar but also to begin acquiring grapes and making first-class wines. Croix accomplished this goal with flying colors and has now been succeeded by the highly-talented Carel Voorhuis.

Maison Camille Giroud occupies a singular niche in Burgundy: it is at the same time among the most dependable and exciting sources of fully mature, traditional Burgundy, and one of the best sources for transparent, terroir-driven current-vintage Burgundy.

title: Camille Giroud Pommard Premier Cru Les Épenots

paras.text: Vinification: De-stemmed, aged for 18 months in barrel (15% new oak), a few months blending in stainless steel tank pre-bottling.

title: Camille Giroud Vosne-Romanée Les Chaladins

paras.text: Terroir: Borders the bottom of the Clos de Vougeot Grand Cru, 220-meters elevation, facing southeast
Vinification: 30% whole-cluster. Aged for 16 monthsin barrel (30% new), 3 months settling in tank.

title: Camille Giroud Vosne-Romanée Les Suchots Premier Cru

paras.text: Terroir: 235 to 300-meters elevation, facing south/southeast, calcareous and marly soils
Vinification: 50% de-stemmed, 3 to 4 gentle punch-downs per day. Aged for 18 months in barrel (no new oak), a few months blending in stainless steel tank before bottling.

title: Camille Savès Champagne Bouzy Grand Cru Extra Brut

paras.text: This is our House's top-of-the range Champagne, synonymous with an exceptional year, made from the best cuvees of Pinot Noir and Chardonnay from vines that are older than 35 years of age growing in the heart of the Bouzy Grand Cru "terroir".
Palate: Roundness marked by red fruits, with a great persistency showing it has good "keeping" potential.

title: Bret Brothers & La Soufrandière Pouilly-Vinzelles Climat Les Quarts

paras.text: Soil: clay and limestone, very high red iron oxide on Bajocian. On the highest and most stony part of « les Quarts »
Vinification & Ageing : Hand-picked grapes, whole berries pressing, 100% vinified and aged in oak barrel (of 228 liters each) for 11 months.

title: Cave de Pomérols Picpoul de Pinet

paras.text: Pale yellow color with green tints. Fresh and fine aromas of grapefruit and exotic fruit. Lime flavors, with typical focusing acidity, are hallmarks of Picpoul. This wine impresses novices and hardened geeks equally.

title: Cave De Sancerre Sancerre Armoiries

paras.text: Light, crisp, and dry with aromas and flavors of citrus, quince, and mineral. Perfect with fish, salad, appetizers, and cheese.

title: Cave De Saumur Blanc Les Plantagnets

paras.text: "Fruity with aromas of citrus fruit and peach, pear or melon, Saumur white wine is a dry and nervous wine and is best served chilled."

title: Cave De Saumur Saumur Blance Les Pouches

paras.text: The vineyard of Saumur is located 150 miles west of Paris. Soil with clayey and silty sands. Several hard limestone rocks underlie the Méron slopes up to the fault of the Loudunais. This particular soil and subsoil has good draining capacity and early ripening potential. Vines : 45 years old - 16 acres - Yield : 50 Hl/Ha
Tasting Notes: Pale gold with touches of silver. Suave nose of ripe fruit, William pear and white peach, with a touch of honey-sweet acacia-lime flowers and a hint of flintiness.
Food Pairing: Fish with cream sauce, roast duck with peaches, Asian food, fresh goat's cheese; also ideal as an aperitif wine.

title: Cave De Saumur Champigny Les Vignolles

paras.text: A restricted area of production for an appellation of great acclaim. It is distinguished by its colour, varying from intense ruby to garnet, denoting round harmonious flavours of ripe red fruit and blackcurrant.

title: Cellier des Princes Côtes du Rhône Reserve du Prince

paras.text: This wine is a blend of three classic grape varieties from the Chateauneuf du Pape area: Grenache, Syrah and Mourvèdre. Grenache brings strengh, fatness and softness. Syrah brings the structure, the spices with aromas of violets and a deep ruby colour. Mourvèdre brings tannins and body. The oak treatment adds complexity, toasted notes of vanilla, grilled spices to the fruit driven base. This Grande Réserve Côtes du Rhône has a solid structure, good concentration, and ripe fruit. It is well balanced and shows a lot of elegance and finesse.
Total destemming, 3 to 4 weeks traditional maceration in concrete tanks. Classic pressing in pneumatic press and daily releases and pumping over.

title: Château Suduiraut Castelnau De Suduiraut

paras.text: Castelnau de Suduiraut is a wine with a distinctive character for which the groundwork is prepared far in advance, even down to the choice of specific plots to give it its own unique identity.

Made from portions of the harvest that are expressive earlier than those used for Château Suduiraut, this wine with aromas of candied yellow fruit, quince, frangipani, mild spices and a hint of minerality is more approachable when young in terms of tasting than its elder.

title: Chakana Estate Malbec

paras.text: The color is deep purple, very intense, quite what you expect from Malbec. Plum, brambly berries, spices and an iris/violet note are apparent on the nose. Intense, fruity flavors with velvety tannins.
80% is coming from the Agrelo vineyard, which is mainly clay and brings a lot of freshness in the wine.
The other 20% are from the Altamira vineyard, which gives riper fruit and allows a little more oak.

"There’s a thread of mountain herbs here, sitting amid ripe plums and blackcurrant. The palate has a very rich and ripe array of red plums that hold the juicy finish. Drink or hold." - James Suckling (April 2019), 90 pts

title: Champagne Mandois Blanc De Blancs Brut Premier Cru

paras.text: The Mandois Blanc de Blancs (100% Chardonnay) is a blend of several terroirs where the Chardonnay finds itself particularly at home. Perfectly representative of the vintage, it is only slightly sweetened to allow the natural character of the Chardonnay to develop to the full. To the delight of champagne enthusiasts, the delicate flavours of this beautiful Champagne express themselves best when it is served as an aperitif. This is one of our most popular Champagnes with Mandois Champagne devotees and the restaurant trade.

title: Champagne Mandois Brut Origine

paras.text: The judicious blending together of three grape varieties (40% Chardonnay / 30% Pinot Noir / 30% Pinot Meunier), sourced from all the property’s crus, endows this Cuvée Brut Origine with perfect balance and remarkable quality. The use of wines from 3 consecutive years also helps ensure its consistency of style.
Fruity and only very slightly dosed (sweetened), this Champagne is perfect as an aperitif where it expresses its natural character to the full.

title: Champagne Mandois Brut Zero

paras.text: The Brut Zero is a non-dosed (non-sweetened) Champagne, traditionally enjoyed inside the Champagne House itself, after it is disgorged "à la volée" (very quickly by hand). Created in collaboration with Francis Bernard, Cellar Master, Brut Zero is aged for 4 years on the lees and is intended to express the quintessence of a very Brut style, perfect for haute cuisine. It has a shimmering appearance with soft tints of gold. It shows rare refinement, with overtones of white flowers and citrus, on the nose. It is distinguished, complex and characterised by fruity apricot and yellow peach flavours. Given its ageing on the lees, the Champagne’s uplifting freshness is surprising. The crystalline and mineral elegance of this Brut Zero Champagne makes it perfectly suited to contemporary cuisine.

title: Champagne Mandois Cuvee Victor

paras.text: This “symphonic” Champagne is essentially composed of grapes from old vines of over 50 years of age growing in Mandois vineyards in Chouilly and Vertus. The low yields produced by these old vines provide both the structure and the balance between concentration and finesse essential to the creation of a fine Champagne. In addition, in order to develop smoothness and complexity, a proportion of the harvest is vinified in oak barrels in the traditional method used by Victor Mandois over a century ago. The tasting fully reflects the quality of this magnificent, carefully-crafted blend: the Champagne is delicate on the nose and shows a creaminess on the palate created by its very fine bubbles. It possesses perfect harmony and long-lasting flavours.

title: Champagne Hugues Godmé Brut Réserve Premier Cru

paras.text: Viticulture: Conversion to organic began in 2007. Biodynamic conversion in 2014 (Biodivin).

Vinification: Natural yeast when possible, no fining or filtration. Large proportion of reserve wines in non-vintage cuvées. Partial or entire fermentation in oak barrel. Dosage exclusively with concentrated grape must.

title: Champagne Hugues Godmé Extra Brut Premier Cru

paras.text: Hugues makes around 900 cases of his Extra Brut Nature a vintage. The blend is 60% Chardonnay, 30 % Pinot Meunier, and 10% Pinot Noir. The final blend is usually around 60% reserve wine from the previous four vintages. Dosage is 3.5 grams/liter.

title: Champagne Hugues Godmé Bois Grand Cru

paras.text: Terroir: Verzenay (Les Chaillots, Les Vignes Goisses) and Verzy (Les Bussets). Chalky soil.
Viticulture: Conversion to organic began in 2007. Biodynamic conversion in 2014 (Biodivin).
Vinification: Moderate sulfur, natural yeast, mostly vinified and aged on the lees in oak. Almost no batonnage, no fining or filtration. Large proportion of reserve wines. Dosage with MCR.

Paul Wasserman: “The Pinot for this cuvée is right on the chalk. It provides a profound mineral anchor while the Chardonnay goes all Tinkerbell around it, conjuring wildly with her wand discreet little comets of flavor. Then the intricate blend of reserve wines from no less than five vintages infuses everything with umami. Godmé’s Extra-Brut is baroque not in the sense that it is busy, but because the mineral anchor is so logical and the embellishments are so crystalline. It reminds me of Bach. As to the finish, it is nothing short of contemplative: deeply saline, elegantly chalky, and marvelously fine and precise. Though an NV cuvée, this is, looks, and behaves like a prestige cuvée. There are few champagnes in our portfolio I drink more of, and every time I do, Hugues’ Grand Cru Extra Brut reels me in, quiets me, and floors me. As Terry Theise wonderfully put it ‘Lots of wines, many of them good wines, let you taste the noise. But only the best let you taste the silence.’ This is one of those.”

title: Champagne Pierre Gerbais Brut Rosé

paras.text: Terroir: 90% from Celles-sur-Ource, 10% Coteaux Champenois, marl and limestone soil, Kimmeridgian bedrock
Vinification: Parcels vinified separately in temperature-controlled stainless steel tanks, indigenous yeast fermentation. 30 months

title: Champagne Pierre Gerbais Grains de Celles Extra Brut

paras.text: The fruit of the most beautiful and complementary grounds of Celles sur Ource. The result of observation and selection work over 8 generations of winegrowers in the Gerbais family.

title: Champagne Pierre Gerbais L’Audace Brut Nature

paras.text: The richness and fruits of Pinot Noir, sublimed by a natural vinification process.
Blended from historical Pinot Noir vines. This vintage comes primarily from a plot planted in 1960 in the grounds known as "Sainte-Marie."
Vineyards rooted in Kimmeridgian soil, composed of marl and limestone, situated in the village of Celles-sur-Ource, in the heart of the Côte des Bar.

A natural wine-growing process, recommendedby Ampelos since 1996 and certified of High Environmental Value. Limited yields fromvineyards with an average age of 30 years. Mechanical tillage, without use of synthetic products.
Vinification process with no added sulphur,using the properties of natural elements as a substitute.
Alcoholic and malo-lactic fermentation, maturing on fine lees in vats without fining or filtration.
Disgorgement: 6 months prior to going on sale Production of 5000 bottles per year

title: Champagne Pierre Gerbais Grains de Celles Rosé

title: Champagne Pierre Gerbais L’Originale Extra Brut

paras.text: Historical Pinot Blanc Vrai vines planted in 1904 in the grounds known as "Les Proies".
Vineyards rooted in Kimmeridgian soil, composed of marl and limestone, situated in the village of Celles-sur-Ource, in the heart of the Côte des Bar.
A natural wine-growing process, recommended by Ampelos since 1996 and certified of High Environmental Value.
Limited yields from vineyards with an average age of 30 years. Mechanical tillage, without use of synthetic products.

title: Champagne Roland Champion Brut Rosé

paras.text: The Champagne rose shows an orange salmon color coming from the red wine base. The pinot meunier brings red fruit aromas of strawberry and raspberry with hints of spices. The palate is juicy and harmonious with good depth and minerality. A delicate balance between Chardonnay, Pinot Meunier and Pinot Noir.

It is a blend of 93% White juice (made from 33% Chardonnay, 33% Pinot Meunier and 33% Pinot Noir) and 7% Pinot Noir red wine. The grapes used to produce the Coteaux Champenois red wine are coming from their vineyards near the Village of Verneuil.
Vinification: Manual harvest; then pressing immediately to avoid oxidation & preserve quality. Free run juice only. Aged three years sur lattes.
Pairings: Excellent as an aperitif, but also delicious with fish or poultry, or with dessert. One bottle do it all !

title: Champagne Roland Champion Special Club Grand Cru

paras.text: Champagne with rich and structured aromas. Very pleasant and generous roundness, nice length in mouth. Golden color with buttery and fruity aromas. All the expression of a magnificent terroir for your most pleasurable moments.

title: Champagne Vazart-Coquart & Fils Special Club Brut Grand Cru Blanc de Blancs

paras.text: Champagne Vazart-Coquart & Fils Special Club Brut Grand Cru Blanc de Blancs | Fine Vines
Vinification : Malolactic Fermentation done – Stainless steel vats with thermoregulation – Bottling and aging with natural cork

title: Champagne Vazart-Coquart & Fils Brut Reserve Grand Cru Blanc de Blancs

paras.text: Champagne Vazart-Coquart & Fils Brut Reserve Grand Cru Blanc de Blancs | Fine Vines

This cuvée “Brut”, in other words only lightly sweetened, is made exclusively from the white Chardonnay grape variety. Full of finesse, this supple and airy wine always contains 30 to 40 % of reserve wines, so that, year after year, you will find the same “Vazart-Coquart” taste so appreciated by wine-lovers.
It can be drunk at any time, but more especially as an aperitif or to accompany fish, seafood and many other first courses.

title: François Mikulski Bourgogne Aligoté

paras.text: We have cultivated our Burgundy Aligoté vineyards as tenant farmers since 1992. They cover an area of 1.5 hectares. The first was planted in 1929 and the second in 1948 by Joseph Boillot, François Mikulski’s grandfather.
Their vines are 100% Aligoté. They are cultivated using non-certified organic methods.

The subsoil consists of fine alluvial river sediment, which is common on the lower part of the slope. The extraction is limited, and the wine is aged in tanks on lees. It is bottled in July to preserve the fruit.
This wine is ideally served chilled, as an aperitif or with seafood or terrine. It should be drunk within a year if fruit aromas are preferred, but it can be stored for longer.
Vinification: Grapes crushed, indigenous yeast fermentation. Aged in stainless steel tank, filtered, bottled in July.

title: Château de la Bouyère Bordeaux (Red)

paras.text: Chateau de la Bouyere (red) has an intense ruby color, enhanced by a beautiful shine. The nose is powerful, with complex aromas combining ripe black fruits and roasted scents. The mouth is fleshy with a dense and tannic flavor, which hints of red fruits and spices supporting this balance through the finish.

title: Chateau de La Greffière Mâcon La Roche-Vineuse Blanc Vieilles Vignes

paras.text: Chateau de La Greffière Mâcon La Roche-Vineuse Blanc Vieilles Vignes | Fine Vines

From a 2.5ha area, the Mâcon V.V. is a blend of 3 vineyards of vines older than 50 years, and aged in 100% oak barrel, 10% new and the remainder in barrels that are up to 10 years used. This wine has twice achieved Wine Spectator's annual "Top 100" list.
Wine-making: The grapes stay 8 days in the tank for the skin fermentation, then get a soft pressing. After the malolactic fermentation, we bottle.

title: Château de La Maltroye Chassagne-Montrachet Premier Cru Clos du Château de la Maltroye

A few words: Perfection on details, no compromising, and the full expression of Terroirs associated with the best elevage possible and the best association of oak barrels

title: Chateau De La Mar Marestal Le Verney

paras.text: Color: bright colour with a golden hue with a green and grey sheen Nose: refined and underlined with a light woody note that allows spicy, animal and smoky scents to meet subtle bouquet notes: hawthorn, quince, rhubarb and almonds.

title: Chateau de Laubade Armagnac VSOP

paras.text: Château de Laubade V.S.O.P. is a blend of several different eaux-de-vie, the youngest being 6 years of age and in which the grape varieties of Ugni-Blanc and Folle Blanche are highly present.
The nose is fruity, in particular with vanilla and prune notes. It also develops aromas of white flowers.
It is soft in the mouth, well-balanced and the aromatic persistence lasts longer than five minutes.

title: Château de Manissy Tavel Cuvée des Lys Rosé

paras.text: This strong aromatic wine, prolongs its freshness by an elegant and harmonious finish. A blending of principally Grenache, Clairette, Cinsault and Bourboulenc, from about 40 years old vines. Start your evening with this young and modern drink!

title: Château de Ségriès Tavel Rosé

paras.text: Beautiful ripe cherry and red berry aromas with floral scents. Good concentration on the palate, flavorful and perfectly balanced. Good acidity and mineral backbone make it a great match with Provencal or Asian cuisine, grilled meat, fresh fruit salads.
Vinification: 'Vin de saignee'. 100% destemmed; overnight maceration in cement tank; low temperature fermentation.
Pairings: Provencal and Asian cuisine, Spicy dishes, Meats, Barbecues, Strawberry Salad

title: Château des Bachelards Fleurie

paras.text: There are many fun, simple styles of Beaujolais like the ‘Nouveau’ used for celebrating harvest or the Carbonic wines that are super fruity. In general, the wines from the southern part of Beaujolais are less prestigious, grown on simple low-lying clay soils. The northern part of Beaujolais is famous for 10 Cru villages high in the hills with granite or volcanic soils as the general base for the best vineyards. Fleurie is the Cru with the greatest concentration of great producers in the Beaujolais area and it is divided into 13 different Climats, or specific sites. Bachelard happens to be in one of the most famous sites, La Madonne, named after the little chapel perched at the top of the hill. With a deep garnet color and bright reflections, the nose is intense with fresh black soil, pepper, violet flowers, and berry fruits. On the palate there is great finesse with graphite-like minerality, a velvety texture, and an expressive finish with delicate tannins. Enjoy now or hold for 20+ years.

Food Pairing: A fun wine for lighter dishes like chicken. The fruit character plays well with cooked bitter greens lie Kale or Broccoli, Chinese foods, and mild curries. Great with cow’s milk cheeses. Serve at 55 degrees.

Varietal Notes: The story of the Gamay grape in Burgundy is a blockbuster! A sibling to Pinot Noir, this ancient grape was gaining popularity in the 14th century because it was much easier to grow and produce than Pinot Noir. In 1395, the then Duke of Burgundy, Philip the Bold, banned the grape entirely and declared it be, ‘destroyed and reduced to nothing’. He disliked the taste very much and this one man nearly brought the grape to extinction. Luckily, the Beaujolais region at the time was largely ignored so the grape survived and found a final home here.
Gamay is typically high in acid and low in tannin, but the wines of Bachelards are anything but typical, this is Gamay at its most complex and age-worthy vinified in a classic Burgundian style.

Terroir: Organic farming certified by Ecocert, biodynamically certified by Demeter, manually harvested fruit with very low yields, high trellising, and no trimming. Picked at optimal maturity from 60 to 80-year-old vines on pink granitic soils dating back 350 million years.

Winemaking: 100% destemmed, the juice is received by gravity and fermentation is with native yeast in concrete tanks for 28 days on the skins. Afterwards the wine rests in 500-liter barrels and larger casks for 24 months. All estate-fruit.

title: Chateau de Suronde Quarts de Chaume

paras.text: Very natural growing, using no weed killers or pesticides. Harvested by hand from vines 15 to 70 years old.

title: Château Des Quarts Pouilly-Fuissé Clos Des Quarts

paras.text: Terroir: East-facing, Quarts vineyard in Chaintré with shallow ferruginous topsoil, Bajocian crinoidal limestone bedrock
; indigenous yeast alcoholic fermentation, full malos, and 18 months' aging in 6-7% new oak (most 1-3 years old) barrels.
Planted to the density of 10,000 vines per hectare (higher than the typical 6,500 to 8,000 vines per hectare in the Mâconnais).

title: Château des Bachelards Saint Amour

paras.text: There are many fun simple styles of Beaujolais like the ‘Nouveau’ style used for celebrating harvest or the Carbonic wines that are super fruity. In general, the wines from the southern part of Beaujolais are less prestigious, grown on simple low-lying soils. The northern part of Beaujolais is famous for 10 Cru villages with granite soils as the general base for the best vineyards. Saint Amour is Beaujolais’ most northerly appellation and is quite versatile when it comes to complexity. The biodynamic wines of Bachelards are some of the most complex and structured of the wines coming from the Saint Amour Cru. Deep garnet with bright reflections, the nose is intense with black soil, pepper, Iris flowers, licorice, and berry fruits. On the palate the wine is firm like the wines of Moulin-à-Vent. The wine shows great freshness, minerality, and an expressive finish with delicate tannins. Optimum at 4-5 years and capable of aging up to 15 years.
Food Pairing: A fun wine for lighter dishes and white meats. The fruit character plays well with Chinese foods and mild curries. Great with fresh cow’s milk cheeses.

Varietal Notes: The story of the Gamay grape in Burgundy is a blockbuster! A sibling to Pinot Noir, this ancient grape was gaining popularity in the 14th century because it was much easier to grow and produce than Pinot Noir. In 1395, the then Duke of Burgundy, Philip the Bold, banned the grape entirely and declared it be, ‘destroyed and reduced to nothing’. He disliked the taste very much and this one man nearly brought the grape to extinction. Luckily, the Beaujolais region at the time was largely ignored and the grape survived, finding a final home here.
Gamay is typically high in acid and low in tannin, but the wines of Bachelards are anything but typical, this is Gamay at its most complex and age-worthy vinified in a classic Burgundian style.

Terroir: Organic farming certified by Ecocert, biodynamic certified by Demeter, from the middle of the slope on south facing hills, manual harvesting of fruits at optimal maturity from 40-60-year-old vines on unique pink granite soils with mica and shale. The vines go deeper here than in Fleurie.

Winemaking: Juice is received by gravity and vinified in concrete vats with native yeast and 28 days on the skins followed by 12 months in equal parts stainless steel and 500-liter casks. All estate fruit and no carbonic maceration.

title: Château Gautoul Cahors

paras.text: Soils: 5 types: silt, clay, limestone, sand and stony according to the respective parcel
Climate: Influenced by the Lot River as well as by the Atlantic and Mediterranean.
Vinification: in stainless steel tanks for 3 weeks. Malolactic fermentation: in tanks at the finish of the alcoholic fermentation.

title: Château Grande Cassagne Rosé

paras.text: Crisp and refreshing, this blend of Grenache and Syrah takes all the aromatic and flavor characteristics of Grande Cassagne Rouge and reframes those aromas and flavors into a chillable, easy drinking Rosé. Garnet jewel in color with aromas of ripe cherry, underbrush and minerals. Anticipate flavors of tangy cherry and blood orange notes, with hints of spice.

Who doesn’t love a lightly chilled Rosé on a hot summer day? This wine is way more versatile, pairing easily with light appetizers or presented as an aperitif at your next dinner party. Pairs with chilled shellfish, oysters, light soups or gazpacho – even sandwiches ranging from chicken or turkey to smoked ham.

Grenache: Some consider Grenache to be as important a grape as the highly revered Cabernet Sauvignon. Estimates put worldwide planting of Grenache at more than 450,000 acres – with 250,000 of those acres in France! Characteristically, Grenache expresses red fruit flavors (raspberry and strawberry) with a subtle, white pepper spice note. Syrah: Again, France commands the lion’s share of Syrah on the planet, with nearly 170,000 acres planted among the world’s 450,000 acres. Virtually every wine producing region employs Syrah to some degree due to its brisk acidity and firm tannins. Terroir and winemaking styles develop a variety of aspects from its complex flavors that range from smoke, bacon, herbs, red and black fruits, white and black pepper, to floral violet.
Winemaking: The Syrah has 6-8 hours of skin contact, and the Grenache has 12-16 hours. Night harvesting is done to preserve freshness. Vines are 40-60 years old. Sustainably farmed.

title: Chateau Grange Cochard Morgon Les Charmes

paras.text: Hand picked and hand sorted. Matured in barrels for 9 to 12 months. Minimal filtration on bottling and low sulphur. Total production around 4,000 bottles from the vines directly in front of the Chateau. “Lightly oaked with vanilla accents, rich on the palate, generous and silky, underpinned with well-structured tannins. An atypical Morgon, but remarkable for its harmony and elegance” Guide Hachette

title: Château Grande Cassagne Rouge

paras.text: Rich yet fresh, this blend of Grenache and Syrah is raspberry colored with aromas of ripe cherry, underbrush and minerals. Anticipate flavors of tangy cherry and blood orange notes, with hints of spice.

This red blend is a real crowd pleaser! It is a versatile wine that is enjoyable as a sipper in social situations to backyard cookouts, from hearty cheeses and cured meats to roasted meats and rustic country stews.
