Syrah: Again, France commands the lion’s share of Syrah on the planet, with nearly 170,000 acres planted among the world’s 450,000 acres. Virtually every wine producing region employs Syrah to some degree due to its brisk acidity and firm tannins. Terroir and winemaking styles develop a variety of aspects from its complex flavors that range from smoke, bacon, herbs, red and black fruits, white and black pepper, to floral violet.
Winemaking: The Syrah has 6-8 hours of skin contact, and the Grenache has 12-16 hours. Night harvesting is done to preserve freshness. Vines are 40-60 years old. Sustainably farmed.

title: Châtaeu Haut-Sarthes Montravel Blanc

paras.text: A classy Cuvée of 60% Sauvignon, 30% Semillon & 10% Muscadelle - Fabulous quality!
Crisp, elegant, fruity & refreshing - our new exclusive award winning White Bordeaux.

title: Château Haut-Sarthes Bergerac Rosé

paras.text: The Bergerac region is located just East of Bordeaux. Wine maker and proprietor Daniel Hecquet, owns 45 Hectares in the Appellation’s best district and is one of the region’s best and most innovative producer. He is known throughout the greater Bordeaux region for crafting among the highest quality and freshest wines in the appellation. He also consults as an enologist for top Chateaux.
Viticultural practices: Higher density (7500 vines/ hectare), hillside plantation, the grapes for Haut-Sarthes Rosé come from the same parcels every vintage.
Vinification: 1 day cold maceration, direct pressing and fermentation in temperature controlled stainless steel vats.

Tasting Notes: Deliciously refreshing dry rosé showing great balance between fruit and acidity. The aromas and flavors reveal precise and expressive notes of red berries and cantaloupe, the finish is clean and delicately mineral. The 2017 is particularly fresh, fruity and expressive, due to the perfect harvest conditions for the vintage.

title: Château Haut-Sarthes Bergerac Rouge

paras.text: Blend of Merlot, Cabernet Sauvignon, and Cabernet Franc. Garnet highlights, intense red fruit aromas, nice tannic structure, and supple tannins.

title: Château Haut-Sarthes Haut Montravel

paras.text: 60% Sauvignon, 30% Semillon & 10% Muscadelle compose aromas of white flowers, honey, and crisp green grass. Citrus driven palette with hints of green apple and pear lend to a refreshing, crisp finish. Pair with poultry, rich fish dishes, or just chill, pour, and drink it on it's own!!

title: Château Haut-Sarthes Haut Montravel Moelleux

paras.text: The red wines of Bergerac, an appellation just to the east of the town of Bergerac, share many of the characteristics of Bordeaux red wines without the lofty prices. This AOC is less than 30 miles from St. Emilion following the same hill on the right side of the Dordogne River where the soil's high iron content contributes to the rich structure, flavor and longevity of the wines. The Merlot, Cabernet Sauvignon, and Cabernet Franc vineyards of Chateau Haut Sarthes produce grapes that are very similar to that of St. Emilion. Foremost, this is a Merlot dominated wine boasting luscious fruitiness and structure. Its wines are ideal accompaniments to the traditional Perigord cuisine.

title: Château Haut Selve Graves Blanc

paras.text: Guava mingled with fresh ginger, fresh snipped herbs and tangerine rind. Complex and ripe with subtle fruit and hints of vanilla and almond in the elegant finish.

Was the biggest property in Bordeaux in the 19th century, with 860 acres. After being destroyed and abandoned, it became the only “new” vineyard of the 20th Century (1993) in the Bordeaux region. 28 of the estate’s 68 hectares are dedicated to white wine, in one of the oldest AOCs of Bordeaux.
Soil: Clay-gravel soils permitting the planting of various grapes. Gravelly soil between the Garonne River and the Lande Forest.
Grape Varietals: Sémillon: 50%, Sauvignon Blanc: 35%, Sauvignon Gris: 15%. (heirloom varietal introduced for its interesting aromatic qualities when vinified in wood).

Vinification: The fruit is hand picked separately by plot and by varietal. Skin content maceration in pneumatic tanks about 18 hours, which produces about 80% of gravity-fed free-run juice. The remaining 20% are obtained by pneumatic pressing.

title: Chateau La Mouliniere Bordeaux Rouge

paras.text: Medium-bodied and loaded with notes of dark fruit, especially black cherries and blackberries. Well-rounded tannins in the finish. Definitely shows class that well exceeds its diminutive price point.

title: Chateau La Mouliniere Bordeaux Blanc

paras.text: La Mouliniere is an 80/20 blend of Sauvignon Blanc and Semillon offers a fragrant nose of citrus and exotic fruits. It is mineral and dry on the palate and the finish is very refreshing. Enjoy with seafood, raw fish and shellfish.

title: Château Lestrille Bordeaux Supérieur

paras.text: A fresh, aromatic unoaked Claret. It shows ripe fruit reminiscent of soft plum and cassis on the nose. On the palate it is soft and juicy, yet well structured with a smooth texture.
Black fruit and cedar notes, with a hint of leather and black pepper. Smooth tannins and balanced acidity.

title: Château Lestrille Entre Deux Mers Blanc

paras.text: This is a fresh wine with lovely citrus and white peach flavours, well-balanced and both lively and round.

Tasting Notes: The pale yellow colour with tints of golden is clear and twinkling. On the nose, a combination of white flower aromas, exotic, peach and citrus fruit aromas. Very flattering on the palate, voluptuous, smooth and very fruity, supported by a well-measured vivacity."
Vinification: Traditionally vinified with the utmost care, respecting the grape, aromas, and the wine's personality.

title: Château Nicot Bordeaux Rouge

paras.text: This wine has a ruby red colour with a fresh nose with fruity notes, distinct and neat in mouth, keeping the finesse and the material. A longlasting and smooth final which is very pleasant.

title: Chateau Pajzos Tokaji Aszu 3 Puttonyos

paras.text: "The 2007 Tokaji Aszu 3-Puttonyos is a blend of 60% Furmint, 20% Harslevelu, 10% Muscat and 10% Zeta that sees two years in three-year-old wooden barrels (136 and 220-liter). With 103 grams per liter residual sugar, it has a more intense nose for a 3-Puttonyos, with peach skin, nectarine, yellow plum and a touch of papaya fruit that shows fine clarity. The palate is medium-bodied with a viscous, honeyed opening of Manuka honey, yellow plum, orange rind and dried mango. There is a salty note on the periphery with a sedate, if ever so slightly predictable finish. Fine. Drink now-2035." - Neal Martin (Dec 2013)
"Sweet yet light-bodied, sporting flavors of lanolin, apricot and baking spices. Well-balanced, with a lingering finish. Drink now through 2020. 1,533 cases made." – BS (Web Only - 2014)

title: Château Pichon Baron Pauillac

paras.text: Our Grand Vin Château Pichon Baron 2nd Cru Classé in 1855 comes from the very oldest vines grown on the historic plots of the estate.
This authentic Pauillac offers an amazing sensory experience with its black fruit flavours and spicy hints. Château Pichon Baron shows great elegance, intensity and exceptional length on the palate.
It is a wine that improves year after year and can age for over 40 years in the cellar.

Château Pichon Baron is very dark, deep and intense in colour. On the nose, the wide aromatic range reveals notes of vanilla and coconut, even a bouquet of black fruits, combined with subtle nuances of spice and cigar box. The attack is full, with smoothness and sweetness. The precise tannins are fine and enveloping. There is a nice, long, opulent finish. Particular attention was paid to maturation, giving this great wine an elegant structural balance. The typicity is clear; the style of this vintage - in which balance is the main feature - is marked by finesse and distinction.

title: Chateau Pajzos Tokaji Aszu 5 Puttonyos

paras.text: 70% Furmint and 30% Zeta. The grapes for the Aszu wines were hand-picked in October and November in 15 passes at an outstanding level of ripeness during sunny, hot and dry days and very cool nights. Pajzos’ Aszu 5 Puttonyos 2009 was aged for three years in 220 liter, Hungarian oak casks, of which 30% were new, followed by three more years in stainless steel tanks. It was then assembled, lightly filtered, and bottled in July 2013. The stunning residual sugar level of 195 grams per liter qualifies the wine to be classified at the 6 Puttonyos level, and it is balanced by 6 grams per liter of acidity. The 2009 vintage’s ideal combination of great ripeness and vibrant acidity is the epitome of the Pajzos house style, and is considered an ideal vintage by the estate. 3,000 bottles made.

title: Chateau Peyros Madiran Vieilles Vignes

paras.text: The Vieilles Vignes is a blend of 80% Tannat and 20% Cabernet Franc with an average vine age between 40-50 years. The wine spends about 12 months in oak barrels about 40% new before it is bottled. This is no shy Madiran. It is full of the power and texture that one associates with the region. With some decanting it is absolutely appropriate with rich dishes of sausage, duck confit and rustic pâtés.

Abundant, ripe, fresh red berry and perfumed blueberry laced with rich, dark plum aromas, lead to a beautifully textured, rounded palate packed with heady black fruit, delicate smoke and fine grained tannins

title: Confidences de Prieuré-Lichine Margaux

paras.text: Lush and alluring, featuring warmed fig, boysenberry and blackberry confiture notes gliding through atop a silky but persistent structure. The long finish lets the fruit play out, with only a modest hint of alder checking in.The Confidences de Prieuré-Lichine is a very pretty second wine. Pliant, supple and inviting, the Confidences is an excellent choice for drinking now and over the next few years. All of the signatures of the Grand Vin come through nicely, but, of course, in miniature. This is a strong showing.

title: Château Puy-Servain Calabre Daniel Olivier Sauvignon Blanc

paras.text: Racy but in control, citrus fruits, green pepper and a fruitful finish. Elegant, delicate grassiness on the nose from the Sauvignon Blanc with a broader feel on the palate from the addition of a small amount of Semillon, finishing lifted and fresh with citrus qualities. A diversity of flavour that many pure Sauvignon at this level lack

title: Château Puynormond Montagne Saint Emilion

paras.text: After assemblage of the three cepages vinified seperately, they are aged 18 months in concrete vats and then bottled - no oak! You have the pure fruit of a Saint-Emilion. The production is 55 to 60 hectoliters per hectare.
Deep ruby color with purple hues due to its youth, this vintage offers a limpid and clear shine.
This wine gives intense and elegant aromas of red fruits such as gooseberry, blackberry, cherry or plum. It offers a beautiful persistence enhanced by a note of cooked fruit.
It is a gourmet and generous wine offering to the palate the same aromas as nose, with the presence of soft tannins, elegant and fine, which allow a nice length in the mouth.

title: Château Puy-Servain Calabre Terrement

paras.text: Tasting: lemon yellow color, fresh pineapple quince aromas, superb sweetness on the attack, which leaves a fresh finish with good acidity.
Place: Puy Servain whose origin comes from "Puy" = summit and from "Servain" = strong wind, because it is a very windy climax.
Type of soil: clay-limestone; very overhauled. Heterogeneous soil with very calcareous areas at the top of the hills
Serving suggestion: drink very cold, as an aperitif, with foie gras, white meats and parsley cheeses.

title: Château Puynormond Montagne Saint Emilion Vieilles Vignes

paras.text: 100% Merlot. Ageing: 12 months in 50% new, 25% 1 year old, 25% 2 years old oak barrels.
This wine has a deep ruby color, which is tinged with dark shades more sustained. Clear and shiny, it offers violet reflections because it is still young.
This wine confers intense and elegant aromas of red fruits on hints of spices; vanilla, cinnamon. It also offers a warm and round woody, enhanced by scents of jam.

This is a gourmet and generous wine offering the palate the same aromas as the nose. The attack is ample and supple. The ripe fruits accompany wonderfully the rounded woody, to finish on a beautiful end of mouth which leaves us dreamer.

It will marry wonderfully with your everyday dishes as with the most elaborate dishes. Salty, sweet, do not hesitate to associate it with your own taste. Red wine and chocolate make a wonderful couple!

title: Château Haut Selve Graves Rouge

paras.text: Sporting a vibrant ruby color with intense aromas Provencal herbs and oak, this special cuvee leaves a great impression. The initial rich, red fruit flavors are followed by enticing tannins and a balanced finish. Aged for 12 months in French oak barrels.

title: Chataeu Revelette Coteaux D'Aix en Provence Rose

paras.text: Vinified with ripe grapes, this traditional rosé, sporting a pale robe with “rose pink” hue, is delightful, beautifully fresh, complemented by lovely aromas of peach, apricot, and good density in the mouth.

title: Château Sainte Roseline Côtes De Provence Le Cloître

paras.text: Le Cloître is a blend of 50% Cinsault, 20% Grenache, 20% Cabernet Sauvignon, and 10% Mourvèdre. In the glass, the wine emanates a brilliant translucent pink with copper highlights. Aromas and flavors of red berry and tropical fruits intermingle with savory herbs and rocky mineral notes. The Cru Classé pedigree is evident in the flavor concentration and rich mouthfeel of the wine, while maintaining a bright, vibrant acidity that is thirst-quenching. I suppose that having popes and saints as part of your history blesses the wines year after year! Easy to enjoy on its own, the Château Sainte Roseline is also perfect with all types of seafood from ocean perch to octopus to swordfish, but would pair equally well with a full-flavored mixed vegetable salad.

title: Château Sainte Roseline Côtes De Provence Lampe De Meduse

paras.text: Lampe de Méduse is the signature wine of Château Sainte Roseline. Made from the best grapes of the estate, the cuvée is available in three colours. The bottle, with its singular and iconic shape, is the result of the reflections of the Baroness de Rasque de Laval.

title: Chateau Roc de Segur Bordeaux Rouge

paras.text: As a Bordeaux Rouge, this wine is intended to be drunk fresh, it is young and fruity with spice and prevelant plums. The nose is dominated by spices and herbs. The earthy finish tastes great going down especially with grilled meats.
Tasting note: A dark purple colour. The nose reveals red fruits aromas (raspberry, cherry). It is fresh with a beautiful structure thanks to the silky tannins, and it can be aged.

title: Château Suduiraut Sauternes

paras.text: Château Suduiraut, classed as a Premier Cru in 1855, is made from grapes selected from the finest terroirs of the property.

This wine is handcrafted at every stage of its elaboration and reveals a remarkable complexity and a golden colour reminiscent of the sun. With age the bright gold evolves into a dark amber colour. With an extensive life-span, it powerfully and harmoniously combines fruit and floral aromas with roasted and candied notes.

title: Clos Henri Petit Clos Sauvignon Blanc Marlborough

paras.text: There is something truly remarkable about young vine Marlborough Sauvignon Blanc and therefore we wanted to create a wine to showcase this vibrant expression. Our Petit Clos Sauvignon Blanc, is intensely refreshing and juicy with concentrated bright fruit flavours. Hints of minerality come through, giving a taste of the wine’s Clos Henri origins and the Bourgeois family winegrowing style.

title: Clos Henri Vineyards Clos Henri Sauvignon Blanc

paras.text: In the French tradition, our vineyard is planted in high density to encourage competition between vines and restrain vigour. This natural vigour control means the vines put more energy into the grapes, rather than the canopy - concentrating the berries. Dry farming (using no irrigation) also helps keep vigour under control. By stressing the vines to just the right level, it forces the roots to go deeper in the soil, thereby getting the purest expression of our terroir and showing more minerality from the river stone soil.

Fermentation occurred in 85% stainless steel and 15% old French oak barrels. The wine was then aged on fine yeast lees for 8 months with lees stirring, both of which enable us to obtain a round Sauvignon Blanc with body and mouthfeel.

An elegant and restrained wine, the delicate nose unfolds to reveal flint, white peach and fresh lemon zest. Fleshy, white stone fruits and extended lees ageing imbue the palate with a richness, while the core minerality leaves a precise and focused finish.

title: Clos Henri Vineyards Petit Clos Pinot Noir

paras.text: Stemming from our French heritage our vineyard has incorporated high density planting to encourage competition between vines and restrain vigour. This natural vigour control means that the vines put more energy into the grapes, rather than the canopy, concentrating on the berries. The younger Pinot vines on our estate are situated on 3 different soil types. All our Pinot Noir is hand-picked in the cool, early mornings to retain fruit integrity.

This wine was fermented in stainless steel open tops and then aged in large (7,500 l) French oak vats for 11 months. Ageing in large oak vats, instead of smaller barrels, gives the wine great balance with subtle oak which enriches structure while retaining aromatic intensity.

title: Comte Armand Bourgogne Blanc Condemaine

paras.text: This young 8 year old vine is located on the town of Volnay in a place called "The Condemaines". Planted on a clay are of Volnay that grows mostly Pinot Noir. The introduction of Muscat Chardonnay (Chardonnay small grain from Macon La Roche Vineuse), was audacious but it payed off in this land of rich and deep tradition.
Chardonnay is regulated better in this type of soil, and wines obtained are accurate and a surprising freshness is enjoyed.
Vinification: Whole-cluster pressing, indigenous yeast fermentation. Aged for 12 months in year-old barrels. Fined and blended in stainless steel tank before bottling.
Pruned to Cordon Royat to limit yields. The Chardonnay muscaté that makes up a small percentage of this wine is a massal selection from Olivier Merlin's Mâcon Les Cras Vielles Vignes.

title: Comte Armand Auxey-Duresses

paras.text: Stemming from a "terroir" Exposed full South, on a hill on the way to the Little Village Auxey, this wine has a full fruit taste with a mineral touch.

South facing hillside, this parcel with an average age of 40 years, is geologically unique to this sector. Indeed, this is one of the most heavily dense limestone areas of the Côte de Beaune (30% active lime). The wines are full of berries and are usually quite young to drink, but can also grow old.
, upper part of hill, facing south, soil with high content of active limestone (30%).
Vinification: 100% de-stemmed, indigenous yeast fermentation. Aged for 18-24 months in older oak barrels.

title: Dashe Carignane Old Vines Evangelho Vineyard

paras.text: We absolutely love these old, gnarled vines planted on their own roots, in an unlikely spot in Antioch, California. Planted in 1890 and growing in deep sandy soil—essentially a vineyard on sand dunes—in the Sacramento River Delta, these are some of the most beautiful, old Carignane vines we’ve ever seen. Since the vineyard is dry-farmed and the soil is essentially pure sand, the roots extend down more than 40 feet to the water table below in some areas. The grapes produce a dark, vibrant wine that shows off how complex a wine the varietal can be.

Taste: Vibrant red fruit including pomegranate, black cherry, and wild strawberry. as well as floral notes of rose and violets. A substantial wine with round tannins and a velvety mouthfeel, balanced by vibrant crisp acidity. Long, sweet finish of red fruits and black pepper spice.

title: Dashe Cabernet Sauvignon Heart Arrow Ranch

paras.text: The Cabernet Sauvignon grown on the property comes from vines planted on a steep slope of bright red, rocky, volcanic soil. The vines struggle to produce fruit on this well-drained rocky soil, which produces tiny amounts of intense, complex fruit that we make into structured, almost Bordeaux-like Cabernet Sauvignon.

Taste: Beautiful structured wine, with great acidity balanced with complex fruit. Entry of blackberry, cassis, pomegranate, and then broader flavors of plum, earth, forest floor, black cherry, medium weight, persistent finish of blackberry, black cherry, mineral, and black peppery spice.

title: Dashe Chenin Blanc Concrete Cuvée

paras.text: Pale gold color, this Chenin Blanc shows beautiful aromas of pear with hints of apricot, minerals, honeycomb, grapefruit, pear, sweet spice finish. On the palate, the wine is rich, with a viscous texture and pear, apricot fruit flavors, hints of grapefruit. crisp acidity, long, lively stonefruit finish. Chenin blanc is certainly a favorite to pair with food and can be enjoyed on its own as an aperitif.

Grapes are picked at night to keep them as cold as possible and are pressed in an egg-shaped concrete fermenter immediately on arrival at the winery. In Dashe’s style, the grapes are fermented on the native yeasts found on the grape skins. The white wines are bottled as soon as possible to keep the freshness and liveliness of the wine intact.

The winemaking team at Dashe has long been a fan of Chenin Blanc from the Loire Valley, and over the years have searched for local Chenin Blanc grapes to make a crisp, dry wine from this classic varietal. They discovered an ideal vineyard in Clarksburg California, home to the vast majority of Chenin Blanc grapes grown in California. This unique area is in the Sacramento River delta, where cool breezes from the San Francisco Bay cool the grapes, creating hot afternoons and cool evenings that make for ideal conditions to grow Chenin Blanc. A 500 gallon egg-shaped concrete fermentation vessel is used to highlight the minerality of the grapes, and the results have exceeded the winemaker’s expectations.

title: Dashe The Comet Old Vine

paras.text: The Comet is a blend of three varietals that completment each other beautifully: Zinfandel, Carignane, and Petite Sirah. Together, they make a rich, complex, full-bodied wine with a tremendous depth of flavor. Each varietal adds flavor components and textural elements that create a wine that is a perfect complement to grilled meats or savory sauces—you can use The Comet to accompany foods much the way you would a nicely-aged Cabernet Sauvignon.

The Petite Sirah comes from the Todd Brothers Ranch, a steep, red-rock vineyard in the Alexander Valley, where the vines struggle to produce a small quantity of grapes resulting in great intensity and structure. The old-vine Carignane comes from 100+ year old vines from the historic Oat Valley vineyard in the Alexander Valley. Finally, the Zinfandel comes from 100 year old vines on one of most favorite vineyards in the Dry Creek Valley, the Louvau family vineyard.
Aromas: Chocolate, black cherry, blackberry, and black current, followed by elements of toffee, vanilla, black pepper, and coffee

Taste: A very structured wine, with a beautiful texture, good acid balance, and firm tannins. The entry is of bright fruit—black cherry, blackberry, and pomegranate—and then a lush texture filled with fruit, cocoa powder, clove, and a spicy finish. The wine has a velvety mouthfeel and long finish. Great weight on the tongue with a slight tannic—almost cabernet-like—structure.

title: Dashe Grenache Dry Creek Les Enfants Terribles

paras.text: We love the fresh, red fruit of these Grenache grapes, which produce one of the most drinkable and lovely wines we produce at Dashe Cellars. Because of the way we make this wine - fermented with the native yeasts on the grapes; aged in large, French oak barrels; unfixed' and bottled with low SO2 levels - we felt this is an ideal addition to our Les Enfants Terribles (the "Wild Children") series, wines made in an Old World style. The resulting purity of flavor, velvety texture, and lush mid palette is a break from the brash, fruit-forward style of many Californian wines.

Taste: Beautiful velvety texture. Entry of intense strawberry, raspberry, and pomegranate fruit. Beautiful floral elements of lavender and violets, long, sweet finish of red fruit, minerals and peppery spice.

title: Dashe Late Harvest Zinfandel

paras.text: This dessert wine is made from grapes grown on the Lily Hill Vineyard in northern Dry Creek Valley. The steep slopes and rocky soil make the vines struggle to survive, which in turn help the vines create very concentrated, complex grapes. Even after waiting an extra four weeks to harvest the grapes, they maintain their acidity and the resulting wine is crisp and clean.

Aroma: Wild cherry, pomegranate, lavender, violets, dried cranberry, black raspberry, cocoa, vanilla, black pepper spice. Taste: Intense, vibrant red fruit – wild cherry, cranberry, pomegranate mixed with darker flavors of black currant, plum, and hints of chocolate and vanilla.

title: Dashe Zinfandel Heart Arrow Ranch Les Enfants Terribles

paras.text: This wine shows excellent fruit and mineral aromas, and the wine has an absolutely beautiful texture and depth of flavor. Although this wine is beautiful to drink right now, it can improve with age as well, at least 8 years from the vintage date.

How is this wine different? First of all, we don't crush the grapes but instead use whole clusters and uncrushed destemmed grapes to create a "carbonic maceration" style of wine. We ferment the wine native yeasts on the grapes; age with the wine in a huge 900 gallon French oak barrel; and bottle the wine with low SO2 levels. Like other wines in the Les Enfants Terribles (the "Wild Children") series, this wine is made in a more Old World style (i.e. soft and elegant) style than a classic California Zinfandel.
Armoa: Extremely aromatic, black cherry, pomegranate, earth, violets, clove spice, black pepper
Taste: Soft, velvety texture, mouthfilling, complex flavors of black cherry, pomegranate, strawberry, black raspberry, chocolate, minerals, and black pepper spice.

title: Dashe Zinfandel Vineyard Select

paras.text: Reddish-purple in color. This wine is very aromatic black cherry, black raspberry, and pomegranate, mixed with hints of cassis, chocolate, and slight peppery spice. Lush , lively texture with lovely black cherry and pomegranate fruit, bright acidity to balance the sweet fruit flavors, black pepper and clove spice, and a long, lively finish of black cherry, raspberry, and hints of cocoa powder.
VINEYARD: Blend of different vineyards in different northern California appellations.

title: Denis Breussin Vouvray Demi Sec

paras.text: The Breussin Estate in Vouvray has been family-owned and operated for five generations and covers 37 acres of Chenin Blanc. Yves and Denis Breussin tend to the vineyard with respect for the vines and the environment. Denis Breussin is a fifth-generation winemaker.
Light and off-dry with flavors and aromas of white flowers, peaches, honey, and toasted nuts. Great with cheese, appetizers, ham, and spicy cuisines.

title: DeBortoli Emeri Pink Moscato

paras.text: Pale translucent pink with fresh fruit aromas and hints of strawberry and musk. Velvety and full with a persistent bead and fresh finish.

We select fruit from vines with generous canopies allowing natural fruit ripening. The fruit is picked and gently pressed and the juice allowed to settle naturally before being filtered. The wine is cold fermented to retain fresh fruit characters.

title: Comte Armand Auxey-Duresses Premier Cru

paras.text: This blending of "terroir" Produces a rustic and fleshy wine, full of fruit with suprising freshness and a smooth finish. Two of the best parcels of the village are assembled to obtain grapes for this wine. The first being Breterins, facing south on land usually used for white wines giving it a mature step forward for the appellation and the wines fruit. On the other hand, Duresses, facing South East on lands of brown clays growing rather dense and tannic wines. The complementarity of these two plots produced a serious wine.
Vinification: 100% de-stemmed, indigenous yeast fermentation in open wooden vats. Aged for 18 months in barrel (25% new oak).

title: Digioia-Royer Bourgogne Passetoutgrain

paras.text: Vinification: 100% de-stemmed, short cold maceration, indigenous yeast fermentation in wood and/or stainless steel tanks. Aged for 12 months in stainless steel tank.

title: Digioia-Royer Chambolle-Musigny

paras.text: Terroir: Parcels from the north to south: Beaux Bruns, Combottes, Condemènes, Pas de Chats, Fouchères, Creux Baissants
Vinification: 100% de-stemmed, indigenous yeast fermentation. Aged for 16 to 18 months in barrel (20% new oak).

title: Digioia-Royer Bourgogne Pinot Noir

paras.text: The nose delivers a wide vista of ripe pinot fruit. Good acidity and tannin and quite enough fruit ‘glue’ to hold everything together. Some bitter chocolate tannin towards the finish. - Burgundy Report
Terroir: 7 different parcels in Morey-Saint-Denis, Gilly-les-Citeaux, and Chambolle-Musigny with clay-limestone soils
Vinification: 100% de-stemmed, short cold maceration, indigenous yeast fermentation. Aged for 12 months, 50% in stainless steel tank, 50% in older barrels. Blending before bottling.

title: Digioia-Royer Chambolle-Musigny Vieilles Vignes Les Fremières

paras.text: Versus the ‘regular’ Chambolle this wine is deeper toned and shows a hint of musky perfume – perhaps a little heavy but quite compelling. Finer tannin here and very good flavour that widens across the palate, filling all the nooks and crannies of your mouth. Long with just a little mineral flavour. Very nice wine. - Burgundy Report
Vinification: 100% de-stemmed, indigenous yeast alcoholic fermentation. Aged for 16 months in barrel (20% new), blending in stainless steel tank before bottling.

title: Domaine Digioia-Royer Bourgogne Hautes-Côtes de Nuits

paras.text: A fresh, acidic wine with a expertly crafted spiced nose. The dark fruit is prominent on the palate. This wine comes from the Plateua above Vosne-Romanee.
Vinification: 100% de-stemmed, indigenous yeast fermentation. Aged for 12 months in barrel (20% new). Racking, blending in tank before bottling.

title: Domaine Alain Burguet & Fils Bourgogne Rouge Les Pince Vin

paras.text: Vinification: 100% de-stemmed, indigenous yeast fermentation, punch-downs and pump-overs depending on vintage. Aged for 18 months in barrel (20% new).

title: Domaine Alain Burguet & Fils Chambolle-Musigny Les Echezeaux

paras.text: Vinification: 100% de-stemmed, indigenous yeast fermentation, minimal intervention. Aged for 19 months in barrel (30% new oak).

title: Domaine Alain Burguet & Fils Chambertin Clos de Bèze Grand Cru

paras.text: Vinification: 100% de-stemmed, indigenous yeast fermentation, minimal intervention. Aged for 19 months in barrel (30% new).

title: Domaine Alain Burguet & Fils Gevrey-Chambertin Mes Favorites Vieilles Vignes

paras.text: Domaine Alain Burguet & Fils Gevrey-Chambertin Mes Favorites Vieilles Vignes | Fine Vines
Terroir: 18 different parcels from the north to the south of the Gevrey appellation (in Brochon and Gevrey), facing east
Vinification: 100% de-stemmed, indigenous yeast fermentation, minimal intervention. Aged for 20 months in barrel (30% new).
A selection of the domaine’s oldest and highest quality vines, the average yield is from 25 to 35 hL per hectare depending on the vintage.

title: Domaine Albert Mann Auxerrois Vieilles Vignes

paras.text: Hand-harvested from Kientzheim and Wettolsheim. Expressive nose, fresh and delicious. Dominated by fresh fruits. Bright Yellow-Gold in color, this Pinot Auxerrois from Albert Mann is simple but expressive. It is silky on the palate and loaded with notes of peach, grapefruit, pineapple, and corefruit. Great with everything from fish to pork.

title: Domaine Alain Burguet & Fils Vosne-Romanée Premier Cru Les Rouges du Dessus

paras.text: Domaine Alain Burguet & Fils Vosne-Romanée Premier Cru Les Rouges du Dessus | Fine Vines
Vinification: 100% de-stemmed, indigenous yeast fermentation, minimal intervention. Aged for 19 months in barrel (30% oak).

title: Domaine Albert Mann Gewürztraminer Grand Cru Furstentum Vieilles Vignes

paras.text: Domaine Albert Mann Gewürztraminer Grand Cru Furstentum Vieilles Vignes | Fine Vines
Hand-harvested from this Grand Cru limestone site in Kientzheim. Floral bouquet of rose and violets. Beautiful complexity. Fruity on the palate, pineapple and clementine.

title: Domaine Albert Mann Pinot Blanc

paras.text: Bright straw. Pinot blanc-dominated aromas of beeswax and white flowers. Enters fresh and clean, then shows bright, lively flavors of white stone fruit, delicate herbs and sweet corn. You may want to drink this easygoing, very food-friendly wine by the bucketful. Hand-harvested from Kientzheim and Wettolsheim.

title: Domaine Albert Mann Pinot Gris Rosenberg

paras.text: A warmly perfumed wine, it has all the aromatic characters of Pinot Gris, rounded and soft with only a few hints of acidity. Off-dry, it is ready to drink.

title: Domaine Albert Mann Riesling Cuvée Albert

paras.text: Bright straw-green. Aromas of kerosene and blood orange. Juicy and ripe on the palate, with flavors of orange, tangerine and yellow apple smoothed by 7 grams per liter of residual sugar. Almost chewy concentration here, but comes across as very nicely balanced, finishing with bright acidity and lingering lemon and cinnamon basil flavors. Not the last word in complexity, but irresistible already. From an assemblage of old vines.

Hand-harvested selection of old vines from 2 fields names : Rosenberg (Wettolsheim) and Altenbourg (Kienthzeim). Expressive nose shows beautiful fruity flavors, citrus fruits, lemon. Attack on the palate is lively underlined by a fine minerality.

title: Domaine Albert Mann Riesling Grand Cru Schlossberg

paras.text: Hand-harvested from this Grand Cru granite site in Kientzheim. Beautiful bottle with a great aromatic complexity, dominance of fruits, citrus fruits underline by a fine minerality. Wine of gastronomy.

title: Domaine Anne Parent Bourgogne Côte-D'Or

paras.text: Vinification : stalking 100%; cold maceration for about 4 days; temperature control; crushing twice a day; total fermentation skins 12 to 14 days
A fine, bright colour, an eloquent, fruity bouquet with hints of cherry. Well- balanced and smooth, this wine is not pretentious, is pleasant and nice to drink whilst relatively young
To be tasted when 3 to 5 years old with pork meats and delicatessen, meats and grilled poultry

title: Domaine Anne Parent Bourgogne Pinot Noir

paras.text: A nice, pleasant and gourmet wine. To be drunk quite young. Appellation: Burgundy Appellation
Wine-Making: Stalking, cold maceration for about 3 to 5 days, temperature control, crushing and pumping over 2 to 3 times a day, total fermentation on skins 10 to 12 days according to vintages.

title: Domaine Anne Parent Corton Grand Cru Blanc

paras.text: A beautiful brilliant gold color. The aromatic complexity expresses a large range of aromas with pear, apricot, and grilled nuts hints. The mouth is rich and dense, while enhanced by its minerality. A refined and balanced wine.
Wine-making : pressing of full grapes, alcoholic and malolactic fermentation in French oak barrels. Light stirring of the lees.

title: Domaine Anne Parent Bourgogne Pinot Noir Selection Pomone

paras.text: This wine is awesome red Burgundy. It’s muscular, deep and rich, and it expresses style, clarity and elegance. It is more than you could ever ask for in a bottle of Burgundy.
Anne Parent notes “the wines have a presence, a life if you will, that is rarely seen and makes them wonderfully satisfying.”
It’s named after Pomona, the Roman goddess of fruitful abundance. And who doesn’t want to party like a goddess, or with one?

Finally, this “Bourgogne Selection Pomone” is actually this: 10% Premier Cru Pommard Noizons, 20% Ladoix Premier Cru, and the balance all from older vineyards (70+ years) from the “correct” side of the Route des Grands Crus in Pommard Village.

Most “Bourgogne” is generic – it can come from anywhere across all of Burgundy. Because the region is generic, the French would consider Bourgogne to be the least significant Pinot Noir in Burgundy. However, 70% of this wine comes from the Village of Pommard. “Village” wines are from a specific village. The tighter the geographic designation, the higher the quality. Then, 30% of this wine comes from premiers crus vineyards – higher quality still, and second only to the famed Grands Crus. As Robert Parker’s
sums this wine up, “this ‘basic’ red Burgundy punches at a high village cru level.”

title: Domaine Anne Parent Ladoix Premier Cru La Corvée

paras.text: A quite steady and brilliant color. A powerful style which gradually opens on cherry and redcurrant hints. The mouth presents firm tannins, which will smoothen with time.
Harvesting : by hand, and strict sorting on 2 sorting tables, one of which is vibrating.
Wine-making : stalking, cold maceration for about 3 to 5 days, temperature control, crushing and pumping over 2 to 3 times a day, total fermentation on skins: 16 to 18 days according to vintages.
Maturing : 14 months in French oak barrels, 30 % of which are new, bottled by us at the winery.

title: Domaine Anne Parent Monthelie

paras.text: Harvesting : by hand, and strict sorting on 2 sorting tables, one of which is vibrating.
Wine-making : stalking, cold maceration for about 3 to 5 days, temperature control, crushing and pumping over 2 to 3 times a day, total fermentation on skins: 16 to 18 days according to vintages.
Maturing : 14 months in French oak barrels, 30 % of which are new, bottled by us at the winery.
​​​​​​​A fleshy and crunchy mouth, with a red fruits expression that leave a fresh sensation. Silky tanins.

title: Domaine Anne Parent Pommard La Croix Blanche

paras.text: A bright and intense ruby colour. Wild cherry and blackcurrant aromas. In mouth, this wine combines strength and subtlety.
Harvesting : by hand, and strict sorting on 2 sorting tables, one of which is vibrating.
Wine-making : stalking, cold maceration for about 3 to 5 days, temperature control, crushing and pumping over 2 to 3 times a day, total fermentation on skins: 16 to 18 days according to vintages.
Maturing : 14 to 16 months in French oak barrels, 30 % of which are new, bottled by us at the winery.

title: Domaine Anne Parent Pommard Premier Cru Les Epenots

paras.text: Delicacy, density, and an innate sense of balance are typical of this great wine. Its colour is intense, the nose is very expressive with violet and red fruits aromas like cherry or morello cherry, which express a great complexity. The mouth is fleshy and concentrated, and the tanins are fine, velvety, and elegant.
Harvesting : by hand, and strict sorting on 2 sorting tables, one of which is vibrating.
Wine-making : stalking, cold maceration for about 3 to 5 days, temperature control, crushing and pumping over 2 to 3 times a day, total fermentation on skins: 18 to 20 days according to vintages.
Maturing : 16 to 18 months in French oak barrels, 30 % to 40 % of which are new, bottled by us at the winery.

title: Domaine Bachey-Legros Chassagne-Montrachet

paras.text: 100% Chardonnay. Pressing by pneumatic press is light and controlled. Alcoholic fermentation is done at low temperature on fine lees, in barrel. We pay great attention to the quality of the lees. These will give the roundness and complexity of aromas we are looking for. At barrelling, we ensure that there are sufficient lees present. After that, oak barrel ageing lasts from 12 to 15 months, depending on the vintage, with regular batonnage (lees-stirring) through to malolactic fermentation.

title: Domaine Bachey-Legros Chassagne-Montrachet Les Plantes Momières Vieilles Vignes

paras.text: Domaine Bachey-Legros Chassagne-Montrachet Les Plantes Momières Vieilles Vignes | Fine Vines

It is less and less usual to find very old Pinot Noir vines in Chassagne-Montrachet. So we have always wanted to keep this plot just as it was planted in 1946 by Joseph Bachey, grandfather of Christiane. It has a very lovely situation, just below the "Abbaye de Morgeot" Premier Cru, on soils that are relatively calcareous. The exposure is favourable to early ripening. The old vines reflect perfectly the natural qualities of the terroir: the roots plunge deep into the limestone and the vines have a low yield, small berries with a thick skin, rich in tannins, and a good proportion of mixed-size millerande grapes. This is a noble raw material. It is totally destemmed before a gentle and delicate vinification, which is necessary to conserve all its elegance. The time in vat is limited to 17 days, almost without human intervention. All the contributes to a wine with tannins which are both naurally powerful and silky. It will keep its deep color and its aromas of black fruits for a long time.

title: Domaine Bachey-Legros Chassagne Montrachet Premier Cru Morgeot

paras.text: Our plot nevertheless reveals a strong identity: concentrated on the lieu-dit "Les Petits Clos", extremely well exposed East-West, in the heart of the appellation. Its rich, red, clay-limestone soils, drawn upon by deeply-rooted vines planted in 1950, give the wine the roundness of great whie wines, heightened and balanced by a good mineral structure.

Fourteen months of ageing on the lees reveals the natural qualities of this exceptional wine. In its youth it already charms with its suppleness, its good length, and its floral notes, yellow fruits and citrus. As it ages a miracle occurs, a veritable metamorphosis. It assumes an intense golden hue and developes even more volume and substance.

title: Domaine Bachey-Legros Maranges Le Goty Vieilles Vignes

paras.text: Maranges... An appellation in full flight which we have to take great care with in order to get the best from it. Le Goty is one of the best areas. The end of our rows are cheek to cheek with the Santenay Charmes. Planted in 1945, the vines' root system delve deep and produce a concentrated wine with an incredible colour of black ink. The grapes tend to mature late and we give them time to ripen fully to obtain the softest possible tannins. Then by vinifying delicately and quickly we allow the purity of the fruit to express itself.

title: Domaine Bachey-Legros Maranges Vieille Vignes

paras.text: Maranges... An appellation in full flight which we have to take great care with in order to get the best from it. The end of our rows are cheek to cheek with the Santenay Charmes. Planted in 1945, the vines' root system delve deep and produce a concentrated wine with an incredible color of black ink. The grapes tend to mature late and we give them time to ripen fully to obtain the softest possible tannins. Then by vinifying delicately and quickly we allow the purity of the fruit to express itself.

title: Domaine Bachey-Legros Meursault Les Grands Charrons

paras.text: 100% Chardonnay. Pressing by pneumatic press is light and controlled. Alcoholic fermentation is done at low temperature on fine lees, in barrel. We pay great attention to the quality of the lees. These will give the roundness and complexity of aromas we are looking for. At barrelling, we ensure that there are sufficient lees present. title: Domaine Bachey-Legros Puligny-Montrachet

paras.text: This classy Puligny displays strong minerality, with some citrus nuances. The palate is precise and mineral with fine concentration of citrus, melon and stone fruits, with a touch of oak, this has a long and enjoyable finish.

Made from a combination of estate and purchased fruit, the Bachey-Legros was barrel fermented in new and used French oak. Classic in style, it displays beautiful aromas of white fruits and nutty oakiness. Apple, peach and lemon dominate on the rich palate, along with a lovely finish of almond, mineral and citrus.

title: Domaine Bachey-Legros Santenay Clos Des Hâtes Vieilles Vignes

paras.text: "Les Hates" is one of the best terroirs in Santenay village. We could discuss its ranking for hours, so close is it to a premier cru; close both in geography, since it is literally surrounded by Santenay Premiers Crus, and also quality. Our plot is in the heart of the Les Hates climat, in Le Clos.

The fact that the vines grow in an enclosed clos gives this unique wine all its particularity and specificity. The vines are protected and the soil subjected very little to erosion, on well-drained, rather calcareous land on a gentle slope. The terroir has therefore kept all its intergrity, and the old vines, planted in 1935, are perfect in getting the best from it. They have maintained an exceptional state of health and their yield self-regulates quite naturally. When harvested, the grapes show lovely concentration, with a lot of different sized, millerande berries. Our Clos des Hates has a strong personality, with good minerality, with tannins that are pure bred from the beginning. On the nose, this wine does a balancing act between the depth of fully ripe black fruits and the freshness of red fruits, with lovely hints of spice.

title: Domaine Bachey-Legros Santenay Les Champs Claudes

paras.text: The Bachey family has been working their vineyards and making wine for 6 generations and the house is located on the oldest street of the village of Santenay-le-Haut. This picturesque quarter dates back to the beginning of the 18th century and is well worth a visit. The estate produces red and white Burgundian, Santenay and Chassagne-Montrachet wines.

title: Domaine Bachey-Legros Santenay Les Charmes Vieilles Vignes

paras.text: The name says it all; this wine has everything to captivate you. Les Charmes are situated just below the "Clos Rousseau" Premier Cru in Santenay. Planted in 1950, these old vines also draw rich, supple and silky tannins from deep down in the limestone. A wine that is very round, with a natural garnet-red color, aromas of fresh cherry and a touch of spices. Elegance, the finesse of exquisite fruit, good length; the magic works immediately.

title: Domaine Bachey-Legros Santenay Premier Cru Clos Rousseau Les Fourneaux Vieilles Vignes

paras.text: Domaine Bachey-Legros Santenay Premier Cru Clos Rousseau Les Fourneaux Vieilles Vignes | Fine Vines
Domaine Bachey-Legros Santenay Premier Cru Clos Rousseau Les Fourneaux Vieilles Vignes
Domaine Bachey-Legros Santenay Premier Cru Clos Rousseau Les Fourneaux Vieilles Vignes

Les Fourneaux is part of the "Clos Rousseau" Premier Cru appellation. This parcel contains our oldest vines, planted in 1914 and some of the oldest of the Cote de Beaune. Its exceptional vines and its age led us to decide to make an exclusive cuvee of it, "apart". The result is clearly a wine "apart", out of the ordinary.

An experience for the palate. These are ancient vines that we treat with much care, and great respect. We work hard supporting, lifting up, bolstering these old vines, all by hand, human hand, in this plot where using machinery is impossible anyway, given the large size of each vine base. So our work is like that of a curator in a botanical museum, with all the emotion that you might feel when you are in contact with an ancient work of art. The deep roots plunge far down into the terroir, giving the grapes tannins of unparalleled velvety smoothness. Those privileged to come and taste it may boast of having drunk such a unique wine, with such identity, marked by very ripe black fruit.

title: Domaine Bachey-Legros Santenay Premier Cru La Comme Vieilles Vignes

paras.text: La Comme is a terroir which we know intimately. It is one of the most famous vineyards in Santenay. Our plot is planted with old vines (1955) and produces fruit which we love to work with: reduced yields, small grapes which are rich in the character of their terroir. Ideally situated, in the middle of the appellation with a 360 degree exposure, these vines are caressed by the sun's rays all day long. The view is magnificent and even offers us a fine view of our Morgeot vines.

The opposite of our Clos Rousseau, both in its geographical situation and in its character, la Comme is a Santenay from the Chassagne side of the village. A mineral wine, powerful, with good aging potential which a short and gentle vinification tames to liberate its seductive power within a solid structure.

title: Domaine Bachey-Legros Santenay Premier Cru Clos Rousseau Vieilles Vignes

paras.text: Domaine Bachey-Legros Santenay Premier Cru Clos Rousseau Vieilles Vignes | Fine Vines

This wine is about balance... Our Clos Rousseau comes from three plots whose vines are all more than 30 years old: Les Fourneaux (planted in 1914), the Grand Clos Rousseau (1980), and the Petit Clos Rousseau (1955). Les Clos and Les Fourneaux are highly complementary. Grand and Petit Clos, their vines flush with the calcareous bed-rock, give the wine its mineral structure, and a dominant characteristic of red fruit, all finesse and elegance. Les Fourneax is where our oldest vines grow. These deep soil bring an exceptional richness in mature and very silky tannins, with aromas of ripe black fruits. The three cuvees are vinified seperately, always gently. We seek to achieve a perfect balance between structure, elegance and aromatic complexity.

title: Domaine Bachey-Legros Santenay Sous La Roche

paras.text: We planted this plot of a half-hectare in 2000. It is showing good characteristics that deserve to be discovered.

The appellation is situated above the "Beaurepaire" Premiers Crus, in Santenay. "Sous La Roche" is named very appropriately, as it is very close to the bedrock, scattered with little murger stone walls, the soils bring lots of mineralogy to the wine. Another peculiarity of the location is that at night the surface stones give off the heat retained during the day, allowing the grapes to mature perfectly, and giving the wine a distance roundness.

All these natural qualities led us to plant Chardonnay here. Ultimately, our Santenay "Sous La Roche" with its natural well balanced freshness has all the qualities of great white wines. A stylish and gourmand wine.

title: Domaine Badoz Arbois Pupillin Pinot Noir

paras.text: Made from the Pinot Noir grape, this cuvée matured in stainless steel vats then aged in lightning, can accompany your meal with an aperitif with cheese. Its beautiful ruby color will seduce you, its fine and attractive nose with aromas of violet will charm you. Round, slightly robust red wine, very tasty as it should be!

title: Domaine Badoz Cotes De Jura Grains De Poulsard

paras.text: Grains de Poulsard is the brand of our Estate identifying the Poulsard grape traditionally vinified as a red with a short maceration. Beautiful and light red dress with amber reflections, "coral". Nose of tender spices, raisins and red fruits, vinous bouquet of red fruits (strawberry, morello cherry), finish of dried fruit and tender spices, enhanced with a tannic touch on the finish. It is an ideal wine for a whole meal where it easily replaces red and white wine. Tasted in any season, it offers more particularly an original and appreciated agreement with Morteau sausage, raclettes, salted meats, fish and grilled meats, white meats, smoked fish.

title: Domaine Badoz Cotes De Jura Tradition Les Grands Roussots

paras.text: Cuvée made from the blend of Chardonnay (60%) / Savagnin (40%). 3 years of aging in oak barrels in our age-old cellars will be necessary for the Savagnin grape variety to obtain this very distinctive taste. Chardonnay is aged in old casks before blending. The nose is overwhelmed by the typical savagnin flavors. Then the chardonnay slowly takes its place. There are nuts and almonds, fruits and flowers. As for the mouth, with its long finish on the nut, it is fresh and spicy.

title: Domaine Bart Bonnes Mares

paras.text: We have one hectare of Bonnes Mares, says Pierre Bart. We are next to Domaine de Voguë, close to the Route des Grands Crus. Since 2007 we use 50 per cent whole bunches and 50 per cent new oak. We think it gives the wine a better balance when you have the same percentage of the two.

title: Domaine Bart Marsannay Au Champ Salomon

paras.text: When it comes to Marsannay, Domaine Bart's selection of crus is an embarrassment of riches. Au Champ Salomon, one of their best, is located in a prime spot on the mid-slope, producing wines which marry power with elegance and longevity. The grapes from 35-year-old plus vines are hand harvested, fermented with native yeasts, aged for 18 months in barrel, of which approximately 30% are new. The Champ Salomon shows its relation to Gevrey-Chambertin next door with aromas of ripe black cherry and strawberry with earth and spice. The palate is dense and rich, with ripe cherry and blackberry fruit over earthy, mineral-laden acidity. This young Burgundy will accompany a steak or grilled pork, served cool, best held for three to five years for a mature experience...

title: Domaine Bart Chambertin Clos de Beze

paras.text: The Clos de Bèze is more sumptuous and less high-toned than the Bonnes-Mares, offering up a bouquet of rose petal, candied peel, rich black cherry, cassis and dark chocolate. On the palate the wine is full-bodied, ample and expansive, its similarly tense chassis of tannin more completely enveloped in layers of ripe but vibrant fruit.

An ultra-spicy and markedly floral nose combines notes of red cherry, wild currant and earth with those of soft game and underbrush nuances. The polished, sophisticated and intense middle weight plus flavors display a lovely sense of verve that can also be found on the mineral-driven and well-balanced finale. Like the Bonnes Mares this isn't an especially big example of the appellation but it's harmonious and should drink well young if that's your preference.

title: Domaine Bart Marsannay Les Favieres

paras.text: A rare white Burgundy made entirely from 45 and 60-year-old vines of Chardonnay Musqué – a clone of Chardonnay with perfumed, Muscat-like characteristics.

title: Domaine Bart Marsannay Les Finottes

paras.text: Soft wood sets off earthy and humus-suffused aromas of forest floor and dark berry fruit. There is good freshness and vitality to the delicious flavors that possess reasonable depth and persistence. This is light but pretty and should drink well young.

Thanks to sandy soils, this wine is particularly aromatic, and the fruit profile is soft and inviting. Pierre Bart, the current generation owner and winemaker at Domaine Bart, treats this wine to no new oak, using only concrete and older oak barrels to showcase the delicate fruit. On the nose the wine displays bright red cherry fruit with sweet clove and nutmeg. The cherry fruit continues into the palate where it is complemented by savory wild mushroom and hints of forest floor. The body is on the lighter side, and the finish is of lingering baking spices.

title: Domaine Bart Marsannay Les Longeroies

paras.text: The area Bart Longeroies Marsannay unveils a purple dress and a nose of rose and violet aromas, a mouth gourmet on raspberry and blackcurrant, with spicy notes. A Marsannay of great finesse.

title: Domaine Bart Marsannay Les Grands Vignes

paras.text: Closer to the village, on the Couchey side of Marsannay, you’ll find Les Grandes Vignes and Champ Salomon. Les Grandes Vignes is quite close to Clos Salomon, but it does not have the same concentration, says Pierre Bart. In terms of winemaking Les Grandes Vignes is exactly the same as Les Echezots.

title: Domaine Bart Marsannay Saint Jacques

paras.text: St. Jacques is a small vineyard on the southern side of the appellation. There are only 2 owners of this vineyard, and Martin Bart is quite proud of it. It is a rich style, showing both black and red fruit notes, a lovely and delightful supple mouthfeel, and extremely pretty sweet fruit notes. It reminds me of a good Morey St. Denis in its combination of minerality and focused fruit. Quite spectacular!

title: Domaine Bernard Reverdy Sancerre

paras.text: Area of the vineyard: 8.83 hectares (19.8 acres)Soil: Limestone-clay (Kimmeridgian marl and
Throughout the year, our philosophy is to allow the grapes the chance to best reflect our land and terroirs.
Vinification: Harvest between the 10th and 21st of September, each parcel at its optimal maturity. Slow fermentation process at low temperatures before maturation on fine lees.

Tasting: Brilliant pale golden robe. The nose opens on fresh, fine and complex fragrances, dominated by white fruit (pear), white flowers and citrus overtones. The palate is very ample, perfectly balanced by a continuous freshness and an accurate tension. Its wonderful bouquet and length will let you with a delicious memory of party in the orchard.
It goes marvellously with seafood and fish (zander, trout, pike...) and, of course, withCrottin de Chavignol goat cheese.

title: Domaine Glantenay Pommard Premier Cru Les Rugiens

paras.text: Located next to Volnay, the terroir of Rugiens is one of most famous of Pommard with its name derived from the word "rougion" - the red of the earth. With sunny southeast exposure, this site is well protected from wind which provides the power and complexities of a well matured wine. On a surface area of just .2ha, the vines are very old, planted in 1935. Hand-harvested into small crates, yields are around 25 hL/ha. Fermentation takes place naturally in gravity fed vats with indigenous yeasts and about a 15 day maceration time. Ageing takes place in oak barrels, maximum 30% new, for to 14-18 months depending on the vintage. After one racking without pump, bottling is done without fining or filtration.

title: Domaine Glantenay Pommard Premier Cru Les Saussilles

paras.text: Uniquely situated on the hillside bordering Beaune, the 1er Cru Saussilles Pommard is just above the small and famous Epenots vineyard and next to the Beaune Clos des Mouches. The name dates back to the Middle Ages: es Saucis or Saussaie, place planted with willows. The vines of this almost .8ha parcel were planted in 1925 (the oldest in the vineyard) from unknown rootstock. Hand-harvested into small crates, yields are around 20 hL/ha. Fermentation takes place naturally in gravity fed vats with indigenous yeasts and about a 15 day maceration time. Ageing takes place in oak barrels, maximum 30% new, for to 14-18 months depending on the vintage. After one racking without pump, bottling is done without fining or filtration.

title: Domaine Berthaut-Gerbet Chambolle-Musigny Premier Cru Les Plantes

paras.text: Vinification: 100% de-stemmed, 3-5 days' cold maceration (10°C), mostly pump-overs with some punch-downs, indigenous yeast alcoholic fermentation. Malolactic fermentation in concrete tanks, 1 year aging in oak barrels (35% new).

title: Domaine Berthaut-Gerbet Clos Vougeot Grand Cru

paras.text: Terroir: Along the east wall of the Clos, minimal slope, rocky soils with more clay
Vinification: 100% de-stemmed, 3-5 days' cold maceration (10°C), mostly pump-overs with some punch-downs, indigenous yeast alcoholic fermentation, aging in oak barrels.

title: Domaine Berthaut-Gerbet Fixin Les Clos

paras.text: Vinification: 100% de-stemmed, 3-5 days' cold maceration (10°C), mostly pump-overs with some punch-downs, indigenous yeast alcoholic fermentation. Malolactic fermentation in concrete tanks, 12 months' aging in oak barrels (20% new), total élevage 20 months.

title: Domaine Berthaut-Gerbet Côte de Nuits-Villages

paras.text: Vinification: 100% de-stemmed, mostly pump-overs with some punch-downs, indigenous yeast fermentation. Aged for 12 months in barrel (no new oak).

title: Domaine Berthaut-Gerbet Gevrey-Chambertin

paras.text: Terroir: 2 parcels (La Burie and Les Crais) at bottom of slope, limestone and marl soils
Vinification: 100% de-stemmed, 3-5 days' cold maceration (10°C), mostly pump-overs with some punch-downs, indigenous yeast alcoholic fermentation, 15-20 days'
. Malolactic fermentation in concrete tanks, 1 year aging in oak barrels (30% new), 6 additional months' blending before bottling.

title: Domaine Berthaut-Gerbet Vosne-Romanée

paras.text: Vinification: 100% de-stemmed, 3-5 days' cold maceration (10°C), mostly pump-overs with some punch-downs, indigenous yeast alcoholic fermentation in concrete tank. Aging in oak barrels (30% new).

title: Domaine Berthaut-Gerbet Vosne-Romanée Premier Cru Les Suchots

paras.text: Vine Age: Planted in 1900 with replacement of vines as necessary (60 years old on average)
Vinification: 3-5 days' cold maceration (10°C), mostly pump-overs with some punch-downs, indigenous yeast alcoholic fermentation. 1 year aging in oak barrels.

title: Domaine Berthaut-Gerbet Gevrey Chambertin Combe du Dessus

paras.text: From a half a hectare parcel called Combe de Dessus, which sits below the Clos des Chezeaux, which is below Cazetiers. Made with approximately 20% new oak.

title: Domaine Bruno Clair Chambertin Clos de Bèze Grand Cru

paras.text: Chambertin Clos de Bèze is a 15.4 ha grand cru vineyard. Clos de Bèze may be called Chambertin, but not vice versa.

This vineyard has a moderate to gentle east-facing slope with many small ripples and waves that interrupt the concavity of the slope, creating several gentle pockets as opposed to one large belly. The variability of the topography is likely influenced by a patchwork of faults and microfaults beneath the surface. The north end of Clos de Bèze dips towards the north.

Clos de Bèze has an 11% average slope gradient, which is quite gentle compared to 17% gradient in Clos Saint-Jacques, but it is slightly steeper than Chambertin. Its elevation is 275 to 300 meters; 310 meters for that little bit at the southwest corner at the very top of the slope where the rows run NS.
It is a warmer terroir than Chambertin because the latter has cooler breezes coming from the Combe Grisard above.

Vinification: Mostly de-stemmed (up to 20% whole-cluster in good harvest), indigenous yeast fermentation, pump-overs, some punch-downs. Aged for 18 months in barrel (0-50% new oak), short blending period in tank before bottling.

title: Domaine Bruno Clair Chambolle-Musigny Les Véroilles

paras.text: Several small plots given up after the phylloxerna crisis, belonging either to the commune of Chambolle-Musigny or to individuals, were rented in order to form two larger and usable plots.

Planted in 1989, in soil favourable to the vine (planted in the 18th and 19th century), but uncultivated since, to produce a wine resulting from a commune which is dear to me for the finesse and the elegance of its wines. The venture appeared very positive because since 1992, first harvest of this vineyard, the wines have been fine and silky. With the years passing and the increasingly deeper rooting of the vines, the wines become more extensive and deep. The wines are well scented, silky and gain in texture and length. Thanks to their natural finesse, they can be drunk young or kept in storage for a few years.
Vinification: 20% whole-cluster, indigenous yeast fermentation in open wood tanks, punch-downs. Aged for 18 months on fine lees in barrel (0- 50% new).

title: Domaine Bruno Clair Corton-Charlemagne Grand Cru

paras.text: Vinification: Delicate pneumatic pressing, indigenous yeast fermentation, racked. Aged for 18 months on fine lees in barrel (0-30% new). Short blending period in tank before bottling.

title: Domaine Bruno Clair Gevrey-Chambertin Premier Cru Clos du Fonteny Monopole

paras.text: Domaine Bruno Clair Gevrey-Chambertin Premier Cru Clos du Fonteny Monopole | Fine Vines

Monopoly of the Domaine Bruno Clair, this plot is located in the upper part of the "climate" les Fontenys and in the continuity of the great vintages of Gevrey-Chambertin, close to the les Ruchottes-Chambertin. Half was planted in 1972 and the other half in 1987. The relatively poor soil is composed of white clay as opposed to red clay at the bottom of Chambertin. The calcareous rock is definitely present in the surface and brings finesse and elegance to this wine from a village known for the power of its wines.

Vinification: 35% whole-cluster in 2016, indigenous yeast fermentation. mostly pump-overs, some punch-downs. Aged for 18 months in barrel (0-50% new oak). Short blending period in tank before bottling.

title: Domaine Bruno Clair Gevrey-Chambertin Premier Cru Clos Saint-Jacques

paras.text: Domaine Bruno Clair Gevrey-Chambertin Premier Cru Clos Saint-Jacques | Fine Vines

According to several old analists, the Clos Saint-Jacques was classified "tête de cuvée" corresponding to our Grand cru of today. It is considered to be the most prestigious of the 1er cru of Gevrey-Chambertin.

The Clos Saint-Jacques is worked by five wine growers. Each owns a plot which extends upwards on the slope and this brings a great balance to the wines. The vines of our plot are particularly remarkable, thanks to the "massale" (visual selection of the most robust vineplants) made by my father more than 30 years ago. Half of the plot was planted in 1957, the other part in 1972. The vines are of an astonishing qualitative regularity there. Le Clos Saint-Jacques always produces a fine, complex wine to keep.

Vinification: 40% whole cluster, indigenous yeast fermentation, minimal punch-downs and pump-overs (one each in general per day). Aged for 18 months in barrel (0-50% new oak). Racked once for short blending period in tank before bottling.

title: Domaine Bruno Clair Gevrey-Chambertin Premier Cru Les Cazetiers

paras.text: Les Cazetiers is next to the Clos Saint-Jacques. Our plot is located in the upper part of the "climat" and is characterized by extremely poor, marly soil and limestone deposits. Three different dates of plantation; a third planted in 1958, another third in 1972 and the rest in 1996. The combination of the type of soil and and the quality of the vines produce low yields and grapes that are "millerandés" (partial crop failure) in the majority of the harvest.

The wine is characterized by very low acidity amply compensated by complex tannins of a surprising richness. The comparison of organoleptic qualities between our Clos Saint-Jacques and our Cazetiers shows in every vintage a very clear difference between the wines: le Cazetiers being more accessible in youth on the aromatic level and by the unique silkiness of the tannins as opposed to the Clos Saint-Jacques which is more reserved in the first years. A good example of the incredible variety of the terroirs and "climates" of the Côte is that these two wines result from vines being about the same age, from the same "massale" selection, having similar maturity and vinified in the same fermenting room, according to the same philosophy

Vinification: Mostly de-stemmed (20% whole-cluster in good harvest), indigenous yeast fermentation, pump-overs, some punch-downs. Aged for 18 months in barrel (0-50% new oak). Short blending period in tank before bottling.

title: Domaine Bruno Clair Marsannay Blanc

paras.text: Marsannay Blanc, comes from various plots on the Marsannay slope, above les Longeroies, les Étalles, les Vaudenelles and les Roseys. It is a blend of 80 % chardonnay and 20% pinot blanc. Purposely planted on poor soil, very fine clay, called " rabbit grounds ", the chardonnay gives fruity aromas whereas the pinot blanc brings roundness and meatiness.
Vinification: Pneumatic pressing, indigenous yeast fermentation. Aged for 18 months in older oak barrels calledfoudres. Short blending period in tank before bottling.

title: Domaine Bruno Clair Gevrey-Chambertin Premier Cru Petite Chapelle

paras.text: Vinification: 30% whole-cluster, indigenous yeast fermentation in open wooden tanks, minimal punch-downs and pump-overs (one each per day in general). Aged for 18 months in barrel (0-50% new).

title: Domaine Bruno Clair Marsannay Blanc Source des Roches

paras.text: Terroir: Multiple parcels: Les Vaudenelles, Les Rosey, Boivins, facing southeast, shallow white marl soil on limestone bedrock
Vinification: Direct pressing, indigenous yeast fermentation (40% new oak). Aged for 16 months in barrel.

title: Domaine Bruno Clair Marsannay Rouge Les Vaudenelles

paras.text: Domaine Bruno Clair is the owner of approximately 11 hectares - 27.18 acres, on the Marsannay commune.

The soils of Marsannay are unfortunately little known worldwide and the wines too often underestimated. Because the commune does not have the prestige of its famous neighbours in the south, the wines of Marsannay are often drunk too young. Our soils give rather tannic and well-structured red wines. Waiting for 3 to 8 years according to the vintage often proves essential to maximize the qualitative potential of the wine and your pleasure.

The soil of les Vaudenelles, 1,58 ha - 3.90 acres, is located at the top of the slope; the soil is poor because of the levelling bedrock. It produces a Marsannay that is fine and elegant. Its color is slightly lighter than that of its peers. The wine always has good aromas, is supple and easy to drink. Marsannay-Vaudenelles wines need 3 to 5 years of cellaring to reach their peak.

Vinification: Up to 20% whole-cluster, indigenous yeast fermentation. Mostly pump-overs, some punch-downs. Aged for 18 months in barrel (0-50% new oak) and/or foudres. Short blending period in tank before bottling.

title: Domaine Bruno Clair Morey-Saint-Denis Blanc En La Rue De Vergy

paras.text: Located just above the les Bonnes-Mares, this plot presents a remarkable pedology: the soil is non-existent. The vines are planted directly on the calcareous bedrock and do very well there; they manage to find crevices between the stones and the rock strata to deeply plunge the roots in search of water and nutrients. A part, 0,64 ha - 1.58 acres, was planted in pinot noir in 1980 and the rest of the plot, 0,51 ha - 1.26 acres, planted in 1981 with chardonnay.

Our white Morey St-Denis is one of the rare white wines of the Côte de Nuits, and the soil lends itself to it remarkably. It is a scented wine and with a strong mineral character. Acidity is always good and the wine, pleasant in its youth, ages very well.
Vinification: Pneumatic pressing, indigenous yeast fermentation, racked. Aged for 18 months on fine lees in barrel (0-30% new oak) or

title: Domaine Bruno Clair Savigny-les-Beaune Premier Cru La Dominode

paras.text: The old vines produce a rich and powerful wine that is not common in the Côte de Beaune.

La Dominode belongs to the 1er cru les Haut-Jarrons. It is at the heart of this lieu (place). The yields are naturally low but regular because the vines were planted in 1902. The exposure to the east is ideal and the ground is a mixture of stones and clay.

I have been vinifying la Dominode since 1979 and it has undoubtedly the most consistent vines of the domaine - always low yields and beautiful maturity of the grapes. The quality and the age of the vines contribute to this consistency. There are, naturally, annual variations according to the vintage and the weather, but the variations are fewer than in other vineyards. The color is always deep, tannins are full and rich. It is a wine that demands a few years of ageing, often more than 10 years, before it is ready to be tasted. A wine to be cellared.

Vinification: Mostly de-stemmed (20% whole-cluster in good harvest), indigenous yeast fermentation. Mostly pump-overs, some punch-downs. Aged for 18 months in barrel (0-50% new oak), short blending period in tank before bottling.

title: Domaine Bruno Clair Morey-Saint-Denis En la rue de Vergy

paras.text: Vinification: 30% whole-cluster, indigenous yeast fermentation in open wooden tanks, minimal punch-downs and pump-overs (one each per day in general). Aged for 18 months in barrel (0-50% new).

This plot presents a remarkable as the soil is non-existent: the vines are planted directly on the limestone bedrock and do very well there; the roots manage to find crevices between the stones and the rock strata to plunge deeply in search of water and nutrients.

Once the grapes arrive in the cellar, the crushing of the bunches helps to improve the texture of the cap and to prolong fermentation time. According to the intensity of the alcoholic fermentation, punch downs will take place from 2 to 8 times per day. Malolactic fermentation usually takes place in the spring when the cellars are heated gently by the warmer weather.

title: Domaine Bruno Clair Vosne-Romanée Les Champs Perdrix

paras.text: Vinification: 30% whole-cluster, indigenous yeast fermentation in open wooden tanks, minimal punch-downs and pump-overs (one each per day in general). Aged for 18 months in barrel (0-50% new).

title: Domaine Brusset Gigondas Les Hauts de Montmirail

paras.text: Deep dark purple color. Fruity and spicy rich nose, complex. Very round and powerful, good length on the palate, solid tannins, beautiful woody, ripe retro-olfaction, chocolate.

title: Domaine Brusset Côtes du Rhône Laurent B

paras.text: Cotes du Rhone Laurent B is 80% young-vine Cairanne and the rest Plan de Dieu, a blend of 60% Grenache, 20% Syrah and 10% each Cinsault and Mourvedre that sees no wood. Its medium-bodied, fresh and fruity, with cherry and blueberry fruit that's juicy.

title: Domaine Jerome Castagnier Bourgogne Passe Tout Grains

paras.text: Domaine Castagnier Bourgogne Passetoutgrains 2016 Domaine Castagnier is made from the Pinot Noir grape (100%).

Garnet color with brilliant reflections. Nose with intense fruit aromas (Cassis, cherry, strawberry, ...). The palate is round, with a nice acidity which enhances the wine. A very accessible and very pleasant wine that will be unanimous !!

title: Domaine Cecile Tremblay Bourgogne La Croix Blanche

paras.text: "Pure, refined, and elegant" are just a few words that describe Cecile Tremblay’s remarkable wines. Based in Morey-St. Denis, Cecile runs this interesting biodynamic 10 acres domaine in the Côte de Nuits. Beginning with the 2003 vintage she has garnered much acclaim from Burgundy insiders and the wine press alike. She has added several more appellations over the last 5 years. Her approach is organic and biodynamique. Cecile believes in very dense plantings, manual harvesting, some destemming but more and more whole-cluster fermentations, 15 to 18 months of élevage in approximately one-third new oak barrels and bottling without fining or filtering.

title: Domaine Cecile Tremblay Chambolle Musigny Premier Cru Les Feusselottes

paras.text: Domaine Cecile Tremblay Chambolle Musigny Premier Cru Les Feusselottes | Fine Vines
Rising figure among Burgundy winegrowers, Cécile Tremblay launched her winery in 2003, on family estate. She converted the vines to organic farming and biodynamics.
Plots are very well located, in Vosne-Romanée, Morey Saint-Denis, Chambolle-Musigny et Gevrey-Chambertin. Hand-picking is the rule in Cécile Tremblay's domain.

title: Domaine Cecile Tremblay Chambolle Musigny Premier Cru Les Cabottes

title: Domaine Brusset Gigondas Les Secrets de Montmirail

paras.text: Made from equal proportions of Syrah and Grenache. Fleshy plum and cherry notes juxtapose savory hints of bramble, smoked meat and earth here. It's full bodied and lavish yet anchored by a grip of firm, fine tannins on the finish. Silky yet invigorating and mineral.

title: Domaine Cecile Tremblay Morey-Saint-Denis Tres Girard
