Plots are very well located, in Vosne-Romanée, Morey Saint-Denis, Chambolle-Musigny et Gevrey-Chambertin. Hand-picking is the rule in Cécile Tremblay's domain.

title: Domain Charvin Côtes du Rhône Le Poutet

paras.text: About 15ha of about (depending on the crop variation each year) 81% Grenache, 7% Mourvèdre, 5% Carignan, 7% Syrah that average just 35hL/ha annually. Some vines are as old as 90 years, with the blend averaging 40 years old. Organically farmed and harvested by hand. On a sandy terroir with more clay than limestone and with some round stones (galets roulés), the slopes are north facing and the parcels are just on the northwest limit of the CDP lieu-dit Maucoil. Only indigenous yeasts are used for fermentation in cement tanks (no wood). Whole clusters macerate for about 21 days. The wine is bottled without filtration after 18 months in vats.

title: Domaine Charvin Chateauneuf du Pape

paras.text: Located in the northwest part of the appellation, with vines chiefly in Cabrieres, Maucoil, and Mont Redon, Laurent Charvin makes one of the most elegant and seamless Châteauneuf-du-Papes . He farms all his 9ha Chateauneuf-du-Pape parcels organically. Depending on the crop variation each vintage the blend is roughly 85% Grenache average vine age 58 years, 5% Mourvèdre 61 years, 5% Vaccarèse 62 years, 5% Syrah 21 years. Opting to produce a single cuvée, the winemaking here is staunchly traditional, with no destemming and fermentation and aging occurring all in concrete tanks for 21 months, bottled unfiltered. This is a wine that can age 20 years from any vintage as well as be accessible quite young with just a little breathing.

title: Domaine Chauvenet-Chopin Chambolle-Musigny

paras.text: Chambolle Musigny is a red wine presented most often as the most "feminine" of the Côte De Nuits.
The intensity and the finesse is expressed there indeed with an elegant subtlety.

Hubert is crafting classic wines with fine delicacy of fruit and rich complexity. The barrel regiment Hubert uses includes a little more new oak than before, but not too much. Roughly one-third new barrels are used for the Village and Premier Crus, and up to two-thirds for the Grand Cru. Always supple, opulent, seductive, and fruit-driven, the offerings from Chauvenet-Chopin are friendly, smile-inducing wines.

title: Domaine Chauvenet-Chopin Clos Vougeot Grand Cru

paras.text: Our plot of Clos De Vougeot, 35 ares is located under the Château De La Tour and is over 60 years old.
The Clos de Vougeot wines have an intense robe, a strong persistence in the mouth, and are long-lasting.

title: Domaine Chauvenet-Chopin Côte De Nuits Villages

paras.text: Côte De Nuits Villages 3 ha 60 located in the municipalities of Prémeaux-Prissey, Comblanchien and Corgoloin.
It is wine from hen to pot, but also family celebrations thanks to an excellent quality-price ratio.
It shines purple reflections of Pinot and its aromas are expressed on a background of cherry, blackcurrant and spices.
Tasting Notes: Bright, cherry flavors finish on a touch of coffee bitterness. Juicy, gentle, drinkable and silky already.
Duration And Aging Method: 14-16 months élevage 50% in stainless steel, 50% in 228L oak barrels-no new oak.

title: Domaine Chauvenet-Chopin Nuits-Saint-Georges Premier Cru Aux Thorey

paras.text: Nuits Saint Georges 1er cru "Aux Thorey" Plot of 52 ares, northern part of Nuits Saint Georges.
The wine displays a robe with intense hues. Sloe and wild flowers compete for the scoop with liquorice-anise notes.

Hubert is crafting classic wines with fine delicacy of fruit and rich complexity. The barrel regiment Hubert uses includes a little more new oak than before, but not too much. Roughly one-third new barrels are used for the Village and Premier Crus, and up to two-thirds for the Grand Cru. Always supple, opulent, seductive, and fruit-driven, the offerings from Chauvenet-Chopin are friendly, smile-inducing wines.

title: Domaine Chauvenet-Chopin Nuits-Saint-Georges Premier Cru Les Murgers

paras.text: Domaine Chauvenet-Chopin Nuits-Saint-Georges Premier Cru Les Murgers | Fine Vines
Nuits Saint Georges 1er cru "Les Murgers" plot of 41 ares, northern part of Nuits Saint Georges.

Hubert is crafting classic wines with fine delicacy of fruit and rich complexity. The barrel regiment Hubert uses includes a little more new oak than before, but not too much. Roughly one-third new barrels are used for the Village and Premier Crus, and up to two-thirds for the Grand Cru. Always supple, opulent, seductive, and fruit-driven, the offerings from Chauvenet-Chopin are friendly, smile-inducing wines.

title: Domaine Chauvenet-Chopin Nuits-Saint-Georges Premier Cru Les Chaignots

paras.text: Domaine Chauvenet-Chopin Nuits-Saint-Georges Premier Cru Les Chaignots | Fine Vines
Nuits Saint Georges 1er cru "Les Chaignots" Plot of 39 ares, northern part of Nuits Saint Georges.
a full, but firm structure, in its youth knows how to acquire charm and elegance over the years.

title: Domaine Chauvenet-Chopin Vougeot

paras.text: Tasting Notes: Dark berry fruit aromas of cassis and violet with an earthiness. Medium-bodied flavors that are supported by moderately rustic tannins and fine length.
Soil Type: In stony, sandy soils which produce medium-bodied wines with lots of elegance and finesse.
Duration And Aging Method: 14-16 months élevage in 228L oak barrels- 40 % new oak

title: Domaine Chofflet-Valdenaire Givry Héritage

paras.text: The Chofflet-Valdenaire estate, located in the hillside hamlet of Russily, has been in their family for over 100 years. Today the 11 hectare Domaine is run by Jean Chofflet’s son-in-law, Denis Valdenaire. He produces deliciously fruity, accessible Pinot Noirs that represent outstanding value. The Domaine possesses very well-placed vineyards with an average age of 30 years. Denis has been dedicated to sustainable farming for many years, and was a very early devotee of lutte raisonnée practices.

title: Domaine Charles Lachaux Pommard Auprès du Clos

paras.text: Terroir: A small Clos on the southern side of Pommard, just next to the southern walls of the Château. Clay-limestone soils, where older vines yield clusters with millerandage.
Vinification: Whole-cluster pressing, indigenous yeast fermentation in stainless steel tank. Aged for 12 months in barrel (no new oak), unfined, unfiltered. No added sulfur.

title: Domaine Chofflet-Valdenaire Givry Rouge

paras.text: The estate’s Givry AOC comes from several sloping vineyard parcels. The grapes are entirely hand-harvested and 100% de-stemmed. The wine is aged half in tank, half in two to three year casks for one year before bottling. The Wine Spectator recently acclaimed the 2009 Givry AOC, commenting that it is “rich and dripping with aromas and flavors of black cherry, blackberry and spice. There’s plenty of flesh to coat the tannins, and a lingering finish.” The magazine also cited the 2009 Givry as a “Top Value Recommended Red Burgundy” (June 15, 2011). It is a richly fruity, stylish, ripe and harmonious wine that represents excellent value and is a fine introduction to Pinot Noir from a dedicated grower.

title: Domaine Claude Dugat Bourgogne Rouge

paras.text: The nose offers rich and expressive aromas of red and black cherries, raspberries and red currant . On the palate the wine is very generous, with a rich, silky texture. This wine is fantastic value and has a tremendous depth and intensity for a Bourgogne Rouge.

title: Domaine Claude Dugat Charmes Chambertin Grand Cru

paras.text: Dark cherries, plum, blueberry, and quince capture this quintessential 'Charmes' bouquet. Exotic spices compliment this medium-bodied wine. Quite elegant now but can be kept in bottle for several years to come.

title: Domaine Claude Dugat Gevrey Chambertin

paras.text: This is a hedonistic wine built for indulgence and pleasure. The bouquet offers layers of juicy fruit and floral notes, as well as a filigree minerality. On the palate, this wine is silky, generous and vibrant with layers of juicy fruit.
Tasting Notes: Cool red pinot fruit, dried flowers, earth, and mineral notes. Medium-bodied flavors that possess fine depth and impressive weight for a Village cru.

Vinification: 100% destemmed. Fermentation is started immediately in concrete vats, but there is virtually no pumping over so as to avoid too tumultuous a fermentation. Grapes are punched down twice a day. Total vatting time is about two weeks after which the juice is left to settle for two days before going to barrel.

Duration And Aging Method: The village Gevrey is aged in a mix of 50% new oak barrels (228L) and 50% one year old oak barrels (228L) for 16-18 months. The barrels are sourced from Francois Frères.50 years old.

title: Domaine Claude Dugat Gevrey Chambertin Premier Cru

paras.text: This is a hedonistic wine built for indulgence and pleasure. The bouquet offers layers of juicy fruit and floral notes, as well as a filigree minerality. On the palate, this wine is silky, generous and vibrant with layers of juicy fruit.

title: Domaine Collotte Bourgogne Blanc

paras.text: Raised 100% in stainless steel tank to retain freshness and precision. This comes substantially from Champ Forey to the east of the village, with a small proportion from En La Caillée, just to the south of the village. Very expressive, fresh and lively with even a hint of exotic fruits, finishing bright and crisp with zesty acidity.

title: Domaine Collotte Bourgogne Pinot Noir Noble Souche

paras.text: Bourgogne “Noble Souché” translates to the “noble vine” from almost 70 year old vines planted in 1947 on Marsannay Cailloux soil from Champforeys. Entirely, de-estemmed, slow fermentation with 5 days of pre-maceration. Aged for 11 months 90% in stainless steel tank, this is a lovely, subtlety rich Côte de Nuits wine.

title: Domaine Collotte Fixin

paras.text: The Fixin is from two parcels of Village Fixin both both with eastern exposition on calcareous clay soil. Aged in oak, 25% new, to round the tannins.

title: Domaine Collotte Marsannay Cuvée Vieilles Vignes

paras.text: The Marsannay Cuvée Vieilles Vignes is assembled from five different terroirs of the appellation: "Combereau", "Favières", " Grasses Têtes ", " Boivin "and "Récilles" on vines of about 50 years old. Completely destemmed, the wine is fermented and aged in tank.

title: Domaine Collotte Marsannay Le Clos de Jeu

paras.text: The Clos de Jeu Marsannay comes from several parcels of 50 year old vines from Clos de Jeu on soft limestone crinoidal soil. Aged in oak, 25% new, this wine is harmonious in its flavors and tannins.

title: Domaine Collotte Marsannay En Combereau

paras.text: The Marsannay Combereau is from the village of Couchey. The 50+ year old vines and shallow soil of crinoidal limestone on bedrock produces very ripe and healthy grapes. Aged in oak, 25% new, to round the tannins. The Combereau Marsannay is a wine with strong and complex aromatics with well-balanced tannin potential.

title: Domaine Collotte Marsannay Les Boivins

paras.text: The Marsannay Boivins is lieu-dit in Marsannay Villages, on vines over 40 years and varying limestone soil. Aged in oak, 25% new, to round the tannins.

title: Domaine Collotte Marsannay Les Champsalomon

paras.text: The Marsannay Champsalomon is from the village of Couchey. The 40+ year old vines on marl soil of the Ostrea Acuminata produces a wine of finesse and minerality with very aromatic fruit and spicy notes. Aged in oak, 25% new, to round the tannins.
A nice fruity nose with lots of raspberry, simple but honest. Mouth is round, fruity, cheerful and pleasant. A good wine to accompany a meal.

title: Domaine Corne-Loup Côtes du Rhône Rouge

paras.text: The wine boasts a dark red ruby color, aromas of red berries, truffles and spices. Complex and rich flavors of red and black fruits with herbal notes coming from the surrounding vegetation (Garrigue).

title: Domaine Courbis Cornas Champelrose

paras.text: 100% Syrah. This cuvée comes from various vineyard parcels across the Courbis domaine, mostly from vines near the base of Cornas slope. They are blended to produce a wine ready for near term drinking upon release. The soils are a combination of only limestone and granite. The Cornas Champelrose benefits from 3 weeks of vatting to extract as much color and flavor as possible. It is aged entirely in casks that are a mix of 25% new; 20% one year; and 55% 2-3 years of age. The barrel-aging period is 12 months, after which the wine is assembled in tank and aged for four more months before bottling. The wine has generous, accessible, pure fruit and shows the full character of its appellation in the attractive Courbis house style.

title: Domaine Courbis Cornas La Sabarotte

paras.text: 100% Syrah. Courbis’ 1.5 hectare Cornas La Sabarotte vineyard is considered to be among the very best sites of the appellation. It has extremely old, low yielding vines; most planted in 1947 but some are even older. The soil is a thin granite-limestone over protruding rocks. The site is perfectly exposed to the south-east. La Sabarotte sees 4 weeks of vatting to extract as much color and flavor as possible. It is aged in 100% new oak casks for 16 months and undergoes its malolactic fermentation in cask. La Sabarotte is Courbis’ most dramatic Cornas, showing saturated black-purple in color with layers of chewy, ripe, sweet fruit with black olive and berry, tar and mineral notes.

title: Domaine Courbis Cornas Les Eygats

paras.text: 100% Syrah. The one hectare, single-vineyard, terraced Cornas Les Eygats site is situated at a relatively high 250 meters of altitude. It has pure, decomposed granite soil and an ideal south-east exposure. The vines are 20 years old. Les Eygats is the last to be harvested. Benefits from 3 weeks of vatting to extract as much color and flavor as possible. It is aged entirely in barriques for 16 months, of which 50% are new and 50% one-year old. A highly concentrated wine, packed with mineral-tinged smoky black fruit that can age for many years but is always inviting when young.

title: Domaine Courbis Crozes Hermitage

paras.text: Typical northern Rhone Syrah notes of smoked meat, iodine, spices, coffee grind, and red and dark fruit.

Tasting Notes: cherry red robe. The bouquet is soft, on red fruits such as raspberry, a little low-key from its bottling. There is a hint of scented flowers, roses. The palate gives bright red fruits with iron in the tannins, drinks well now, with that mineral sense serving it well for that purpose. The length is sound, the aftertaste clear. There is a good spot of intensity in the red fruit. 13°.

title: Domaine Courbis L'Aube IGP Collines Rhodaniennes

paras.text: Tasting Notes: dark red robe, lighter top. The bouquet comes with some reserve, has a smoky, clear black fruited ensemble, the fruit not that prominent as yet. It carries a little mystery, and can emerge rather stylishly. The palate holds enjoyable black berry fruits, with squeezy tannins in step, the finish rounded and complete for this grade of wine. It carries well and clearly into the close. Ideal with steaks, grills, has clear detail. 13°.

title: Domaine Courbis Saint-Joseph

paras.text: 100% Syrah. This cuvée comes from various vineyard parcels across the Courbis domaine, blended to produce a wine ready for near term drinking upon release. The soils are a combination of only limestone and granite. Vinified in temperature controlled stainless steel tanks with 15 days of vatting. Aged in a combination of 20% tanks and 80% barrels (15% new, with the balance 2 to 3 years old). After 10 months, the barrel aged wine is assembled back into tank for a few more months before bottling. The wine has generous, accessible, pure fruit and shows the full character of its appellation in the attractive Courbis house style.

title: Domaine Courbis Saint-Joseph La Cotte Sud

paras.text: La Cotte Sud is from a 1 hectare, south-facing parcel located on the Glun/Châteaubourg border, 500 meters from the Courbis winery. The vineyard is on a steep slope with a granite-sand-stony soil. Laurent and Dominique planted the vines in 1993 with the hope of eventually producing an exceptional St-Joseph wine that parallels their Cornas La Sabarotte. Prior to 2015, the Cotte Sud fruit was blended into the Domaine’s basic St Joseph. The Courbis brothers chose to launch their new cuvee in extraordinary 2015 vintage because the wine attained quality level they aimed for. It was vinified over 4 weeks in stainless steel tanks to extract as much color and flavor as possible. It was then aged in 50% new and one-year-old oak casks for 16 months and underwent its malolactic fermentation in cask. The Cotte Sud is Courbis’ most dramatic St-Joseph wine. 300 cases were made in 2015.

‘Vivid purple. Mineral- and spice-accented aromas of ripe dark berries, licorice and violet on the nose. At once fleshy and energetic, offering juicy blackberry and bitter cherry flavors, and taking on a hint of smokiness and a touch of cola on the back half. Turns sweeter on the nicely persistent finish, which features supple tannins and lingering smoke and floral nuances.” Josh Raynolds in VINOUS.

title: Domaine Courbis Saint-Joseph Les Royes

paras.text: 100% Syrah. The terraced, cliff-like Saint-Joseph Les Royes vineyard is a spectacular “cirque” or extremely steep amphitheater. It is located at the southern limit of the Saint-Joseph appellation, on the border of Cornas. The exposition is to the south-east, so the amphitheater retains the heat of the day, while completely protecting the vines from northerly winds. The soil is a mixture of clay, granite, and limestone (the latter being the source of the small amount of Les Royes Blanc.) Yields are a miniscule 25 hl/ha and the vines average 30 years of age. The Syrah grapes for Les Royes Rouge are given a three week maceration period and fermented in temperature controlled stainless steel tanks. The wine is aged 100% in barrels, of which 1/3 are new; 1/3 one wine and 1/3 two wines. After 12-14 months in cask, the wine is assembled and aged for 3 additional months in tank before bottling. A profound and complex wine with sweet black cherry-raspberry fruit, notes of minerals and smoke, and ripe tannins that give it remarkable structure.

title: Domaine Daniel Bouland Cote De Brouilly Cuvée Melanie

paras.text: Daniel’s parcel lies within the lieu dit Tête Noire, high on the Cote de Brouilly, which like Côte de Py in Morgon, is volcanic blue schist. This terroir gives the wine its distinctive minerality to go with the elegance and structure of Brouilly.

title: Domaine Daniel Bouland Morgon Schiste Bellevue

paras.text: This cuvée of Morgon, Daniel produces from a single parcel in lieu-dit Bellevue where the soil is schist, and like Côte de Py, has a distinctive mineral quality and above all “class” that comes out more and more with age.

title: Domaine Daniel Bouland Morgon Vieilles Vignes Corcelette

paras.text: Daniel’s classic Morgon, vines 60-70 years, with a combination of part of the cuvée being aged in tank and part in 2000 Liter Rousseau foudre. Fine, silky and long, from the sable soil.

title: Domaine Daniel Bouland Morgon Vielles Vignes Delys

paras.text: Daniel Bouland Morgon Les Delys is a gorgeous expression of Gamay from Beaujolais. Daniel Bouland is a great producer of old-fashioned Morgon. From less than 7 hectares of old vines in the Douby, Côte de Py, and Delys, lieux of Morgon, plus small parcels in Chiroubles and Cote de Brouilly, he makes wines that can age 20 years, and are comparable to fine Côte de Nuits Burgundies. His Corcellette Morgon vineyard is 60-75 year-old vines. De Lys (between Corcellette and Ville Morgon) was planted in 1926. In 2014 he acquired another old-vines parcel - Bellevue, on schiste and granite. All his grapes are hand-harvested and vinified with full clusters in order to extract all the organoleptic qualities and bottled unfiltered.
DeLys is sable soil and one of the best situated in the appellation. Daniel’s parcel was planted in 1926 and yields are sometimes as low as 15 hl/ha.

title: Domaine Darviot-Perrin Chassagne Montrachet Rouge Premier Cru Les Bondues

paras.text: Domaine Darviot-Perrin Chassagne Montrachet Rouge Premier Cru Les Bondues | Fine Vines

Location: “Les Bondues” is a small, prestigious, eastern-facing Premier Cru vineyard located just south of Chassagne-Montrachet, 100 yards south of Montrachet. Bondues is a lieu-dit within Chenvottes. The Darviots are the only vignerons to have Pinot Noir in this particular vineyard.
Tasting Notes: Almost garnet in color with a deep rim. The bouquet is full of deep, brooding red fruit with polished wood notes. This is a robust and meaty full-bodied wine.

title: Domaine Darviot-Perrin Meursault Premier Cru Genevrières

paras.text: Tasting Notes: Pale gold color. The bouquet has notes of ripe peach and apricot. On the palate, this wine is broad and rich with huge power, and a long, caramel, and brûléed peach finish.

title: Domaine Darviot-Perrin Meursault Premier Cru Perrières

paras.text: Tasting Notes: Golden with silver tints. A lovely minerality is present in the bouquet; complex, yet refined and discreet. The palate has depth; it has a dense and suave mouth feel with tight acidity; rich and satiny texture.

Location: Aux-Perrières, a property that is shared between Domaine Darviot-Perrin and Coche-Dury. It is a Premier Cru vineyard located in the southern portion of Meursault, at one of the highest elevations of the Cote d’Or

title: Domaine de Cristia Chateauneuf-du-Pape
Domaine de Cristia Chateauneuf-du-Pape Cuvée Rennaissance

paras.text: Ageing: Grenache aged in 2-3 yeard old barrels, Mourvèdre aged in new barrels, for 18 months.

title: Domaine de Cristia Côtes du Rhône
Domaine de Cristia Chateauneuf-du-Pape Vieilles Vignes

paras.text: Age of vines - 85 years old. Ageing - 12 months in 2-3 year-old barrels,then 6 months in concrete vats.

title: Domaine de la Mordorée Chateauneuf Du Pape La Reine des Bois

paras.text: 80% Grenache, 10% Mourvèdre, 5% Syrah, 2.5% Vaccarese, 2.5% Counoise. 60 year-old vines Aged in 50% oak barrels. Deep ruby red color, red fruits aromas leading to leather, black truffles and coffee notes. Fat and concentrated on the palate, with liquorice and dark fruit flavors. Pairs well with game and red meats, cheeses.

title: Domaine de la Charbonnière Chateauneuf du Pape Blanc

paras.text: These grape varieties come from 2 different but complementary terroirs: the sandy soil "Mourre des Perdrix" and the soil "Brusquières"
The picking is entirely by hand, with sorting in the vineyard and again in the cellar.
manual harvest and sorting at the estate by vibrating table, destemming and crushing of the grapes.

Grenaches and Roussanne are aged 75% in stainless steel vats for seven months, with stirring on the lees. The rest is aged in new oak barrels for seven months, with regular batonnages. Clairette stays 100% in stainless steel vats for keeping fruit and freshness.

Tasting Notes: The nose is on fruits with yellow and white flesh, dominated by peach and exotic fruits.A few notes of vanilla and brioche bring an extra touch of fat. The richness of its mouth unfolds and ends with a mineral note.

title: Domaine de la Villaudiere Sancerre

paras.text: Clear wine with pale golden tint. Has smells of citrus fruit. Very crisp wine with a refreshing balance.

title: Domaine de la Mordorée Cotes Du Rhone La Dame Rousse

paras.text: Rosé, slightly orange (mordorée color). Aromas of citrus fruits, straweberry, cherry, floral notes. Palate is very rounded, fresh and long finish.
Pairs well with cold meats and delicatessen, fowl, white meats, grilled lamb with Provence herbs, fish soup, fried fish, pastas, pizzas and all Asian dishes.

title: Domaine de Montorge Montagny Premier Cru Les Quatre Clochers

paras.text: All 12 hectares of Yann Flandre's estate are recognised as Premier Cru vineyards. On these he waits until the last nail-biting minute for grapes to ripen. Once they're pressed, the wine is aged in stainless steel for a year. This brings you some of the tastiest fruit-forward Chardonnay in Burgundy. Its mineral notes of peaches and white flowers are chased by a long, delectable finish.

A relatively complex wine which combines a fruitiness and citrus component with the minerality of the terroir. The mouth feel follows the nose flavors with a certain power and gourmet feeling. Excellent finish and length!

title: Domaine de Piaugier Côtes du Rhône La Grange de Piaugier
Domaine de Piaugier Côtes du Rhône Villages Sablet

paras.text: Vinification: Destemming, 3 weeks in tank, aged partly in concrete tanks, partly in four season-old oak barriques. Bottled without filtering.

title: Domaine de Piaugier Côtes du Rhône Villages Sablet Les Briguieres

paras.text: Soil: Clay with limestone and sand Varieties: Grenache, Mourvedre Yield: 40 hl/ha Age of Vines: 45 years Harvest: manual Vinification: Destemmed, one month in tank, aged in one to four season old oak barriques for two winters. Bottled without filtering.

title: Domaine de Piaugier Gigondas

paras.text: Soil: Clay with limestone and sand Varieties: Grenache, Mourvedre, Syrah Yield: 35 hl/ha Age of Vines: 40 years Harvest: Manual Vinification: Picked in whole bunches, 1 month in tank, 70% aged in concrete tanks, 20% in one season old oak barriques and 10% in new oak barriques. Bottled without filtering.

title: Domaine de Pouy Côtes De Gascogne IGP

paras.text: To prevent oxidation, grapes are taken directly from the vines to the vats in isothermal tanks protected by a layer of inert gas. Grapes are then poured into one of eight 50-ton pneumatic temperature controlled presses, followed by skin contact maceration at 15°C / 59°F for 8 to 12 hours before being gently pressed. Stainless steel fermented. The must is then transferred to underground cold storage vats and kept at 5°C / 41°F for three to five days. Dry ice and refrigerated vats are used to slow fermentation and storage at –4°C year round ensures freshness. Bottled to order.

title: Domaine Denis Bachelet Bourgogne Aligoté

paras.text: Vinification: Direct pressing, light settling of lees, fermentation and aged in barrel (20% new oak).

title: Domaine Denis Bachelet Bourgogne Pinot Noir

paras.text: Terroir: Two lieux-dits: Pressonier and Grand Champs. Limestone and clay soils, facing southeast
Vinification: 100% de-stemmed and crushed, indigenous yeast fermentation. Aged for 16-18 months in barrel (no new oak).

title: Domaine Denis Bachelet Charmes-Chambertin Grand Cru Vieilles Vignes

paras.text: Vinification: 100% de-stemmed, indigenous yeast fermentation. Aged for 16-18 months in barrel (30-60% new oak).

title: Domaine Denis Bachelet Gevrey-Chambertin Les Évocelles Vieilles Vignes

paras.text: Domaine Denis Bachelet Gevrey-Chambertin Les Évocelles Vieilles Vignes | Fine Vines
Vinification: 100% de-stemmed, crushed, indigenous yeast fermentation, extraction by punch-downs. Aged for 16 months in barrel (60% new oak).

title: Domaine Denis Bachelet Gevrey-Chambertin Premier Cru Les Corbeaux Vieilles Vignes

paras.text: Domaine Denis Bachelet Gevrey-Chambertin Premier Cru Les Corbeaux Vieilles Vignes | Fine Vines
Domaine Denis Bachelet Gevrey-Chambertin Premier Cru Les Corbeaux Vieilles Vignes
Domaine Denis Bachelet Gevrey-Chambertin Premier Cru Les Corbeaux Vieilles Vignes
Vinification: 100% de-stemmed, crushed, punch-downs, indigenous yeast fermentation. Aged in barrel (50% new oak).

title: Domaine Denis Bachelet Gevrey-Chambertin Vieilles Vignes

paras.text: Terroir: Two lieux-dits: Pressonier and Grand Champs. Limestone and clay soils, facing southeast
Vinification: 100% de-stemmed and crushed, indigenous yeast fermentation. Aged for 16-18 months in barrel (no new oak).

title: Domaine des Cassagnoles Cotes de Gascogne

paras.text: Dry white wine, fruity, lively with a good finish. Balanced and harmonious. Finale sweet.

Each grape variety is vinified separately. Small skin maceration for the Colombard and the Gros Manseng. Pneumatic pressing, cold stabilization, fermentation under controlled temperature of 18°C. Aged in tank until bottling. Crispy and zesty wine, very pleasant, especially enjoyed with tarts and cakes either salty or sweet, with seafoods, grilled fishes, some cheese.
Age of Vines: 30 years average Grape Variety: 45% Ugni Blanc, 34% Colombard, 15% Chardonnay, 6% Gros Manseng
Vinification: Each variety is harvested and vinified separately with assembly in February/March. Picking off at harvest - Skin Contact- Pneumatic pressing

title: Domaine des Cassagnoles Gros Manseng

paras.text: The Gros Manseng produces fleshier, more ample wines with fruity apricot and pear aromas. It is a lively wine, but not to excess, with a persistent final. It may be kept for several years and should be drunk chilled, at a temperature of 10/12°. " Gros Manseng Sélection " is a dry wine, and the perfect accompaniment to cooked fish. "Gros Manseng Medium" is a semi-dry wine that is perfect as an aperitif or with foie gras. It may be kept for between 5 and 6 years. Our Sweet Gros Manseng is only produced during exceptional harvests. It is a very elegant wine that may be kept for between 10 to 15 years. The 2003 vintage received a Silver medal at the 'Concours Général Agricole' held in Paris, in 2004, and was elected 'Cépage d'Or' in the same year. The "Gros Manseng matured in oak casks" is a powerful wine with vanilla aromas, which develop over time. It is a vin de garde (wine for ageing), but which may also be drunk young with blue-veined cheese or spicy cuisine.

title: Domaine des Comtes Lafon Meursault

paras.text: Terroir: Blend of older vines (En La Barre, En Luraules, Les Crotots, Clos de la Baronnne) and younger vines (1
Vinification: Whole-cluster pressing, indigenous yeast fermentation in barrel, racked after malolactic. Aged for 18-22 months on fine lees, blending in tank, light fining if necessary.
Combined replantation method, with a blend of massal selection and clonal selection (at least 5 different types). Pruning is mostly Guyot, with some Cordon Royat.

title: Domaine des Comtes Lafon Meursault Clos De La Barre

paras.text: Vinification: Whole-cluster pressing, indigenous yeast fermentation in barrel, racking after malolactic. Aged for 18-20 months, blending in tank, light fining if necessary.

title: Domaine des Comtes Lafon Meursault Désirée

paras.text: Terroir: Parcel known as les Petures (or Plures), east-facing, minimal slope, thick red clay soil.
Vinification: Whole-cluster pressing, indigenous yeast fermentation in barrel, acking after malolactic. Aged for 18-22 months, blending in tank, light fining if necessary.

In the vineyards, the rootstock is a mix of massal (60%) and clonal (40%) selection. This terroir is perfect for Pinot Noir, which explains why most of the neighboring parcels are planted with that variety. However, this is a Chardonnay, making it a rare find.

The name for this cuvée, Désirée, comes from an old cadastral (land registry) appellation which was eliminated in 1973. The domaine is legally allowed to use this name on their labels thanks to precedence: they have been labeling wine from this parcel under the name Désirée since the late 1800s.

title: Domaine des Comtes Lafon Meursault Premier Cru Charmes

paras.text: Vine Age: Half a hectare planted in the 1920s, half a hectare in the mid-1990s, 0.07 in the 1960s
Terroir: Charmes du Dessus, facing east, minimal slope, deep clay-limestone soil with crumbly rocky subsoil.
Vinification: Pneumatic press, indigenous yeast fermentation. Aged for 18-22 months in older oak, fining if necessary.
In the vineyards, the rootstock is a mix of massal and clonal selection. Total yields are between 40 and 50 hectoliters per hectare, depending on the vintage.

title: Domaine des Comtes Lafon Meursault Premier Cru Genevrières
Domaine des Comtes Lafon Meursault Premier Cru Goutte d’Or

paras.text: Vinification: Whole-cluster pressing, indigenous yeast alcoholic fermentation. Racked after malolactic. Aged for 18-22 months on fine lees, blended in tank, fining if necessary.

This is a small parcel with generous yields and a high proportion of old vines. The team uses a combined replantation method, with a blend of massal selection and clonal selection (at least 5 different types). Pruning is mostly Guyot, with some Cordon Royat. Rootstock is 161-49.

title: Domaine des Comtes Lafon Meursault Premier Cru Perrières

paras.text: Terroir: 4 parcels, 10-16% slope, , facing east/southeast, shallow white limestone and marl soil on crumbly limestone subsoil
Vinification: Pneumatic pressing, indigenous yeast fermentation. Aged for 18-22 months in older oak, fined if necessary.

Cru: Les Perrières Dessous and Perrières Ginette. In the vineyards, a mix of massal and clonal selection is used. The older vines have a more irregular yield from year to year, but yields generally average around 30-45 hl/ hectare.

title: Domaine des Comtes Lafon Montrachet Grand Cru

paras.text: 3 hours' gentle pneumatic pressing, 24 hours' cold-settling, indigenous yeast fermentation. 18-22 months' aging, fining if necessary.

In the vineyard, the rootstock is entirely massal selection. These vines are fairly weak, and were severely attacked by the court-noué virus. The change to biodynamic agriculture has improved vine health overall, though yields are still low: 20-35 hl/ha on average.

title: Domaine des Comtes Lafon Volnay Premier Cru Champans

paras.text: Terroir: En Champans, facing east, gentle (2%-5%) slope, deeper crumbly limestone soil with little rocks

Vinification: 100% de-stemmed, cold (12-15°C) settling, indigenous yeast fermentation in temperature-controlled stainless steel tanks, punch-downs 1-2 times per day. Aged for 18-22 months in barrel (33% new).

The well-draining soil in this vineyard is home to the domaine's oldest vines. Their rootstock is a majority massal selection, with a mix of massal selection and clones for the newer plantings from 1989. This terroir is very precocious and regularly produces very mature grapes, creating dense but less tannic wines than those of Santenots.

When the grapes arrive to the cellar, the goal of the winemaker is keep some of the benefits of whole cluster fermentation but avoid the herbacious flavors that come from the stems. The clusters are thus de-stemmed with the most delicate machine possible in order to keep a maximum of whole grapes. After pressing, the young wine settles for 1 to 2 weeks in tank, separating the sediment of solids from the liquids to avoid unwanted lees during aging. The barrels are then filled by gravity and undergo a late malolactic fermentation. The wine is racked twice during aging.

title: Domaine des Comtes Lafon Volnay Premier Cru Clos des Chênes

paras.text: Terroir: Higher altitude, gentle (2-5%) slope, facing east, medium-deep light-colored clay soil with softer limestone rocks

Vinification: 100% de-stemmed, indigenous yeast fermentation in temperature-controlled stainless steel tanks. Cold (12-15°C) settling, punch-downs 1-2 times per day. Aged for 18-22 months in barrel (33% new).

This tiny parcel is perfectly situated, overlooking the Caillerets. The vines here are healthy, though they are not rigorous producers (25-40 hl/ha). The rootstock is entirely massal selection, and the grapes ripen later here compared to other parcels owned by the domaine.

When the grapes arrive to the cellar, the goal of the winemaker is keep some of the benefits of whole cluster fermentation but avoid the herbacious flavors that come from the stems. The clusters are thus de-stemmed but with the most delicate machine possible in order to keep a maximum of whole grapes. After pressing, the young wine settles for 1 to 2 weeks in tank, separating the sediment of solids from the liquids to avoid unwanted lees during aging. The barrels are then filled by gravity and undergo a late malolactic fermentation. The wine is racked twice during aging.

title: Domaine des Comtes Lafon Volnay Premier Cru Santenots-du-Milieu

paras.text: Terroir: East-facing, shallow red clay soil, hard limestone substrate: a sunny, early-ripening site

Vinification: 100% de-stemmed, cooled (12-15°C), 4-6 days' whole-grape maceration, 10 days' indigenous yeast fermentation in stainless steel tanks, 1-2 punch-downs per day. 1-2 weeks' settling in tank, gravity transfer to oak barrel (1/3 new). Racking, 18-22 months' aging on fine lees in same barrels, blending in tank.

Cru Santenots-du-Milieu is about 8 hectares in total surface area, meaning this domaine owns almost half of the appellation. Their parcel has a high proportion of old vines. When replanting they use a combined method, with a blend of massal selection and clonal selection (at least 5 different types). Pruning is mostly Guyot, with some Cordon Royat.

title: Domaine Des Corbillières Touraine Rose

paras.text: 70% Pinot Noir 30% Pineau d'Aunis, Direct press rosé fermented in stainless steel. Medium salmon in color, with fresh roses, red berry fruit and fresh herbs on the nose. It is crisp on the attack, showing very good density of fruit on the palate, yet it’s delicate and very well balanced and has a long finish.This is a nice aperitif wine, it will pair well with summer fares such as salads, seafood and other light dishes.

title: Domaine Des Corbillières Touraine Rouge Les Demoiselles

paras.text: Fabel Barbou purchased Domaine des Corbillières in 1923. Now run by his great-grandson, Dominique and his wife, Véronique, they produce some of our favorite red, white, and rosé wines. For the Les Demoiselles red they blend Pinot Noir, Cabernet Franc, and Côt (Malbec). The result is a delight. It’s a great red for an herb crusted pork roast.

title: Domaine Des Corbillières Touraine Sauvignon Blanc

paras.text: The show opens with a fresh, lively perfume of citrus and green apple, gently seasoned by hints of Sancerre-like minerality. On the palate, one is greeted with a rush of zesty, melony Sauvignon Blanc; the characteristic plumpness provides mouthfilling, pleasing fruit and weight. On the finish, zesty acidity gives the wine brilliance, freshness and lift. An inspired choice for weddings and other celebrations, this is also an ideal house white for all occasions. Pair this versatile Sauvignon Blanc with fresh prawns, salmon, pasta salad, grilled chicken, or cut veggies.

title: Domaine des Croix Beaune Premier Cru Les Bressandes

paras.text: Vinification: 100% de-stemmed, indigenous yeast fermentation in uncovered wooden tanks. Aged for 15 months in older oak barrels, a few months blending in tank.

title: Domaine des Croix Beaune Premier Cru Les Cents Vignes

paras.text: Terroir: Different parcels in large lieu-dit: upper slope has brown gravelly-clay soil (
Vinification: 15% whole-cluster, indigenous yeast fermentation in uncovered wooden tanks. Aged for 16 months in older oak barrels, a few months blending in tank.

title: Domaine des Croix Beaune Premier Cru Les Grèves

paras.text: Vinification: 25% whole-cluster, pneumatic pressing, indigenous yeast fermentation in uncovered wooden tanks. Aged for 16 months in mostly older barrels, a few months blending in tank.

title: Domaine des Croix Beaune Premier Cru Les Pertuisots

paras.text: Terroir: 2 parcels with brown clay soils (40-50cm deep), Jurassic limestone bedrock
Vinification: 20% whole-cluster, indigenous yeast fermentation in uncovered wooden vats. Aged for 16 months oak barrel (1/6 new oak), a few months blending in tank.

title: Domaine des Croix Beaune Rouge

paras.text: Vinification: 15% whole-cluster pressing by pneumatic press, indigenous yeast fermentation in uncovered wooden tanks. Aged for 16 months in older oak barrels, a few months blending in tank.

This wine is sourced from Blanches Fleurs (a well-draining and early-ripening site), Blanchisserie (shallow soils), Beaune 1er Cru les Teurons (redder clay soils of oxidized iron with limestone rocks), and Pointes de Tuvilain (marl and clay soils).

title: Domaine des Croix Bourgogne Pinot Noir

paras.text: Cherry-red in color, this Pinot Noir's nose is full of ripe, soft fruit and hints of mineral. Smooth palate, the creamy fruit help the finish. A modern styled wine that is comparable to a premier cru or maybe even a Grand Cru.
Vinification: 100% de-stemmed, pneumatic press, indigenous yeast fermentation in uncovered wooden tanks. Aged for 16 months in older oak barrels, then a few months blending in tank.

title: Domaine des Croix Corton Charlemagne Grand Cru

paras.text: Vinification: Whole-cluster pressing, indigenous yeast fermentation. Aged for 12 months in barrel (15-20% new oak).

title: Domaine des Croix Corton La Vigne au Saint Grand Cru

paras.text: Vinification: 40% whole-cluster, pneumatic pressing, indigenous yeast fermentation in uncovered wooden tanks. Aged for 16 months in barrel (up to 33% new oak), a few months blending in tank.

title: Domaine Des Lambrays Clos des Lambrays Grand Cru

paras.text: Terrain: Undulating facing east/southeast, 250m to 370m above sea level, divided into three distinct lieu-dits
Harvesting: Brouin favours fruit freshness, so the Clos is one of the earliest to harvest
Vinification: Usually with 100% stems included, although in some vintages a percentage of destemmed grapes

title: Domaine Drouhin-Laroze Bonnes Mares Grand Cru

paras.text: The name of this climat derives from an unearthed bas-relief portraying a trinity of Roman goddesses. We know that in Roman times the cult of this trinity, protectors of the harvests, was widespread.
Our 1.5 hectare Bonnes Mares parcel is situated exclusively on the Chambolle-Musigny side on shallow, clay and ferruginous red soil.

The Domaine's Grands Crus are matured in oak barrels (80% new barrels) made from wood from the Allier and Nivernais regions. We favour light to medium-plus toasts as this ensures the perfect harmony between the wine and wood tannins.

The eye is immediately caught by the vermilion hue. The first nose conveys discrete hints of blackcurrant bud and flowers. Spices and small red fruit aromas appear on the palate on aeration with liquorice contributing character. The sweet flavour of rose provides subtlety and style. The overall harmony ensures depth and results in a dense, superb and peerlessly elegant wine.
Matching food: Duck breast fillet stuffed with foie gras, deer fillet with mustard, sweet potatoes, roasted Bresse chicken.

title: Domaine Drouhin-Laroze Chambertin-Clos de Bèze Grand Cru

paras.text: This parcel belonged to the monks of the Bèze abbey and vines were planted here as early as 630 AD.
It is referred to as the "King of Wines" and Camille Rodier noted that this one wine contained the qualities of all Great Burgundy.

The Grands Crus are matured in oak barrels (80% new barrels) made from wood from the Allier and Nivernais region. We favour light to medium-plus toasts as this ensures the perfect harmony between the wine and wood tannins.

The Chambertin Clos De Bèze has an intense purple colour with a fragrance of small red fruits and liquorice on the nose providing strong aromatic majestic quality. On the palate the attack is balanced, clear, sound and rich. Its melted, spicy and precise tannins offer roundness and lightness on the finish. With a hint of rose, this elegant wine suggests its sensuality. A wine to be laid down.

title: Domaine Drouhin-Laroze Chambolle-Musigny

paras.text: The name Chambolle comes from the French word describing the aspect of the foaming Grône stream in the wake of storm showers. Original name: "Campus Ebullien" (bubbling field).

This village appellation is obtained from two lieux-dits: Les Baudes in Premier Cru appellation directly below Bonnes Mares - surface area 0.18 hectares - and Les Véroilles in Villages appellation situated immediately above Bonnes Mares - surface area 0.04 hectares. These two parcels were planted in 2000 and 1981 respectively.

The Chambolle-Musigny is matured in 20% new oak barrels and barrels previously used for one wine made from wood from the Allier and Nivernais regions. We favour light to medium-plus toasts as this ensures the perfect harmony between the wine and wood tannins. With a sustained ruby colour, it is deemed a feminine wine by virtue of its subtlety and elegance. A very fine floral fragrance on the nose characterises its aromatic refinement. Very expressive and typical, it combines a vigorous and warm body. Its suave texture and fruity aromas complete its length and leave us with a liquorice finish.

title: Domaine Drouhin-Laroze Chapelle-Chambertin Grand Cru

paras.text: The monks from Bèze first built a chapel here in 1155. Virtually in ruins, the wine growers undertook its rebuilding in 1457. In 1830 it was razed to the ground. The older generations called it the "grande chapelle" or the "haute chapelle".
The Chapelle-Chambertin appellation is situated at the foot of Chambertin-Clos de Bèze. Our parcel represents 0.52 hectare and one half was planted in 1973 and the other half in 1986.

The Domaine's Grands Crus are matured in oak barrels (80% new barrels) made from wood from the Allier and Nivernais regions. We favour light to medium-plus toasts as this ensures the perfect harmony between the wine and wood tannins.

Limpid and brilliant, the Domaine's Chapelle-Chambertin has a woody vanilla nose with a slight floral touch. On the palate, its controlled and subtle tannins ensure elegance, subtlety and a majestic quality and its aromatic subtlety suggests fruit, spices and wood. Its pure features convey plenty of style. The tannins are tender and supple. However, we are brought back to order by its complexity and mineral liveliness on the finish.

title: Domaine Drouhin-Laroze Clos de Vougeot Grand Cru

paras.text: Our one hectare parcel is situated in the area of Clos de Vougeot called "des Papes" and, more especially, in the "Plante l'Abbé" and "Quartier de Marei Haut" lieux-dits. The produce from this upper third section of the Clos de Vougeot was reserved for the Popes in Avignon.

Our Clos de Vougeot parcel is situated in the "Plante l'Abbé" and "Quartier de Marei Haut" lieux-dits in the most westerly section of the Clos de Vougeot. Separated by a path, these two parcels have a total surface area of 1 hectare and were planted in 1976, 1989 and 2007.

The Domaine's Grands Crus are matured in oak barrels (80% new barrels) made from wood from the Allier and Nivernais regions. We favour light to medium-plus toasts as this ensures the perfect harmony between the wine and wood tannins.

When young, it is characterised by its raspberry red to deep garnet colour. Its full-bodied bouquet is reminiscent of black fruit, liquorice, spices, with woody and leather hints. On the palate, melted wood slightly dominates aromas of black fruit, truffle, anise and cherry. The intense, powerful and precise tannins of this Grand Cru accompany a long, unctuous finish.

title: Domaine Drouhin-Laroze Gevrey-Chambertin

paras.text: There are several possible explanations regarding the origin of the name Gevrey: is it derived from the Gallic "Gibriacus" or from the combe de Lavaut, "Gaba" in Latin meaning "gorge".
Surface area: 330 hectares of which 51 hectares extend into the village of Brochon

We have 8 Gevrey-Chambertin parcels situated in the following lieux-dits: En Combe, En Champs, En Vignes Belles, Croix des Champs, En Jouise, En Pallud, Aux Mairchais and Aux Epointures. The surface area of our Gevrey-Chambertin parcels amounts to 4 hectares.
Our Gevrey-Chambertin is matured in oak barrels previously used for one wine made from wood from the Allier and Nivernais regions, with medium to medium-plus toasts.

With a fine colour and visual aspect and good texture, on the palate the Gevrey-Chambertin leaves a sensation of freshness with a delicate body and slight woody hints. Its tannins are melted in a tender and silky texture that highlight its aromatic refinement and subtlety.

title: Domaine Drouhin-Laroze Gevrey-Chambertin Premier Cru Au Closeau

paras.text: From "Clou", which, in Burgundy, is synonymous with "Clos" and is a reminder that this parcel was enclosed by a wall.
Our parcel Au Closeau, planted in 1943, measures 0.44 ha, or 80% of the parcel's total surface - almost a monopoly for the Domaine.
Au Closeau is located at the southern end of Gevrey Chambertin, across from Mazis-Chambertin.

The Gevrey-Chambertin 1ers Crus are matured 40% in new oak, the balance made up of casks that have undergone one vinification. Their oak comes from the Allier and the Nivernais. We favour a light to "medium plus" toast to obtain perfect harmony between the wine and oak's tannins.

This wine is a deep ruby with a delicious nose including red and black fruit and mixed spices. The blend on the palate of more cherry, vanilla and raspberry aromas, brings freshness to this round, fleshy and silky texture. The delicacy of these aromas and the fruit on the finish make this a very charming appellation.
Matching food: Grilled red meat, roast pork, mild cheeses like Cîteaux Brillat-Savarin

title: Domaine Drouhin-Laroze Gevrey-Chambertin Premier Cru Clos Prieur

paras.text: This parcel was originally the property of the monks of Cluny Abbey (Prieuré de Cluny).
Having Premier Cru status, it is situated South of the Village and its close neighbours are Mazis-Chambertin to the West and Chapelle-Chambertin to the South.
Our Clos Prieur parcel is 0.30 hectare and was planted in 1954 with a section replaced in 2003.

The Gevrey-Chambertin Premiers Crus are matured in 40% new oak barrels and barrels previously used for one wine made from wood from the Allier and Nivernais regions. We favour light to medium-plus toasts as this ensures the perfect harmony between the wine and wood tannins.

Its deep and lively cherry red colour reflects the predominance of mostly black and stewed fruit. Its consistent and tender tannins convey sweetness to the palate. Aromas of peppery vanilla and Morello cherry are present. This is a precise wine that offers a silky finish.

title: Domaine Drouhin-Laroze Gevrey-Chambertin Premier Cru Lavaut Saint Jacques

paras.text: Domaine Drouhin-Laroze Gevrey-Chambertin Premier Cru Lavaut Saint Jacques | Fine Vines
Situated in the part north of the village, just before the Combe of the same name. The appellation is very often written as "Lavaux"; however, the AOC is officially registered as "Lavaut".
Situated north of the village, at the entrance to the Combe, our parcel covers 0.30 hectare and was planted in 1943.

The Gevrey-Chambertin Premiers Crus are matured in 40% new oak barrels and barrels previously used for one wine made from wood from the Allier and Nivernais regions. We favour light to medium-plus toasts as this ensures the perfect harmony between the wine and wood tannins.

Lavaut Saint Jacques has aromas of red fruit and violet. The palate is sound, lively and fruity from morello, conveying delicacy and gourmandise. A discrete woody nose suggests elegance while the tannic structure reveals the majestic quality. Good length on the palate.

title: Domaine Drouhin-Laroze Latricières-Chambertin Grand Cru

paras.text: In the Middle Ages this climat produced such good quality wines that is was called the "Petite Merveille" (tiny wonder). "Latricières" is derived from "La tricière" which in old Burgundian dialect refers to land that is unfit to farm, land that has barely any value at all.

The Domaine's Grands Crus are matured in oak barrels (80% new barrels) made from wood from the Allier and Nivernais regions. We favour light to medium-plus toasts as this ensures the perfect harmony between the wine and wood tannins.

With a dark ruby colour, Latricières-Chambertin is virile and powerful. This is already clear on the nose, with the intensity and subtlety of the fragrances of black fruit (blackberry and blueberry), liquorice and spices. On the palate the attack provides great aromatic complexity and is concentrated, massive and solid. The wine remains elegant and its delicious tannins are seductive. With round substance and good length, it is said to be "masculine and very balanced".
Matching food: Ravioles with mushrooms and foie gras, duck breast fillet with morels.

title: Domaine Drouhin-Laroze Morey-Saint-Denis Très Girard

paras.text: The name Morey probably comes from a snout-shaped hill standing to the south-east and called "Moure" in pre-Latin.
With less than 100 hectares, it is one of the smallest Côte de Nuits appellations.
Planted in 1946, our 0.18 hectare parcel of Morey-St-Denis is situated in the top part of the "En Très Girard" lieu-dit.

This appellation is matured in new oak barrels and barrels previously used for one wine made from wood from the Allier and Nivernais regions. We favour light to medium-plus toasts as this ensures the perfect harmony between the wine and wood tannins.

Its colour is deep garnet with purplish glints when this appellation is young. The bouquet, with black fruit, blackcurrant, blueberry, red stone fruit and a touch of vanilla, gives way to a fleshed vinous body presenting fruity, melted tannins and a harmonious woody nose. Morey-Saint-Denis offers a pleasant style that balances body strength and the expression of the fruit.

title: Domaine Drouhin-Laroze Musigny Grand Cru

paras.text: Musigny most likely derives its name from "Musinus", the name of the owner of a Gallo-Roman villa in this place.
This Grand Cru is matured in 100% new oak barrels with personalised toasts made from a selection of the finest woods from the forests in the Allier and Nivernais regions.

The colour of the Musigny is a delicate and deep magenta purple with wild rose, violet, blackcurrant and raspberry on the nose. With age come odours of leather and cherry spirit. Its almost caramelized grapes and aromas of open flowers embalm the palate with a texture of voluptuous taffetas. Its length leads us towards the endless complexity of its aromas.

"It may not possess the powerful splendour of a Chambertin or the silky and meaty calibre of a Romanée, but what sumptuous colour, what exceptional elegance, what richness of body and bouquet with blackcurrant, wild rose and raspberry fragrances." Camille Rodier.
Matching food: Semi-cooked foie gras terrine with roasted figs, scrambled eggs forest, burgundy trout, duck aiguillette with orange

title: Domaine du Clos de Tart Mommessin Clos De Tart

paras.text: Beautiful savoury notes with lovely bright red fruit too and spicy nuances, silky on the palate with a long spicy finish. Extremely elegant. 94/100 - 2018-2028 (Gerard Basset - Decanter - January 2015) Deep red-ruby. Expressive aromas of black raspberry, spices, stone and pepper. Lush and ripe but with excellent sappy energy to the flavors of dark berries, licorice, flowers and curry powder. Very dense and sweet for the year without being heavy or over the top. Most impressive today on the very long, vibrant finish, which features broad, fine-grained tannins and lovely rising perfume. The thicker 2012 may surpass this wine in the long run, but I have a weakness for Clos de Tart in cooler vintages. 93-95 - 2023-2038 (Vinous International Wine Cellar - Stephen Tanzer - Antonio Galloni - January 2015) This is Sylvain Pitiot's last vintage in charge at Clos de Tart but he has gone out on a high. I only tasted an approximation of the final blend - there are six "building blocks" - but it's a powerful, concentrated, comparatively late picked red, with quite a bit of oak, firmish tannins, dark fruits, some sap and sweetness and the concentration to age. 94 - 2020-30 (Tim Atkin - Burgundy 2013 Special Report - February 2015)

title: Domaine du Clos de Tart Mommessin Morey St Denis Premier Cru La Forge De Tart

paras.text: Domaine du Clos de Tart Mommessin Morey St Denis Premier Cru La Forge De Tart | Fine Vines

The La Forge de Tart expresses the same characteristics as the Clos de Tart with undoubtedly less complexity but a fierier and more straightforward style. The fruit displays the typical aromas of young vines. The palate exhales a ‘juicy' and lively character that makes this wine very attractive. (Jacques Devauges - Clos de Tart)

Here are the main features of this wine : Vines age : less than 25 years old Full flowering : 4th of June Harvest : September 17th Yield : 31 hl/ha Average alcohol content : 13.3% volume Average pH : 3.54 Malo-lactic fermentation : June 2015 Aging : 17 months in new oak barrels Bottling : end of March 2016

title: Domaine Edmond Vatan Sancerre Clos La Néore

paras.text: The Domaine Edmond Vatan is located in the small village of Chavignol in the county of Cher. The domaine produces « le Clos de la Néore », probably the most sought-after wine in Sancerre appellation… and also the most confidential ! Only 4.000 bottles are produced per year, to be relativized depending on climatic conditions to which the domaine is deeply attached. That is to say that being lucky enough to get a taste of these crus is all about privilege. You will furthermore find very few info on the Domaine Edmond Vatan : confidential, we said. Confidential and also singular. The vines are planted on kimmeridge, a stratigraphic subsoil dating back from Late Jurassic ! This clay-limestone soil rich in sea-shells fossils provides a mineral salinity on the finale. A singularity that’s been well leveraged by the Vatan family.

One hectare. No more and no less. One facing south parcel located at Monts Damnés. An outstanding terroir through the incomparable richness of its soil : conditions are optimal and allow the Sauvignon to remarkably be developed. It’s indeed an understatement to say that the Vatan family has one true high-end know-how. Edmond first, who paved the way for a virtuosity that never left the family business. Then came Anne, the daughter, yet archeologist until 2008. She was not allowed to prune back in the days and now she’s in charge of the production. The result is exactly the same : elegant and gorgeous wines. A more than honorable result for Anne who admits she

title: Domaine Emmanuel Darnaud Crozes Hermitage Les Trois Chenes

paras.text: Location : Northern Côtes du Rhône, on the east bank of the Rhone river. The climate is continental with a Mediterranean influence.

Vinification : The grapes are harvested by hand, destemmed, then cold macerated and fermented in open concrete vats with regular temperature control. During this period, the winemaker treads, punches and pumps over several times.
Type of ageing : The wine is divided (35% in new barrels, 35% in one-year barrels, the rest in 2-3-year barrels) and left to mature for 13 months.

Tasting note : Deep gleaming ruby red. A lovely aromatic complexity with cherry and violet, ending on notes of mocha and spices. The mouth brings out fine, silky lingering tannins. This is a wine with elegance, fineness and delicacy.

title: Domaine Emmanuel Darnaud Crozes Hermitage Mise En Bouche

paras.text: A perfect bistro wine, this fruity syrah is comes from younger vines than the "les trois chenes". It has hints of dark berry fruits similar to the "les trois chenes" and the palate is just as wonderful.

title: Domaine François Lamarche Clos Vougeot Grand Cru

paras.text: Vinification: Hand picked, 80 to 100% de-stemmed depending on the vintage. Vatting period of about 15 to 18 days, in open oak vats at a low temperature (controlled by thermo-regulation).
Maturation: In oak casks for between 16 and 20 months (between 60 and 100% new oak depending on the vintage). Bottled with no fining and no filtering.
Aging in Bottles: Depending on your personal tastes and the vintage, between 6 and 30 years.

title: Domaine Grand Veneur Chateauneuf-du-Pape Rouge Le Miocene

paras.text: The wine is produced from vineyards located in the northern part of Châteauneuf du Pape and the vines are grown using organic methods. This cuvee will express year after year a great power and aromatic complexity.

An intense dark-ruby color. The nose develops aromas of ripe black fruits (such as blackberry), cherry and spice box. The palate reveals strong yet elegant tannins. The finish is long and luxurious. This is the Chateauneuf du Pape expression, displaying all the characteristics of the terroir.
Vinification: Harvest is sorted by hand, destemmed and crushed. Fermentation temperature is controlled at 30°C.

title: Domaine Grand Veneur Chateauneuf-du-Pape Rouge Les Origines

paras.text: Deep and brilliant, purple-red colour. An exciting nose with aromas of black fruit (blackcurrant, cherry) spices and vanilla. This great aromatic complexity is found on the palate: the spices and ripe fruit appear with an elegant woodiness and harmonious tannins. The finish has good aromatic length and introduces a touch of liquorice and pepper.
Vinification: Harvest is sorted by hand, destemmed and crushed. Fermentation temperature is controlled at 30°C.
Vatting period of 18 to 20 days. Matured in vats (grenache) and in oak casks (syrah and mourvèdre).

title: Domaine Grand Veneur Cotes du Rhone Blanc Reserve

paras.text: Aromas of flowers and stone fruit. Fruits dominate on the palate with touches of almond and white peach. A slight liveliness appears on the finish, which creates a perfect balance.
Varietals: 40% Viognier, 50% Roussanne, 10% Clairette (2018) / 30% Roussanne, 30% Grenache Blanc, 20% Clairette and 20% Viognier (2019)

title: Domaine Grand Veneur Cotes Du Rhone Reserve

paras.text: The Côtes du Rhône is made from various type of soils, but it mostly comes from limestone terraces with sand and red clay. This give to the “Reserve” an extraordinary richness and complexity with a mediteranean style.
Traditional wine making and ageing is performed in vats only. Bottling after 10-12 months.

The colour is purple-tinged garnet.The aromatic range of the nose goes from fresh berries (wild raspberry, blackcurrant, blackberry) to spices.The palate is big and full-flavoured, with silky-smooth tannins and aromas of the fruit already mentioned. The finish introduces touches of liquorice and pepper. A Côtes du Rhône with great complexity for an every day drinking.

title: Domaine Grand Veneur Cotes du Rhone Rosé Reserve

paras.text: Salmon-pink color, clear and brilliant. The nose is fruity and spicy, reminiscent of wild strawberry and fine Provencal spices. The palate is full, well-balanced and fruity, with a long, fresh finish. A beautiful and delicate rosé.
Varietals: 70% Grenache, 20% Syrah, 10% Mourvedre (2018) / 50% Grenache Noir, 25% Cinsault, 20% Syrah and 5% Mourvedre (2019)
Vinification: A part is drawn off the skins with short maceration and the other part is from direct press. Fermentation in stainless steel at cool temperature. Bottling 5 months after harvest.

title: Domaine Grand Veneur Cotes Du Rhone Villages Les Champauvins

paras.text: Intense, brilliant garnet-red color. It reveals lovely fruit, loads of body and a heady bouquet of ground peppers, raspberries cherry liqueur, currants, and spice box. Full-bodied and dense, it tastes more like a "baby Chateauneuf" than a Cotes du Rhone. Goes very well with grilled meat or vegetable. It is also delicious with cheese, such as camembert, brie and gouda.

title: Domaine Grand Veneur Lirac Clos De Sixte

paras.text: An intense red garnet color. On the nose, aromas of red and black ripe fruit (kirsch and wild blackberry). The mouth is full, with aromas of blackcurrant liqueur and spice. Tannins are both harmonious and elegant thanks to the fleshiness of the wine. Hints of licorice and vanilla on the finish, which gives the wine length and complexity.

title: Domaine Humbert Frères Gevrey Chambertin Premier Cru Craipillot

paras.text: A small vineyard of just under three hectares, Premier Cru Craipillot makes wines that Manou Humbert describes as ‘feminine’ in style, especially compared to the power and weight of Estournelles St. Jacques. The 65 year old vines lie just above Gevrey-Chambertin itself. A mid-weight palate here provides elegant red and black fruits and gentle spice on the nose, and delicate cassis, raspberry and strawberry flavours on the palate. Oak is extremely well-managed in order to allow the fruit to come to the fore; the pretty berry character will mellow into typical gaminess of Pinot Noir, ably supported by the vintage’s freshness on the finish. An understated wine that will suit those eager to begin drinking it earlier than some of the other wines from this domaine.

title: Domaine Jacques-Frédéric Mugnier Bonnes-Mares Grand Cru

paras.text: Vinification: 100% de-stemmed, 15 to 20 days alcoholic fermentation with indigenous yeasts and maceration in open wooden vats. 18 months aging in barrel (15% new oak).

title: Domaine Jacques-Frédéric Mugnier Chambolle-Musigny

paras.text: Les Plantes, covering approximately 0.56 hectares (1.4 acres) and planted in 1968-69 is classified as Premier Cru although we have decided to use it only as « village » classification.
La Combe d'Orveau, covering approximately 0.77 hectares (1.9 acres) was planted over several periods from 1952 to 1998. Annual production varies between 3000 and 7000 bottles approx.

This wine is recognisable by its intense bouquet which is simultaneously fruity, floral and very delicate. To complement the aromas, the wine has a supple structure that is always light and fine; the finish is long and blossoming on the palate.
Vinification:100% de-stemmed, vinification in open wooden vats. Aged for 18 months in barrel (15% new).

title: Domaine Jacques-Frédéric Mugnier Chambolle-Musigny Premier Cru Les Fuées

paras.text: Domaine Jacques-Frédéric Mugnier Chambolle-Musigny Premier Cru Les Fuées | Fine Vines

title: Domaine Jacques-Frédéric Mugnier Chambolle-Musigny Premier Cru Les Amoureuses

paras.text: Domaine Jacques-Frédéric Mugnier Chambolle-Musigny Premier Cru Les Amoureuses | Fine Vines
Vinification: 100% de-stemmed, 15 to 20 days indigenous yeast fermentation and maceration in open wooden vats. Aged for 18 months in barrel (15% new oak).

Ultra-elegant and pure aromas are comprised by notes of spiced plum, red raspberry, green tea and a pretty range of floral elements. The rich and satin-textured mouthcoating middle weight flavors possess an excellent sense of energy along with an abundance of minerality that adds a sense of lift to the dusty, focused and gorgeously persistent mildly austere finale. This is a classically styled Amoureuses of grace and lace and one that should age effortlessly for years.
