title: Meo-Camuzet Échezeaux Les Rouges Du Bas Grand Cru

paras.text: Échezeaux is loyal to its appellation through the finesse of its attack on the palate and its overall balance. But it's also a wine with pronounced acidity, which gives it freshness and structure and bestows upon it a sometimes austere finish.

Tasting: Échezeaux is loyal to its appellation through the finesse of its attack on the palate and its overall balance. But it's also a wine with pronounced acidity, which gives it freshness and structure and bestows upon it a sometimes austere finish.

Aging: This wine needs to be kept for a long time if it is to reveal all its richness. The natural acidity contained in the grapes tends to constrict it somewhat when it is young, and time must play its part to make it better balanced.

Maturing: Its development is slow, and right up to the moment when it is bottled, the wine is a little austere. Time is necessary, for this is a wine which tends to remain indifferent to whatever treatments you try to apply to it. It must like to be left alone. It may just react to new casks, Bertranges being the oak that is the most successful.
Vinification: The vinification requires little intervention, as the grapes already contain the elements which it takes to succeed.

Vines: The original planting dates from the end of the 40's, but about one quarter of this was renewed a few years ago. The grapes are small, particularly at the top of the plot. They ripen quickly, and a high sugar level combined with excellent acidity can often be observed, and this produces wines of intensity. The only difficulty is that these are grapes which have to be "snapped up” at harvest time: you cannot wait, or they will spoil.

Situation: As its name - "les Rouges du Bas” - does not indicate, this vineyard plot of about 1 acre, is situated at the upper limit of the Échezeaux appellation. The altitude explains perhaps the aromatic freshness often found in this wine, even though its east/south-east orientation also influences its early maturity. The nature of the soil changes with the altitude: lighter and lighter as you get higher.

title: Domaine Michel Bouzereau Bourgogne Cote D'Or

paras.text: From four hectares of vines across Puligny and Meursault, in 2018 the mix is 60-40 in favour of Meursault, and the ageing is 60% in 300-litre barrels, with the balance in 228-litre
, and much care is lavished to create a modern, satisfying white Burgundy. Drink now to 2024.

title: Domaine Charles Lachaux Aligoté Les Champs d’Argent

paras.text: Terroir: Located in the commune of Vose-Romanée, bottom of the slope. Very white, marly soils.
Vinification: Whole clusters directly pressed, indigenous yeast fermentation in barrel. Aged for 12 months in barrel (no new oak), unfined, unfiltered. No added sulfur.

title: Domaine Michel Bouzereau Bourgogne Cote D'Or Clos Du Moulin

paras.text: From four hectares of vines across Puligny and Meursault, in 2018 the mix is 60-40 in favour of Meursault, and the ageing is 60% in 300-litre barrels, with the balance in 228-litre
, and much care is lavished to create a modern, satisfying white Burgundy. Drink now to 2024.

title: Domaine Michel Bouzereau Meursault-Genevrieres Premier Cru

paras.text: Notes of pink grapefruit and rose petal swirl from the glass, with such alluring, attractive fragrance. There’s a quince note, too, and wild flowers. This is so complex, pure, and long. A delight.

title: Domaine Michel Bouzereau Meursault Les Perrières

paras.text: Just starting out, this wine, fresh from bottling, shows its weight, structure and distinct minerality. The fruit is coming along behind, ripe yellow peach and pink grapefruit over wood. It is very ageworthy—give it at least 3–4 years, certainly longer.

title: Domaine Michel Bouzereau Meursault Les Tessons

paras.text: The Les Tessons vineyard lies among a cluster of lieu dit vineyards just west of the village. Burgundy authority, Clive Coates MW named Domaine Michel Bouzereau as one of the “best cellars for (these) Deuxièmes Crus.” Coates went on to call the domaine the “best of the Bouzereau cellars [with] fine, racy, stylish wines which can be held longer than most.” Bouzereau began picking a little early, in late August, preserving the zippy acidity levels a ripe vintage. Burghound’s Allen Meadows writes that the domaine’s clearly outperformed the general quality of the vintages. The wine is showing lovely aromas of citrus, peach, apple, and a hint of smoke.

title: Domaine Michel Bouzereau Meursault Les Grands Charrons

paras.text: Domaine Michel Bouzereau et Fils is one of Meursault's most distinguished growers, creating rich and voluptuous wines. Grands Charrons sits at the same height as the Meursault Premiers Crus but with a more easterly exposure. This wine is beautifully aromatic with a bouquet of toasted hazelnuts, orange blossom and butterscotch. The palate offers up flavours of white fruits with a sublime honeyed richness and hint of toasted oak.

title: Domaine Michel Bouzereau Puligny Montrachet Le Cailleret Premier Cru

paras.text: Domaine Michel Bouzereau Puligny Montrachet Le Cailleret Premier Cru | Fine Vines

Jean-Baptiste is fortunate to have a small holding of this top Puligny Premier Cru which he has transformed into a brilliant wine. Fine bright light colour, with a very chiselled nose, quite intense, building to a lemon finish, very pure and intense, superb persistence. With intensity more than weight, blindingly bright starry wine.

title: Domaine Michel Bouzereau Puligny Montrachet Les Champs Gains

paras.text: This powerful and expressive wine seduces by the invigorating freshness of its bouquet with accents of citrus (lime), fresh laurel and spices. Nourishing, tactile but very energetic and active, the mouth is full of fresh fruits, between white fruits and citrus fruits, and the finish, spicy, already develops an unusual persistence.

title: Domaine Michel Juillot Mercurey Premier Cru "Clos Tonnerre" Rouge

paras.text: Manual harvest – Selective picking on sorting table – 100% destemming – Open fermentor – 20 days vatting – Temperature control – Natural yeast – Low intrusive, with such a level of concentration, the structure comes naturally and allows all the soil expression. Vertical press.

Allen Meadows: “A more deeply pitched nose is composed by plum, earth, pepper, spice and various ripe dark berry aromas that are sufficiently ripe to possess a top note of menthol. The mouth feel of the middle weight flavors is very rich, indeed to the point that they are suave. There is fine volume and the dry extract coats the mouth on the solidly persistent finish where the peppery character of the nose reappears. This should also drink well young.”

title: Domaine Michel Juillot Mercurey Premier Cru "Les Champs Martins" Rouge

paras.text: Domaine Michel Juillot Mercurey Premier Cru "Les Champs Martins" Rouge | Fine Vines
Soil: clayey-limestone and marl, alternating gravels limestone pebbles on surface
Manual harvest – Selective picking on sorting table – Full bunches in the press – 12 hours settling of the big lees – Fermentation in oak barrel – Temperature control – Natural yeast.
14 months in oak barrel – 30% new barrels – Malolactic fermentation completed – Fining before bottling.

Allen Meadows: “Here too there is enough residual sulfur present to make decanting this advisable in order to allow the fresh citrus, essence of pear, spice and wide-ranging floral elements to shine. There is that lovely sense of underlying tension to the lightly mineral-inflected middle weight flavors that display just enough wood to notice on the palate coating finish. This is quite good and should be accessible young but offer a few years of upside development potential.”

title: Domaine Michel Lafarge Beaune Premier Cru Grèves

paras.text: Terroir: Moderately steep slope facing directly east. Moderately deep, gravelly, light soils on limestone. 225 to 300-meters elevation.
Vinification: 100% de-stemmed, indigenous yeast fermentation, pneumatic press. Aged for 18 months, unfiltered.
Etymology: From the common Latin word GRAVA, meaning "crumbly stone, gravel, little stones, fine scree, sandy soil."
In Burgundy, vineyards named Grèves are generally scree-covered lands that are particularly suitable for growing vines.

Site: Les Grèves is one of the largest vineyards in Beaune, spanning most of the hill from top to bottom. The elevation ranges from 225 to 300 meters and measures well over half a kilometer across. The vineyard is located directly upslope, west of Beaune. The slope varies from steep at the top to nearly flat at the bottom. It faces directly east.

Geology and Soil: Because this vineyard is so large, the geology and soils are highly variable. The soil is moderately deep (50 cm), very gravelly, with significant amounts of silt and sand. There is very little clay with thick layers of poorly-sorted stones throughout. This texture makes for very light and dry soils.

Lafarge Parcel: The Lafarge parcel of Les Grèves stands out from the entire vineyard. This parcel is located in the northwest corner near the top of the slope at approximately 260-meters elevation. Small crumbling walls surround the vineyard on most sides, and although Frederic says that these small walls do not quite function exactly as a clos, they do help to stop the runoff from other vineyards, keeping his vines healthy. The vines within these small walls sit in a small concavity of the slope that looks like its own little nook, or cradle. Within this cradle are some of Lafarge’s oldest vines of Pinot Noir, with the oldest being up to 96 years old.

title: Domaine Michel Lafarge Beaune Premier Cru Les Aigrots Rouge

paras.text: ​​​​​​​Vinification: 100% de-stemmed, whole grape vinification, indigenous yeast fermentation, 15% new oak, unfined, unfiltered.

title: Domaine Michel Lafarge Bourgogne Pinot Noir

paras.text: Vinification: 2 weeks cuvaison, indigenous yeast fermentation. Aged for 18 months in older barrels.
These vines are located lower down on the hill, with equal distance between the village of Volnay and the

, on the limit of Volnay village and Bourgogne regional appellations. There is some talk that this parcel used to be classified a Volnay but was de-classified for some reason, though talking to Frédéric, it's been considered Burgundy-level since as long as he remembers. Regardless, ignoring official classification hierarchy, this wine is, as Russell puts it, a "baby Volnay": single-vineyard, might-as-well-be-Village-level wine with that typical Volnay limestone terroir. Entry-level pricing with a roundness that makes it approachable and easier to drink younger.

title: Domaine Michel Lafarge Meursault Vendanges Sélectionnées

paras.text: Vinification: Whole-cluster pressing pressed, cold settling, indigenous yeast fermentation in barrel, racking. Aged for 12 months, fined/filtered if necessary.

title: Domaine Michel Lafarge Meursault

paras.text: Vinification: Whole-cluster pressing pressed, cold settling, indigenous yeast fermentation in barrel, racking. Aged for 12 months, fined/filtered if necessary.

title: Domaine Michel Lafarge Volnay

paras.text: Terroir: Blend of parcels in northern and southern parts of Volnay, including Les Famines, Les Buttes, Des Cros Martin, all have clay-limestone soil
Vinification: 100% de-stemmed, pneumatic pressing, indigenous yeast fermentation Aged for 18 months in older oak barrels, unfiltered.

title: Domaine Michel Lafarge Volnay Premier Cru Clos du Château des Ducs Monopole

paras.text: Domaine Michel Lafarge Volnay Premier Cru Clos du Château des Ducs Monopole | Fine Vines
Terroir: Very gentle slope facing southeast. Deep, brown, clay soils on limestone. Monopole and true clos located in the garden of Domaine Lafarge. 290-meters elevation.
Vinification: 100% de-stemmed, pneumatic press, indigenous yeast fermentation, lightly settled. Aged for 18 months in older barrels, unfiltered.

Site: The Clos de Chateau des Ducs is located in Volnay, in the humble garden of the Lafarge Domain—making this hidden gem a true clos as well as a true monopole. The vineyard sits at an elevation of 290 meters. The slope is very gentle. It faces southeast. The vineyard is quiet and small with lush green trees, and there are even a few wandering chickens.

Geology and Soil: The soil here is deep because it stays in place thanks to the walls of the clos. The soil is brown (very little iron) and clay-rich. After about 35-40 cm of brown clay soil, there is a 25-centimeter layer of gravel—giving the vineyard excellent drainage.
Lafarge Parcel: Le Clos du Château des Ducs is a parcel that belongs entirely to the Lafarge domain, called a "monopole" in French.

The walls of the clos provide protection in many ways—they protect the soils from washing away or receiving outside material, and they also protect the vines from wind and frost, making this vineyard one of the warmest and often one of the first to be harvested. Frédéric believes that the well-drained soils make for lighter, softer wines.

title: Domaine Michel Lafarge Volnay Premier Cru Clos des Chênes

paras.text: Terroir: Shallow, red clay soils on limestone. Located at the intersection of the 4 premier cru vineyards of Volnay: Clos des Chênes, Les Caillerets, Taille Pieds, and En Champans. Moderate slope facing southeast.
Vinification: 100% de-stemmed, pneumatic pressing, indigenous yeast fermentation, light settling. Aged for 18 months, unfiltered.

Site: The Clos des Chênes is a large vineyard occupying most of the midslope, south of Volnay. Clos de Chênes has excellent neighbors, with Les Caillerets to the south, Taille Pieds to the north, and En Champans to the northeast. The slope is moderate and faces southeast. This position on the slope provides a clean, fresh breeze.

Geology and Soil: The bedrock geology of Clos de Chênes seems to influence a major transition in soil and terroir across the vineyard. The upper portion of Clos de Chênes has whiter soils and tends to produce wines with more structure, tannin, and austerity than the redder, richer soils at the bottom of the vineyard. Interestingly, the upper portion of the vineyard with whiter soils also has a slightly convex shape to the slope. This indicates that the soil is likely shallower, whereas the lower portion with redder soil is more concave, providing a small space, or “belly” for soil, and nutrients, to accumulate.

Lafarge Parcel: Frédéric believes that location is everything for this complex vineyard. The Lafarge parcel of 55 year-old vines is in the Northeast corner of the vineyard and is the first parcel to the south of Taille Pieds at the intersection of the 4 premier cru vineyards of Volnay (Clos de Chênes, Les Caillerets, Taille Pieds, and En Champans). The depth of the soils in the Lafarge parcels varies from 28-38 cm, but Frédéric only works the first 5-10 cm of the soil. The Lafarge parcel is on the lower portion of the vineyard with the convex slope where the soils are more red and more iron-rich, which give the wines their original, generous expression with great potential for aging.

title: Domaine Michel Lafarge Volnay Premier Cru Les Caillerets

paras.text: Terroir: Very gentle slope facing east. Moderately deep to shallow, reddish brown, clay soils on limestone. 275-meters elevation.
Vinification: 100% de-stemmed, indigenous yeast fermentation, 15% new oak, unfined, unfiltered.
are frequently used in Burgundy to describe stony soils. They stem from a Gallic word CAL-YO (caillou) meaning stone or stony slope.

Site: Les Caillerets is located approximately 1 km south of Volnay on the lower portion of the slope. It sits at approximately 275-meters elevation. The slope is very gentle to flat with some small undulations within the walls of the Lafarge parcel. It faces just south of east.

Soil: The soils of Les Caillerets are approximately 40 cm deep. They are reddish-brown, very dense, and clay-rich. The vineyard is very rocky with up to 40% small (gravel to cobble sized) poorly-sorted limestone stones on the surface.

Lafarge Parcel: The Lafarge parcel of Les Caillerets is very unique because it is surrounded by walls that influence the small undulations in the topography and contributes to the quiet, peaceful atmosphere. Frédéric believes that the minerality of this terroir is what makes it one of the greatest terroirs of Volnay—salty, lingering, and energetic. Because Les Caillerets is made in an almost identical fashion to Les Mitans, these two wines provide a good opportunity to taste the terroirs.

title: Domaine Michel Lafarge Volnay Premier Cru Les Pitures

paras.text: Terroir: Gentle slope facing southeast. Soils are moderately deep, brown clay on limestone bedrock. 250-meters elevation.
Vinification: 100% de-stemmed, whole grape fermentation, indigenous yeast fermentation, 15% new oak, unfined, unfiltered.

title: Domaine Michel Lafarge Volnay Premier Cru Les Mitans

paras.text: Terroir: Gentle slope facing southeast. Soils are moderately deep, brown clay on limestone bedrock. 250-meters elevation.
Vinification: 100% de-stemmed, whole grape fermentation, indigenous yeast fermentation, 15% new oak, unfined, unfiltered.

Site: Les Mitans sits downslope from the small village of Volnay. It is located at approximately 250-meters elevation. The vineyard lies on a low, gentle slope that faces just south of east. Even though Les Mitans lies in the direct path of a small combe to the west, Frédéric does not believe that the vineyard experiences much influence from it—possibly due to its distance down the slope.

Soil: The soil is approximately 35-40 cm deep. The soil is deep brown in color with a dense, clay-rich texture. The brown color indicates that the soil is not rich in iron, which is a notable difference from other great vineyards of Volnay, such as Caillerets and Clos de Chênes. Approximately 20% of the surface is covered in small (gravel to cobble-sized) limestone stones. The stones in the vineyard are poorly sorted indicate some alluvial influence.

Lafarge Parcel: The vines in the Lafarge parcel are approximately 65 years old. The vines are planted downslope to the east. Frédéric points out that the clay-rich soils of Les Mitans are surprisingly light and “springy” when stepped on, a factor he strongly attributes to biodynamic farming. He also believes that the final wine reflects this springiness in its freshness, femininity, and balance between clay and stone influences.

title: Domaine Michel Lafarge Volnay Vendanges Sélectionnées

paras.text: Vinification: 2 weeks in tank, indigenous yeast fermentation. Aged for 18 months in barrel (7% new), one racking.
This cuvée is made only in good years when yields are high enough in Volnay to warrant putting aside grapes from the older vines.

title: Domaine Michel Niellon Chassagne-Montrachet Blanc

paras.text: Sourced from several parcels, totaling just under two hectares; Michel is often the first to pick in his area, preferring good acidity for freshness in the wines. The vines were planted in 1963 and 1993. This is full-bodied, with the classic Chassagne aromas of ripe yellow orchard fruit and resin.

title: Domaine Michel Niellon Chassagne-Montrachet Clos Saint-Jean Premier Cru

paras.text: Domaine Michel Niellon Chassagne-Montrachet Clos Saint-Jean Premier Cru | Fine Vines

The Chassagne-Montrachet 1er Cru Clos Saint-Jean is one of the highlights of the Niellon portfolio this year, unwinding in the glass with notes of pear, lemon, toast, nutmeg and subtle smoke. On the palate, the wine is medium to full-bodied, satiny and concentrated, with terrific depth, racy acids and a long, stony finish. 1992 was the first vintage for these vines, Niellon's holdings here having previously been planted entirely to Pinot Noir, and they are clearly hitting their stride today.

title: Domaine Michel Niellon Chassagne-Montrachet Premier Cru Clos De La Maltroie

paras.text: Domaine Michel Niellon Chassagne-Montrachet Premier Cru Clos De La Maltroie | Fine Vines
Selected from a parcel of vines planted in 1977, half to Chardonnay and half to Pinot Noir.
Aroma: Succulent flavors or juicy peach, fresh pears, exotic fruits and bright citrus.
Length/Type of Fermentation: Grapes are fermented in stainless steel tanks and then transferred to oak barrels for malolactic fermentation.

title: Domaine Michel Niellon Chassagne-Montrachet Premier Cru Les Vergers

paras.text: Les Vergers is on the more gentle part of the slope north of the village of Chassagne, with clay and gravelly limestone soils. This climat gives the wine a crisp mineral profile layered over silky citrus and orchard fruit notes. The vines were planted in 2001.

title: Domaine Michel Niellon Chassagne-Montrachet Premier Cru Les Champgains

paras.text: Domaine Michel Niellon Chassagne-Montrachet Premier Cru Les Champgains | Fine Vines
Champgains sits at the crest of the slope between Chassagne and Puligny; the plot is just under half a hectare, planted in 1988. Clay and fragmented rock soil.

title: Domaine Michel Niellon Chassagne-Montrachet Premier Cru Les Chaumées

paras.text: Domaine Michel Niellon Chassagne-Montrachet Premier Cru Les Chaumées | Fine Vines

Pale, bright yellow. High-pitched aromas of citrus fruits, mint and flowers. Concentrated and tactile, with the flavors of pineapple, lemon, lime, pear drop and fresh hay supported by a firm mineral underpinning. Slightly glyceral and exotic, this wine finishes with palate-staining minerality and sneaky length. Coutoux notes that the vines in this rocky site are in very good shape and never produce overipe fruit.

title: Domaine Michel Niellon Chevalier-Montrachet Grand Cru

paras.text: This famous grand cru has soils so rocky that Michel had to use small explosives when he replanted his plot of 28 rows of vines in 1970. The shallow soils force the vines to struggle as they produce small quantities of exceptional, highly-extracted fruit. The resulting wine is mineral-driven with a strikingly complex nose of ripe fruit, acacia blossom and stone.

title: Domaine Michel Niellon Chassagne-Montrachet Rouge

paras.text: Sourced from several parcels, totaling just under two hectares; Michel is often the first to pick in his area, preferring good acidity for freshness in the wines. The vines were planted in 1963 and 1993. This is full-bodied, with the classic Chassagne aromas of ripe yellow orchard fruit and resin.
A minerally expression drives this sleek white, whose flavors evoke white peach, white flowers and citrus oil. Light-bodied and intense, with fine length.

title: Domaine Nicolas Joly Saviennières Clos De La Coulée De Serrant

paras.text: First planted in 1130 by Cistercian monks, the Clos de la Coulée de Serrant has been in the Joly family since 1962. Nicolas Joly began converting the family domaine to biodynamics in 1981 and has been a leader in the movement to apply Rudolf Steiner’s agricultural philosophy to the vine. His daughter, Virginie, worked her first harvest in 2002, and has brought a pragmatic vision to her father’s holistic goals. The 17.2 acres of vines at the Clos are between 35 and 80 years old, growing on steep schist slopes. The wine ferments and ages in 500-liter barrels, with no more than five percent new oak in a vintage. Whether or not you appreciate the style and the sometimes-oxidative character, there are no other wines like it. Deep gold in color, dark in its earthy savor, this layers floral scents, ginger and ripe pineapple with earthy notes of schist. It has a kind of invisible freshness, open and racy, delicately detailed. Give this time in the cellar and plenty of air; it is used to oxygen and only gains freshness over the course of several days open.

"Golden yellow. Aromas of tobacco, ripe yellow peach and brioche. A multilayered wine with its own distinctly “orange” character, the broad-shouldered apricot flavor is accented by tea leaf and lime. Concentrated, warm and deep, finishing with an unmistakable extract sweetness and a supple texture. This was my favorite of the six Chenin Blancs I tasted at the estate..." --Stephen Tanzer
Vine Age: Due to re-plantings, the average age is 35-40 years old (oldest vines planted in 1935)
Vinification: Indigenous yeast fermentation in tank or 500L barrel (no chaptilization or temperature control). Aged for 6-8 months in 500L barrels (5% max. new oak), low sulfur doses.

title: Domaine Nicolas Joly Saviennières Les Vieux Clos

paras.text: Joly's golden-yellow Savennières Les Vieux Clos is pure and elegant on the herbal and flinty nose, where spicy lemon/lemon grass and ripe, concentrated fruit aromas are displayed. Very well defined! On the palate, the 14.5% alcohol comes along in perfect balance: very elegant and finesse-full. since the powerful body is lifted by a piquant acidity, a lovely transparency and finesse, and finally escorted by a dense and lush fruit texture. The finish is very precise, fresh and aromatic, but also full of elegance, salt and stimulation. (RP)

Vinification: Indigenous yeast fermentation, no temperature control or chaptalization, in tank or barrel, no settling of must. Aged for 6-8 months in older barrels, 1-2 rackings, very low sulfur additions.

title: Domaine Nicolas Rossignol Pommard

paras.text: Terroir: Blend of parcels from Pommard including Le Poisot (southeastern corner), En Boeuf (northwest near Beaune), Les Petits Noizons, Les Vignots
Vinification: Some whole cluster, few days cold (14°C) soaking, 6 to 8 days indigenous yeast alcoholic fermentation. 18 months aging on fine lees, 1 racking, unfined, unfiltered.

title: Domaine Nicolas Rossignol Bourgogne Pinot Noir

paras.text: Since the 2013 vintage, this cuvée has also included the vines (planted in 1922) from Nicolas' Héritières cuvée.
Terroir: Multiple village-appellation parcels in Volnay and Pommard, lower and flatter land. Mix of brown soils from clay to silt and rocks (rich but shallow)
Vinification: 100% de-stemmed, 10 to 15 days cold (14°C) soaking, 6 to 8 days indigenous yeast alcoholic fermentation. 1 year aging on fine lees, 1 racking, unfined, unfiltered.

title: Domaine Nicolas Rossignol Volnay Premier Cru Cailleret

paras.text: These vines were owned by Nicolas' grandparents. Some went to his uncle and some to his father, but he was able to acquire both portions.
Vinification: 100% de-stemmed, 10 to 15 days cold (14°C) soak, 1 week indigenous yeast alcoholic fermentation. 18 months aging in barrel (20% new), 1 racking, unfined, unfiltered.

title: Domaine Pascal et Nicolas Reverdy Sancerre Les Coûtes

paras.text: A single hillside plot of 55 year old vines on chalky Kimmeridgian Marne (aka Terre Blanche), hand-harvested at 45 hl/ha. Fermented and aged in stainless steel tanks. Bottled unfiltered.

title: Domaine Nicolas Rossignol Volnay Premier Cru Santenots

paras.text: Terroir: Santenots du Bas, gentle slope, deeper iron-rich red soil with large rocks, and sandy texture

Vinification: 100% de-stemmed, indigenous yeast fermentation, minimal punch-downs. Aged for 18 months in barrel (25% new oak). Nicolas strives to use sulfur only prior to bottling. Total sulfur: 20-45 mg/L.

title: Domaine Patrice Rion Bourgogne Chardonnay

paras.text: Hand-harvested, the bunches are pressed whole, then fermented and matured in older oak barrels for 12 months.
Visually: Our white Burgundy has a crystal clear, limpid appearance, frequently with green tints.

On the nose: This wine shows in its youth white flowers, lilies and ferns, which evolve into notes of hazelnut. As it ages, the wine shows honeyed, sometimes buttery accents, with additional aromas of spice and sugared chestnuts, and often mentholated fruits.
On the palate: The wine is round at the beginning, but its clear acidity gives it a tension that leads to a beautiful mineral finish.

Our white Burgundy is versatile and wonderful with food. Its liveliness makes it a great aperitif wine. Its aromatic range and persistence make it a star with fish, shellfish and seafood. Serve around 12 C. Drinks best within the first five year of its life.

title: Domaine Patrice Rion Chambolle-Musigny Les Cras

paras.text: Vineyard placement and geology: Situated halfway up the hill and facing full east, the parcel is particularly well-placed for a Village wine. The shallow clay soil contains a significant amount of crushed limestone.
Yield and production: 30-35 hl/ha for an average annual production of 2400 bottles
Hand-harvested and scrupulously sorted, the wine is fermented in open stainless steel tanks for around three weeks, then matured in oak barrels, with about 50% new oak, for 18 months.
On the nose: small red fruits dominate, particularly redcurrants, followed by more complex aromas of white pepper and a sense of freshness.
On the palate: the wine is quite chewy for a Village-level appellation. It starts straight and tense in the mouth, with its minerality helping to draw out the finish to an impressive length.
Its open profile allows this wine to go well with most meats, but particularly well with feathered game such as duck, pheasant and quail.

title: Domaine Patrice Rion Chambolle-Musigny

paras.text: This wine is characterized by its extreme finesse, depth and silky, elegant tannic structure. Its individual personality comes from the great age of the vines.

Vineyard placement and geology: Two parcels combine to produce this wine. The first is at the bottom of the slope on fairly deep clay soil; the second at the top of the hill on mostly limestone soil. It’s the combination of the two terroirs that makes the whole greater than the sum of its parts.
Yield and production : 35-45 hl/ha for an average annual production of 3000 bottles.
Hand-harvested and scrupulously sorted, the wine is fermented in open stainless steel tanks for around three weeks, then matured in oak barrels, about 50% new, for 18 months.
To the eye, the wine is a fairly lightly colored, but with flashes of brilliant sparkles at the edge.
On the nose, aromas of cocoa and eucalyptus mingle with small red fruits and redcurrants.

On the palate, its concentration doesn’t detract from its finesse, with a tannic structure that is there, but very discreet. Above all, it’s the wine’s length on both the nose and palate that characterize this delicate appellation
Its elegance and finesse permit this win to go with more delicate meat dishes, such as roast pigeon or guinea hen, or other feathered game.

title: Domaine Patrice Rion Chambolle-Musigny Premier Cru Les Gruenchers

paras.text: Chambolle-Musigny’s “Les Gruenchers” is famous for its proximity to Grand Cru “Bonnes Mares”—only several hundred feet away—and, along with Dujac’s far-more expensive bottling, Patrice Rion’s breathtaking example boldly offers another reason for its stardom.

This is a Premier Cru linked to prestige names like Dujac and Fourrier, but with this singular bottle, Rion has unabashedly squeezed between the two, staking its claim as one of the greats. It’s an extraordinary expression of pure, cellar-worthy Burgundy that has only continued to climb in acclaim and rarity—only 100 cases are produced each year! Patrice Rion has impressively built up his holdings to include some of the finest terroirs in the Côte de Nuits and this 2014 “Les Gruenchers” is among his best. It’s horse-and-plow farmed and classically crafted, ultimately making this $99 gem a brilliant value when compared to the mighty titans it competes with. Our small supply means that we can only offer up to four per person today, so don’t miss this limited, high-flying Pinot Noir. It is impeccable red Burgundy through and through.

title: Domaine Patrick Baudouin Anjou Blanc Effusion

paras.text: Gateway to our local chenins, Effusion is our first real dry chenin cuvée, inaugurated in 2001.
Assembly of plots of hillsides on cinerites, rocks of volcanic origin, sandstone conglomerates, all resting on the schist base of black Anjou.
Effusion is a wine of aromatic freshness, as its name suggests while remaining well structured. From aperitif to cheese, including fish and grilled white meats.

Vinification and Aging: Direct pressing. Overnight settling at cellar temperature. Assembling of the batch in the tank and starting on the Domaine's leaven. Setting in barrel, top settling by fermentation (guillage). Spontaneous malo. Land filtration.

title: Domaine Denis Bachelet Côte de Nuits-Village

paras.text: Terroir: 3 plots in Queue de Hareng in Brochon, 3 plots in Vignois, 1 plot in Créole. Limestone and clay soils, facing east at about 300-meters altitude,
Vinification: 100% de-stemmed, crushed, indigenous yeast fermentation. Aged for 16-18 months in barrel (25% new oak).

title: Domaine Patrick Baudouin Anjou Blanc Les Saulaies

paras.text: Another plot that can offer large shale chains. On the left bank of Layon and with centuries-old vines. This plot often offers us vintages with a few residual sugars. In the glass, always of race, finesse, elegance, length. Roasted poultry, veal, fish, crustaceans, cheeses…

Pale golden with green nuances, its nose mixes anise with candied lemon, then it is nuanced with sweet almond and white pepper, before delicately revealing its accommodation with a few white peach fragrances.

The mouth reveals it more precisely by its texture. Woody, it offers a weave for the wine, it gives it a relief that suits the taste buds who explore it to discover each floral element, fruity or spicy. The intense freshness further accentuates the aromatic effects.
Slow fermentation in vats and Burgundy barrels of 5 wines. Total malolactic fermentation. Aging in barrels on fine lees.

Vinification and Aging: Delivering wines, not making them: not acting, or at least, is a very demanding choice, requires precision and sometimes… a lot of work! Neither yeasting nor chaptalization ... Slow pressing - Natural settling 24 h - Slow fermentation in vats and Burgundy barrels of several wines. Total malolactic fermentation. Aging in barrels on fine lees, from harvest (October) until before bottling, in May.

title: Domaine Patrick Baudouin Anjou Rouge Les Coteaux D'Ardenay

paras.text: On the slopes of the hamlet of Ardenay, next to two restored mills, Cabernet Francs planted in 1990 on sedimented ashes left by very old volcanoes. Tillage, limited yields, maturity: we don't like the aromas of green pepper, pyrazine, sharp tannins.

In the cellar, total destemming, long, sweet infusion of one month, maturing in barrels of several wines until bottling. A "Terroir" wine, the Coteaux d´Ardenay have complex and deep aromas combined with a fresh, long, Loire mouth. The dense and structured, but fine, frame of this wine will allow a harmonious confrontation with characterful red meats, game, leg of lamb, ribs of beef or steaks, flank or tab. Complex and deep allied with a fresh and long mouth , Loire. Winter dishes are also welcome (stews, stews, etc.).

title: Domaine Patrick Baudouin Quarts de Chaume Les Zersilles

paras.text: The hillsides of Zerzilles a Chaume have long been known. Facing south east, it is perfectly suited to the production of sweet wines exceptions. Thin soils, poorly developed on a base of Carboniferous age. Presence of coal shale and sandstone.
, thin/poor soil of shale and sandstone on Carboniferous-era bedrock, facing southeast.
Vinification: Gentle pressing, indigenous yeast fermentation in 1 to 3-year-old Burgundian barrels . Aged in older barrels, racking and blending in tank for 1 month before bottling.
At harvest, pickers pass up to five times through the vines to be sure they pick only grapes with concentrated botrytis.

title: Domaine Patrick Baudouin Savennières

paras.text: The best-known vintage of the dry chenins of Anjou, right bank of the Loire. Plot planted in 2019, on alteration of talcose ocher shale. On a gentle slope facing south, in the town of Savennières, view of the Loire. She deserves her name! Horse work since fall 2016. April 2017: the plot was completely frozen, like a large part of the Savennières vines. In 2018, she came back to life!
A structured but fresh wine, which requires an association with elaborate dishes: white butter fish, cream poultry, mushrooms.

title: Domaine Patrick Baudouin Coteaux du Layon Les Coteaux

paras.text: Coteaux du Layon on freshness, naturally concentrated like all our sweet wines, but without the action of botrytis.

Light and pure, more on white fruit than candied. As an aperitif, but it will also go well with salads with foie gras or gizzards, with smoked fish and cooked or parsley cheeses. Its freshness will also suit unsweetened fruity desserts, such as apricot pies.

Vinification and Aging: Intervening at a minimum does not mean: deciding nothing. We take the responsibility not to sulphite the juices leaving the press, not to add selected yeasts, not to chaptalize ... Slow pressing - Natural settling 24 h - Slow fermentation in Burgundy barrels of 3 and 4 wines. Total alcoholic and malolactic fermentation. Aging in Burgundy barrels on fine lees, from harvest (October) to July (duration 10 months) then aging in vats until bottling. But we accompany, monitor, and intervene when we deem it necessary, until the setting: racking, aging, light sulfitages ... Wine does not exist without the work of the winemakers.

title: Domaine Paul Autard Chateauneuf Du Pape

paras.text: Bright ruby-red. Smoke- and spice-accented aromas of ripe red berries and licorice carry a smoky mineral topnote. Focused, penetrating and firm, showing bright lift to the raspberry and bitter cherry flavors. Closes with resonating spiciness, gripping tannins and an echo of candied red fruit.

title: Domaine Paul Autard Côtes Du Rhône

paras.text: 85% Grenache and 15% Syrah, from grapes grown in several parcels just outside the Châteauneuf-du-Pape appellation in Courthézon. The vines average 45 year old, with the oldest being 75 year old. The grapes are all handpicked and transported to the winery in small boxes so as not to damage the fruit. Autard sorts the harvest twice, and then de-stems and lightly crushes the fruit to spontaneously begin the fermentation process by releasing the juice. Maceration and fermentation take place in temperature-controlled stainless steel tanks over 25 days. Autard’s tanks are equipped with a pneumatic mechanism to carry out pigeage (or punching down of the cap) to ensure optimal and gentle extraction. In addition, two pumping over operations (remontages) are carried out daily for 10 days, to enhance extraction and aerate the wine, in order to obtain a plush texture. Each of the varieties are vinified separately, assembled in late January, and aged in stainless steel tanks until bottling in late February. Autard’s Côtes-du-Rhône is a smoky, complex wine, loaded with warm raspberry fruit, showing many of the best attributes of Châteauneuf-du-Pape. 14.5% alcohol.

title: Domaine Paul Jaboulet Aîné Cotes du Rhone Parallele 45 Blanc

paras.text: Food Pairing: Pork, Rich fish (salmon, tuna etc), mature and hard cheese, poultry, cured meat

title: Domaine Paul Jaboulet Aîné Cotes du Rhone Biographie

paras.text: One of the most complete and natural Cotes du Rhone offerings from a big wine domaine is Caroline Frey’s Jaboulet Biographie Cotes du Rhone and this warmly ripe and pleasing wine is a tremendous value in this price class with pure Grenache plummy fruits leading the way on the medium bodied palate. Frey has led Domaine Paul Jaboulet Ainé into the full conversion to organic viticulture throughout their range and this fresh and delicious Cotes du Rhone Rouge is one of the newly all organic certified lineup. This wine, from a stellar and riper Rhone vintage, has a classic blend of mostly Grenache along with a healthy dose Syrah and Mourvedre, which adds a deeper complexity than you’d expect in a southern Rhone entry level wine and as it gets air it almost takes on darker character in line with the Northern Rhone or higher elevation Gigondas. The vines are mainly over 40 years old, with some well over 80, and there is plenty of concentration in the profile with boysenberry, plum, huckleberry, cherry and strawberry fruits, peppery spices, mineral essences, iron/meaty elements, a hint of embers, anise, dried flowers and a touch of cedar.

title: Domaine Paul Jaboulet Aîné Côtes du Rhône Parallele 45 Rosé

paras.text: A blend of 50% Grenache, 40% Cinsault and 10% Syrah, the Cotes du Rhone Parallele 45 Rose comes across as significantly less tutti-frutti than some past vintages, instead offering hints of dried spices and crushed stone. It still shows redmberry flavors and some peachy notes, but this medium-bodied wine finishes with sufficient citrusy acids to be refreshing.

title: Domaine Paul Jaboulet Aîné Côtes du Rhône Parallele 45 Rouge

paras.text: This Cotes du Rhone takes its name from the 45th North parallel which runs two kilometres from the cellars of Maison Paul Jaboulet Aine In the village of Pont de l’Isere, a monument symbolises this line with the inscription: “the South begins here”. The wine has had this name since the beginning of the 1950s. 60% Grenache ; 40% Syrah.
Northern style Cotes du Rhone, with beautiful fresh Syrah character. Notes of wild berries, white pepper, lavender and cherries. This balanced red finishes with incredibly juicy Grenache love.

title: Domaine Paul Jaboulet Aîné Crozes-Hermitage Domaine de Thalabert Rouge

paras.text: Domaine Paul Jaboulet Aîné Crozes-Hermitage Domaine de Thalabert Rouge | Fine Vines

The Côtes du Rhône red wine Crozes Hermitage Cuvée Domaine de Thalabert, with a deep Ruby color, limpid and brilliant, an Intense, complex and aromatic nose with a melt of small red fruits mixed with animal notes.

title: Domaine Paul Jaboulet Aîné Crozes-Hermitage Les Jalets

paras.text: Les jalets, « rocks » in old French, refers to the round pebbles deposited by the alpine glaciers which are very present in the Crozes Hermitage appellation. The wine mainly comes from the Châssis plain. Production does not exceed 40 hectolitres per hectare. It is a light wine, with agreable soft tannins, which give immediate pleasure.

title: Domaine Paul Jaboulet Aîné Hermitage La Chapelle

paras.text: If you did not know, La Chapelle is not a vineyard. It’s a trade marked name. It takes its name from the small chapel of St. Christophe. The fruit is sourced from Bessards, Le Meal, Greffieux and Rocoules.

To produce the wine of Jaboulet La Chapelle, the grapes are 100% destemmed and are fermented on a parcel by parcel basis. The amount of new, French oak used to age the wine varies from vintage to vintage, depending on the character and quality of the harvest.

The wine is full bodied, concentrated and with expressive black fruit and leafy, earthy and iron scents. Typically, Jaboulet La Chapelle requires a decade or two to become civilized. The wines from the best years can age 30-40 years.

One of the reasons for the continued improvement of Jaboulet La Chapelle is the draconian selection for the wine. Previously, up to 7,000 cases of wine were produced. But today, the average annual production is closer to 2,000 cases per vintage of Jaboulet La Chapelle.

title: Domaine Paul Jaboulet Aîné Hermitage Le Chevalier de Sterimberg

paras.text: 70% Marsanne, 30-35% Roussanne, mainly from La Croix, Rocoules, Maison Blanche, oldest Marsanne 1900s, 25-33% egg vat (since 2009) fermented, raised 9 months, 67-75% new, 1-2 year 225-litre oak casks fermented, raised 9 months (until 2003 mix of 10% new, 45% each 1 and 2 year oak used, until 1998 vat-fermented, 1998-2009 then all oak, malo blocked, organic wine, 11,500-20,000 b, up from 8,000 b

Pale yellow; the nose is reserved, but elegant, has an air of cooked lime, mandarin, gun flint. The palate is light for a Hermitage blanc, is fashionably tense etc, its maker hankering after the North; it has a floral presence, white fruits led by apricot with peach stone, then a touch of late grip, tang. The aftertaste is nutty, shows citrus, vanilla. This carries some inner strength, as it should. I can see it gaining some weight. 14°.

title: Domaine Paul Jaboulet Aîné Hermitage Maison Bleue Rouge

paras.text: Replacing La Petite Chapelle in the Jaboulet lineup is the Hermitage La Maison Bleue. Rather than being a selection of lots that didnt make the cut for La Chapelle, its more terroir-based, with the wine coming from the eastern (non-granitic) side of the appellation. Because of that, its softer in style, with a rich, velvety texture. Cedar and spice notes frame cassis and cola notes, lingering through the long, supple finish.

title: Domaine Paul Pernot Bâtard-Montrachet Grand Cru

paras.text: Vinification: The cellar being in Puligny, (high water table), is not dig down very deep. It is not a very cold cellar, and subject to change of temperature with the seasons. Also with an early winter, alcoholic fermentation and malolactic will be slow, if the summer in early, Paul(S) the first racking is s done in May( for Bourgogne Aligoté/ Bourgogne blanc) to insure the fresh-ness of the wines - Put in stainless cask, the wine has been fine and bottled in July. - Bottling had been done in July.

History: Family estate since 6 generations, and now 3 generations are running the domaine, Paul, his 2 sons Paul and Michel, and his grand child Philippe. One of the largest domaine in Puligny Montrachet started by the family but Paul extended and re planted slowly many vineyards like Clos des Folatieres despite the hard work which had to be done. He said now it will be easier with the new tractors/ machines.

The top value of the domaine: If we ask to Paul Pernot what are the important points Farming - Sustainable with a control of production by de-buding - Plowing. No herbicide - Anticipation on sickness and due treatment to have no risk. Too difficult to cure

title: Domaine Pavelot Savigny-les-Beaune 1er Cru Les Serpentières

paras.text: Terroir: Facing south, this cru located mid-hill has a moderate slope. The soil, marly and deep, is embellished with some angular pebbles. The name of "Serpentières" most certainly originates from the formerly numerous presence of snakes attracted by the vicinity of some sources.

Expression: This beautiful ruby red wine seduces with the elegance and liveliness it exudes. Its pure nose combines fruit and minerality specific to the locality. On the palate, the structure is harmonious, fresh and of good length, all the subtlety of a vine of respectable age.
Guard: Very pleasant in its youth, it has a very good capacity of guard (7-10 years).
