title: Domaine Pavelot Bourgogne Rouge

paras.text: Terroir: Wine from several parcels in the Burgundy appellation located at the crossroads of the municipalities of Savigny-les-Beaune, Pernand-Vergelesses and Aloxe-Corton. It is located on the foothills of the coasts, the deep clay soil gives the vine a stress-free growth.

Expression: This wine exudes scents of fresh fruit. Elegant and charming, it coats the palate with sweet cherry. An initiatory wine, it offers the right key to discover all the riches of our other appellations.
Mets: Pâtés, terrines, rillettes, cold meats, andouillette, bourguignonne hotpot, cooked cheeses…
Serving Temperature: 12 to 14 ° C for a young wine, 14 to 16 ° C for a more ripe wine.

title: Domaine Pavelot Savigny-les-Beaune Premier Cru Aux Gravains

paras.text: Terroir: A vintage located on barely pronounced hillsides, the light soil is composed of sediments mixed with a fairly large proportion of gravel. Characteristic which gives its definition to the locality, Gravains - graviers. Facing south.

Expression: From a deep garnet, this wine with ripe fruit aromas, offers an intoxicating bouquet. The very elegant texture of this wine offers a perfect harmony between fruit and tannins. The most beautiful balance of the range.
Food: Beef bourguignon or other meats in sauce, feathered and haired game, cheese, type: friend of Chambertin…

title: Domaine Pavelot Savigny-les-Beaune Premier Cru La Dominode

paras.text: Terroir: Cru located on a moderate slope whose clay soil contains a significant part of sand. Exposed to the east, this terroir takes its name from the Latin "Dominus", it was originally owned by the "Lord" of Savigny. Not always located on wine maps, this terroir is located between Les Marconnets and Les Jarrons 1er cru.

Expression: With its intense and deep garnet, this wine offers a bouquet, of great complexity, where fruit, spices and musk mingle. Velvety, fleshy, intense, persistent, so many qualifiers that make this cru the spearhead of the domain.
Guard: Very vinous Pinot, this wine of great aging (15 years) also knows how to be appreciated in its young years. For power lovers.
Food: Boeuf bourguignon, wild boar filet mignon, venison with great huntsman sauce, cheeses, type: Cîteaux, Epoisses, Soumaintrain…

title: Domaine Petroni Rosé Corse AOP

paras.text: Pale in colour, the wine is rich and intense on the nose, displaying floral and fresh fruit aromas and a touch of minerality.
The same complexity is found on the palate, where the wine is long- lingering and refreshing.
Enjoy with antipasti, Mediterranean dishes like stuffed aubergines and courgettes, sushi, fish curries.
The soil around Aléria is characterized by its clay sediments left over by the evaporation of the Miocene sea (5 Ma).
This rosé is made from carefully selected grapes which are picked during the coolness of the night to prevent oxydation. Fermentation takes place at low temperatures of 14-18°C and lasts 3 weeks.

title: Domaine Pavelot Savigny-les-Beaune Rouge

paras.text: The place called "Les Planchots" (55 years old) located on the plain, on a deep soil with a sandy structure, gives a rich and oily wine dominated by aromas of citrus fruits (grapefruit ..) and dried fruits.
The place called "Les Vermots" (15 years old) located on hillsides on a limestone soil, gives a lively wine with a dominant mineral and fruity (peach…).
The combination of these two plots gives a very aromatic and round balanced wine.
Guard: Wine of pleasure, Savigny can be appreciated from its first year of bottling

title: Domaine Petroni Rouge Corse AOP

paras.text: This red wine has a ruby hue with violet hints. On the nose, the wine offers aromas of red fruit (strawberries, blackcurrant and raspberries) as well as delicate spice and a light minerality. It is supple on entry to the palate with red fruit flavours and subtle roasted notes. The finish is ample with silky tannins and good length.
Perfect with grilled red meat, pizza and sheep’s milk cheese. Serve between 16 and 18°C
The soil is characterized by its sand and clay sediments left over by the evaporation of the Miocene sea (5 Ma).
Traditional, long fermentation (20 days) in concrete vats. 12 months maturation in stainless steel tanks.

title: Domaine Pierre Damoy Bourgogne Rouge

paras.text: Lots of flavor of dark fruit balanced against earth tones. A well balanced Pinot Noir, that is good to drink now but will also age well.

title: Domaine Pierre Damoy Chambertin Clos De Bèze Grand Cru

paras.text: The Clos De Beze Grand Cruin grand cru vineyard faces east on a well-drained, gentle slope on the lower hillside east of Chambertin-Clos de Bèze. It is said that the small Notre Dame de Bèze chapel on this site was intentionally burned in the 1830s so that the land could be planted to more vines. This wine comes from a 2.2-hectare (5-acre) plot covered with thin, stony, limestone soils, around the original La Chapelle vineyard; the vines were planted in 1947. The bouquet is disarmingly hedonistic, with hints of violets and honeysuckle layering the opulent, dark-cherry expression. The palate demonstrates quintessential elegance— silk on velvet—with delicious length to the dark fruit and earth flavors.

title: Domaine Pierre Damoy Chambertin Grand Cru

paras.text: The limestone soils of Chambertin have the same ratio of fine earth to pebbles (68 to 32 percent) as Montrachet and—like the Montrachet wines—Chambertin has the potential to age magnificently. This rich, generous wine is selected from a half-hectare (1.2-acre) plot at the extreme north end of the 12.9-hectare (32-acre) vineyard, at an altitude of 275 to 300 meters (900 to 985 feet).
Chambertin: small 1 hectare plot at extreme northern end of the vineyard Colour: dense garnet; Bouquet: brooding, animal, inky, forest floor; Palate: dense and unyielding; strong tannin profile.

The wine finds some of its focus with time in the glass. A round, textured finish supported by muscular yet well-integrated tannins is totally inviting. Floral notes add an attractive note of brightness. Nevertheless, this is a highly promising wine. Damoy's Chambertin parcels were planted in 1973 and 1974.

title: Domaine Pierre Damoy Chapelle Chambertin Grand Cru

paras.text: Chapelle-Chambertin is considered one of the sturdiest and richest Gevrey's Grand Crus, in turn the more masculine Burgundy's village. Damoy, with his organic production style, owns the largest slice of it. Slow to open up, it gradually releases a deep scents bouquet made of cherry dipped in chocolate, blackberry, undergrowth and tar, dark cocoa bitter orange. Ripe, chewy yet juicy, silky yet viscous, great balance and alive tannin, blueberry's acidity, remind of orange, long and complex bitter finale. Top.

title: Domaine Pierre Damoy Gevry Chambertin La Justice

paras.text: First grapes contracted in 2008 Ripe cherrystone nose ; concentrated and ripe palate with great energy

title: Domaine Pierre Damoy Marsannay La Brétignière

paras.text: Minuscule amounts of this are made and it’s powerful and weighty with a strong structure and earth character.

"A touch of wood spice adds a bit of breadth to the earthy and distinctly somber dark berry fruit nose that introduces precise, intense and energetic flavors that culminate in a firm and mineral-inflected finish. Like the Gevrey villages this is not likely to be a good candidate for early drinking."

title: Pierre Damoy Bourgogne Blanc Les Ravry

paras.text: The domaine does not grow Chardonnay, so they purchase grapes for this wine from the Ravry climat in Fixin. This wine is fresh and crisp as a result of fermenting the juice predominantly in stainless steel tanks, with a small percentage fermented in barrels for complexity and mouthfeel. These vines, rooted in clay-limestone soils, yield a pretty, mineral-driven wine accented by citrus and floral notes. The flavors display excellent structure and density and a long finish.

title: Pierre Damoy Chambertin ​​​​​​​Clos de Bèze Grand Cru Réserve

paras.text: Clos de Bèze Réserve, formerly Vielles Vignes : since 2002 a selection from old vines planted in 1920 in the far southern section of the Clos Only made in vintages when Pierre notices a definite superior level of quality . Always strictly limited availability.The wine is of monolithic proportions in the mouth beating all comers by its density , richness and length. 300→ 900 bottles maximum,

"A background touch of wood serves as a backdrop to the exuberantly spicy dark berry fruit, earth and soft floral nuances. There is good concentration to the powerful and mineral-driven broad-shouldered flavors that possess an abundance of palate coating dry extract that also buffers the very firm tannic spine on the balanced and strikingly persistent finish. This should be great in time but patience will definitely be required."

`Pierre Damoy has one of the largest holdings in Clos de Bèze, with 5 hectares. His prices are almost reasonable by the standards of the Grand Cru, and quality is high. Stylish, sexy and very smooth, this has that winning combination of sweet blackberry and black cherry fruit, excellent structure, appealing oak and a long, creamy finish. Drink 2018-30'

title: Pierre Damoy Chambolle-Musigny
Pierre Damoy Gevrey-Chambertin

paras.text: Gevrey-Chambertin, known to be sturdy and masculine, gained fame as Emperor Napoleon’s favorite wine and remains one of the best known. This bottling, which comes from four small plots in Gevrey-Chambertin, offers deep, ripe cherry aromas that lead to the round, plump mid-palate, structured tannins, and rich, lingering finish.

title: Pierre Damoy Gevrey-Chambertin Clos Tamisot

paras.text: Clos Tamisot, a 1.5-hectare monopole planted in 1922 and 1945, is referred to as Pierre’s

, as it is located right behind the Damoy family residence (it is also Pierre's favorite). The well-draining clay and limestone soil fosters intricate complexity in these very old vines’ small yields. A top site of Gevrey Villages. A wine that you would expect from the Gevrey Chambertin Appellation with its earthy, herbal nose and great depth and length. A litte bit of minerality makes the finish balanced and structured.

title: Pierre Damoy Marsannay Les Longeroies

paras.text: This is the most northerly appellation of the Côte d’Or, nearly reaching Dijon, and it encompasses three villages. Pierre Damoy purchases fruit from this vineyard and, as the site is vulnerable to hail damage, his choice of winemaking techniques varies according to the local vintage conditions. Starting with the 2013 vintage, he has added grapes from Marsannay La Bertinière, which lies on the southern side, closer to Fixin.
Dark, rich and explosive on the palate; saturated black-cherry aromas and flavors, with notes of tar, licorice and smoky oak.

Nice color. Impressive nose of black cherry jam, very pleasant. Mouth well made, lots of tannins, but quality flavor. Good length, it ends with a grain of tannin impressive for the appellation. Very long.

title: Domaine Pierre & Jean Baptiste Lebreuil Corton Charlemagne

paras.text: As it ages, the colour shifts towards yellow or amber. The bouquet, delicate in the extreme, features buttery notes of baked apple, citrus fruits, pineapple, lime, bracken, juniper, cinnamon, and flint. Honeyed notes are frequently present. The older vintages (25-30 years) reveal leather and truffle. Both the glass and the palate are filled with its powerful exhalations. Corton- Charlemagne is an astonishing demonstration of what the Chardonnay grape is capable of in terms of richness, power, concentration, distinction and balance. Rarely do we see such a perfect synthesis between grape variety and terroir.

title: Domaine Pierre & Jean Baptiste Lebreuil Savigny-les-Beaune

paras.text: Situation: 5 plots make up this appellation ranging from an altitude of 230 to 300 meters. 80% are between the hillsides of 1er cru below the village, the others are on the heights on less earthy soils.
Culture Mode: The estate obtained Reasoned agriculture certification in December 2008. No use of herbicide and insecticide since 2003. A reflection on bio-dynamism has been underway since 2011.
Harvest: Manual. The grapes are then transported in small boxes fairly quickly to avoid crushing the berries and the risk of oxidation.

Vinification: the harvest is completely sorted, destemmed before being put in tank or it will remain approximately fifteen days. Cold maceration (8 ° c), for 6/8 days with pumping over the juice. Follows the alcoholic fermentation for 8 to 10 days with punching down in order to extract the different components of the film. Separation of the drop and press juices, settling in order to eliminate the solid parts then entonnage (barrels).
Breeding: 12 months in oak barrels, 10% new. Aging on the lees, racking in July. Natural malolactic fermentation.
Bottling Process: Light filtration on earth. Bottling is done at the estate with our own bottling line in November-January.
Tasting Notes: Red fruits, finesse and concentration are the key words to define the qualities of this wine. Keeps 3 to 10 years.

title: Domaine Pierre-Marie Chermette Beaujolais Cuvee Traditionelle Vieilles Vignes

paras.text: Domaine Pierre-Marie Chermette Beaujolais Cuvee Traditionelle Vieilles Vignes | Fine Vines
Robe - crimson. Nose - intense ripe small red fruit including crushed strawberry and raspberry, sometimes a little hard liquorice at the end Palate - purity of fruit, freshness and finesse.

title: Domaine Pierre-Marie Chermette Beaujolais Origine Vielles Vignes

paras.text: This wine is emblematic Domaine du Vissoux where, from 1986, they wanted to bring back the Beaujolais of yesteryear. This cuvée is crafted to pure Beaujolais tradition: it does its Easter duty in big oak tuns, is fined using egg white, it is not chaptalised and undergoes only the lightest of filtering. The lively, intense fruitiness is very close to the grape itself. Concentration and freshness make this a Beaujolais with character.

title: Domaine Pierre & Jean Baptiste Lebreuil Savigny-les-Beaune "Aux Grands Liards"

paras.text: Domaine Pierre & Jean Baptiste Lebreuil Savigny-les-Beaune "Aux Grands Liards" | Fine Vines
Situation: in the heart of Savigny-les-Beaune, ideally located in climates classified as Premier Cru, facing south, slight slope.
Culture Mode: The estate obtained Reasoned agriculture certification in December 2008. No use of herbicide and insecticide since 2003. A reflection on bio-dynamism has been underway since 2011.
Manual. The grapes are then transported in small boxes fairly quickly to avoid crushing the berries and the risk of oxidation.

the harvest is completely sorted, destemmed before being put in tank or it will remain approximately fifteen days. Cold maceration (8 ° c), for 6/8 days with pumping over the juice. Follows the alcoholic fermentation for 8 to 10 days with punching down in order to extract the different components of the film. Separation of the drop and press juices, settling in order to eliminate the solid parts then entonnage (barrels).
Red fruits, finesse and concentration are the key words to define the qualities of this wine. Keeps 3 to 10 years.

title: Domaine Pierre-Marie Chermette Les Griottes Beaujolais Rosé

paras.text: Very original, Beaujolais rosé is great to surprise and impress your friends. Ideal for the summer months, friendly patio meals, relaxed barbecues in the garden and Asian cuisine. The pale pink robe with fuchsia notes is a surprising reminder of pomegranate seeds! Personality of the cuvée We started making rosé in 1985, at that time it was a real rarity in the Beaujolais region. Pierre-Marie has never made his rosé by bleeding (that is to say, drawing the juice off a vat of red Beaujolais to make it more concentrated) but has always vinified his as a wine in its own right. From the vine to the glass 1 hectare of Gamay in Le Bois d’Oingt, siliceous-clay soil giving light and fruity wines. Integrated vinegrowing, manual harvest, Guyot pruning. Vinification: a cuvée in its own right, with direct pressing after 1 to 2 days maceration depending on the year. No yeast seeding, no chaptalisation, minimum SO2, pneumatic pressing. Tasting notes Robe - pale, limpid pink. Nose - light floral and fruity aromas Palate - lip-smacking and round, notes of wild strawberry, blackberry, tart cherry, ending on a touch of star anise or pomegranate seed.

title: Domaine Pierre-Marie Chermette Moulin à Vent "Les Trois Roches"

paras.text: Purchased in 2002 by Martine and Pierre-Marie Chermette, the vineyard at La Rochelle overlooks the famous antique moulin à vent or windmill that gives the appellation its name. It is southeast facing with a subsoil rich in manganese, giving the wine quite a noble disposition.The three different plots of vines we use for this cuvée give a wine that is full and balanced: Rochegrès from 1ha. gives finesse, Roche Noire from 2 ha. gives liveliness and fruit while La Rochelle from 1.5ha. contributes power. The manganese-rich subsoil endows nobility on the whole resulting in an ‘all round’ Moulin à Vent that may be enjoyed from now for its fruity side or cellared to mature for up to 10 years. Integrated vinegrowing, goblet pruning, manual harvest at full ripeness Traditional Beaujolais vinification with “rack and return”, 10 to 12-day maceration in vats, no yeast seeding, no chaptalisation, minimum SO2, pneumatic pressing Maturing: half in tuns and half in 1 to 5-year-old barrels
Nose - floral bouquet, iris, violet, peony, red and black fruit, hints of vanilla.
Palate - concentration in finesse, tannins with a patina, creaminess, velvety suave texture, red and black cherry flesh, mineral and spicy vanilla notes to finish.

title: Domaine Pierre-Marie Chermette Fleurie Poncié

paras.text: From 4.5 hectares of a south-east facing slope called Poncié in the heights of Fleurie planted 35 years ago. It is so steep that no mechanisation at all is possible, but that results in a wine of feminie elegance and supple tannins. The soil is made up of pink granite rich in mica and quartz with a crumbly surface. Integrated vinegrowing, goblet pruning, manual harvest at full ripeness Traditional Beaujolais vinification Beaujolaise with “rack and return”, 10-day maceration in vats, no yeast seeding, no chaptalisation, minimum SO2, pneumatic pressing Maturing: 6 months in old oak tuns. This wine has a feminine personality, packed with finesse and suavity. Silky tannins, crimson tints and a floral iris, violet and rose bouquet with a peppery touch on the palate.
Palate - the silky Poncié tannins give suppleness, delicacy and elegance. Really flavourful. over and above red fruit, you will find notes of toast and undergrowth with an end that is often peppery.

title: Domaine Pierre Usseglio Châteauneuf du Pape

paras.text: Type of Soil: Sand, clay, limestone and rolled pebbles. This diversity of terroir allows us to obtain complex and balanced wines.

Vinification: Our red Châteauneuf-du-Pape is made in the traditional way. The vines are between 35 and 75 years old. The grapes harvested manually, are destemmed at 60%. Fermentation is followed by thermoregulation, it lasts 25 to 35 days.
Breeding: The wines are aged in oak barrels, in 1/2 muids, in concrete vats and barrels over a period of 12 months.
Tasting: Our Tradition has aromas of red fruits and black fruits; blackberry and blueberry, as well as spicy notes.
It is a concentrated and structured wine, it is a wine for aging. We recommend tasting it in 6-8 years.

title: Domaine Pierre Usseglio Châteauneuf du Pape Cuvée Mon Aieul

paras.text: Vinification: We make a plot selection to develop this cuvée. Only vines aged 75 to 90 years are used in the final assembly, they come from plots in La Crau, Les Bédines and Les Serres.
We did not do any destemming for this vintage and the vatting is followed by thermoregulation, it lasts from 30 to 40 days.
Breeding: The wines remain in concrete tanks in order to obtain an expressive fruitiness. BEST OF WINE: The optimal period for drinking is between 10 and 15 years.
Tasting: The “Cuvée de mon Aïeul” is a pure and concentrated wine. The nose is very complex with notes of raspberries, licorice and spices. It is a powerful wine with great elegance.

title: Domaine Pierre Usseglio Châteauneuf du Pape L'Unique

paras.text: Vinification: 25 days maceration in stainless steel vats and thermo-regulated concrete. Fully scuffed.
Tasting: The nose reveals notes of garrigue and black cherries, the mouth is intense with soft tannins. This wine is concentrated and charming.

title: Domaine Pierre Usseglio Châteauneuf du Pape Reserve Deux Frères

paras.text: Breeding: 50% of the wine is stored in demi-muids and 50% in new barrels of 2 to 3 wines.
Tasting: Ample, concentrated, this cuvée develops aromas of black fruits, licorice and smoky notes. The texture is smooth and the tannic structure requires a few years of aging.

title: Domaine Pierre Usseglio Lirac

paras.text: Vinification: The vines are around 40 years old. The grapes are harvested manually, the harvest is totally destemmed. Fermentation is followed by thermoregulation, it lasts from 20 to 30 days.
Breeding: The wines are aged in concrete tanks and demi-muids over a period of 12 months.
Tasting: The wine has aromas of spices, black fruit, cherry and liquorice. The tannins are dense, the mouth is fresh and elegant. It presents notes of jam and black cherries.

title: Domaine Ramonet Bourgogne Aligoté

paras.text: Aligoté is the second most planted grape variety in Burgundy, behind Chardonnay. This pure expression of the grape is pale white in color and high in acidity, with crisp, fresh notes of apple and lemon.
Fermentation: Vinification starts in tanks before the wine is transferred to French oak barrels. Stirring of the lees is done three to four times. Racking takes place after malolactic fermentation.

title: Domaine Rapet Savigny-Les-Beaune

paras.text: A great Burgundy red wine from the Savigny-les-Beaune commune. The grape variety used is Pinot Noir. This parcel is more than 50 years old. The name "Aux Fournaux" refers to the coal kilns of which remains have been found.

Red wine vinification: We aim to obtain fruity wines, rich in blended tannins, which is the mark of well ripened grapes. We bring in the grapes in small crates for careful sorting in the winery, a conveyor belt enabling us to fill the tanks without damaging the grapes. The fermentation lasts 15 days with pigeages, punching down of the cap, allowing the wine to soak up the richness and the colour from the grape-skins before pressing. Ageing takes place in barrels of which 20 % are new. Racking by the means of a bellow eliminates the need for a pump. All these precautions limit handling of the grapes and the wine as much as possible thus preserving all the richness.

The importance of this commune resides in the size of it's surface and the number of renowned climats*. Our Savigny-les-Beaune comes from the "les Fournaux" climat*, characterized by a deep and ferruginous ground. The wines are coloured, elegant, quite powerful, marked by a dominant of Morello cherries, black currant, raspberry, then subsequently developing notes of undergrowth after some years. Savigny-les-Beaune is delicate with discreet tannins.
* The term "climat" constitutes the Burgundy definition of "Terroir", in other words the specific geological and climatic conditions found on a defined plot of land.

title: Domaine Ratte Clos Maire Rouge

paras.text: The Clos Maire cuvée is the vinification of red Trousseau and Pinot Noir grapes from the same vine in complantation. The grapes are destemmed directly from the vineyard, manually, and the grains arrive intact in the winery: a semi-carbonic maceration gives this wine lots of freshness and exceptional fruitiness. Ideal with spicy dishes as well as red meats.

title: Domaine Ratte Savagnin Ouillé Naturé

paras.text: Naturé: old name of Savagnin. From plots planted on blue and gray marl soil. The grapes are harvested late, by hand, in order to have a sufficient degree for a better expression of their character. Long and delicate pressing, natural fermentation and bottling without filtration. It surprises with its aromatic palette, with a dominant floral and fresh. Goes well with fish and seafood, white meat and spicy curry dishes.

title: Domaine Ratte Trousseau "À la Dame"

paras.text: The special "Trousseau à la Dame", rarely seen, has small, loosely-knit clusters. The vines are grown on the Côteaux des Corvées, the best slope of Arbois for Trousseau, Marne du Lias, covered with eboulis calcaires.

title: Domaine Patrice Rion Chambolle-Musigny Premier Cru Les Fueés

paras.text: is one of 24 Premier Cru climats in the Burgundian commune of Chambolle-Musigny in the Cote de Nuits. Essentially a southern extension of the famed Bonnes

title: Domaine Robert Groffier Bourgogne Passetoutgrain

paras.text: The Bourgogne Passetoutgrain is a blend of 25% Gamay and 75% Pinot Noir. It has a fine, exuberant bouquet with veins of blue fruit and hints of pressed flowers. The palate is medium-bodied with a citrus-fresh opening and a sharp line of acidity that lends this Passetoutgrain good vigor, even if it cuts away a little swiftly on the finish.

title: Domaine Robert Groffier Bourgogne Pinot Noir

paras.text: Year after year the Domaine Robert Groffier produces wines that rank with the greatest in Burgundy. Not only are they elegant, rich and concentrated, but each "cru" truly reflects its respective "terroir". A high proportion of old vines, ... 40 years and more, as well as prime locations and constant attention to the vines during the growing season, all contribute to the greatness of the Groffier estate.

title: Domaine Robert Groffier Chambertin Clos-de-Bèze Grand Cru

paras.text: All the hundreds apply here: whole bunches, new wood and the age of the parcel. Built to last, this is a brilliant wine from Nicolas Groffier, which soars above the vintage conditions. It's subtle, complex and refined, with some of the latent power of the grand cru. Dense raspberry and black cherry fruit on the palate lead to a stylish, lingering finish.

The Chambertin Clos-de-Bèze Grand Cru contains 100% whole bunch fruit, matured entirely in new oak, which is barely noticeable on the nose, allowing the terroir to show through. Indeed, it is almost as difficult to discern the stem addition – a positive attribute, in my opinion. The fresh, taut palate is medium-bodied with fine tannin and quite linear in style, stricter than Les Amoureuses, with a more saline/marine-influenced finish that lingers in the mouth. Excellent, though I might have a soft spot for the Les Amoureuses and the Bonnes-Mares this year.

title: Domaine Robert Groffier Chambolle-Musigny Premier Cru Les Sentiers

paras.text: Enticing and complex aromas and flavors of wild berry, cherry, rose, sandalwood are married to a firm structure. The overall impression is one of harmony and finesse, with a lingering aftertaste.

The Gevrey-Chambertin 1er Cru Les Sentiers was touched by the frost and the old vines here suffered according to Nicolas Groffier. Due to depleted quantities it is 100% whole bunch fruit matured in one-third new oak. It has a lifted bouquet with blackberry, black cherry and hints of blue fruit, a subtle mineral tension underneath. The palate is medium-bodied with a strict, quite saline entry, rather peppery thanks to the stem addition. A structured but fresh finish that is complex and cerebral rather than willing to please at this early stage. Cellar this away for a decade and I believe it will repay your patience.

title: Domaine Robert Groffier Chambolle-Musigny Premier Cru Les Hauts-Doix

paras.text: Domaine Robert Groffier Chambolle-Musigny Premier Cru Les Hauts-Doix | Fine Vines

The Chambolle-Musigny 1er Cru Les Hauts-Doix, one-third whole bunch and new oak, was not touched by the frost according to Nicolas Groffier. It has a very fragrant, almost Vosne-like bouquet that is beautifully defined and disarmingly pure. The palate is very well balanced with fine tannin, a succinct line of acidity, extremely pure like the aromatics with a silky smooth finish that is utterly seductive and as elegant as you will find this vineyard. Superb.
Taut and focused, with black cherry and blackberry flavors fused to the bracing structure. Lithe and long, this adds spice and stone notes on the chalky finish.

title: Domaine Robert Groffier Chambolle-Musigny Premier Cru Les Amoureuses

paras.text: Domaine Robert Groffier Chambolle-Musigny Premier Cru Les Amoureuses | Fine Vines

The Chambolle-Musigny 1er Cru Les Amoureuses was matured in 15% new oak, a drastic reduction than previous vintages to express the terroir. It is 100% whole cluster fruit. It has another really quite bewitching bouquet with detailed black and red fruit, crushed violet, just a hint of vanilla pod in the background. The palate is medium-bodied with fine grain tannin, pure black cherry and blue fruit, outstanding mineralité and a pixelated, crystalline finish that beckons you back for another sip.

Effusive aromas of flowers, sandalwood, black currant and blackberry are allied to a delicate frame. Balanced in a slim way, with an open, silky texture and a long, mineral-tinged aftertaste. All about finesse.

title: Domaine Ramonet Bâtard-Montrachet

paras.text: One of the most renowned wines of Domaine Ramonet, Bâtard-Montrachet is produced from grapes grown in brown limestone soil that is heavy with clay. It is refined with beautiful acidity, and aromas of stone fruit and apple. We recommend serving this wine after it has aged for at least five to seven, or up to 20 years.
Fermentation: Vinification starts in tanks before the wine is transferred to French oak barrels. Stirring of the lees is done three to four times. Racking takes place after malolactic fermentation.

title: Domainie Robert Groffier Bonnes-Mares Grand Cru

paras.text: Bonnes Mares is a very exiting vineyard, as there is a lot of talented producers making wines from this large and complex grand cru. There are a lot of owners and plots on this vineyard, hence also relatively often a possibility to either rent a plot of buy grapes from this terroir. The ownership structure of Musigny is somewhat more static as is the case with the Vosne-Romanée Grand Crus – where the possibility to get a piece of land or grapes is very rare indeed.

Bonnes Mares is 15.05 ha – hence almost 40% larger than Musigny – and is located in both Chambolle Musigny and Morey-Saint-Denis. The main part is in Chambolle-Musigny – north of the village and Chambolle-Musigny Les Fuées – and only 1.52 ha of Bonnes Mares is located in the Morey appellation – just south of Clos de Tart – or actually inside Clos de Tart.

The true Bonnes Mares begins at the southern end of Clos de Tart – but actually there is a part of Bonnes Mares located within the enclosed walls of Clos des Tart – this part is now a part of Clos de Tart, although it’s named Bonnes Mares in the official cadastre (register of plots). The plot was included in Clos de Tart in 1966,

Bonnes Mares continues from Clos de s Tart to Chambolle Musigny Les Fuées and the village part of Chambolle Musigny Les Cras, with the top of the slope not being a part of Bonnes Mares but either village or the 1er cru part of Chambolle-Musigny Les Véroilles (a monopole of Domaine Ghislaine Barthod).

title: Domaine Robert Groffier Gevrey-Chambertin Les Seuvrées

paras.text: Healthy dark red. Aromas of black cherry, black raspberry, licorice, rock and game are slightly wild in an enticing way. At once rich and juicy in the mouth, with firm acidity giving the black fruit flavors a penetrating quality for the wine. This very concentrated village offering finishes with surprising length and firm mineral-driven acidity, and may be in the process of shutting down in bottle.

Gevrey Chambertin Seuvrees: 70% of the stems were included in the fermentation process, rich sweet fruit and very concentrated this has a 1er cru level of quality with extremely small yields of 20 HL/Ha. The vineyard is across from Mazoyeres Chambertin Grand Cru!

title: Maison Roy Dundee Hills Incline Chardonnay

paras.text: This Chardonnay showcases balanced tropical fruit including lychee, white peach, and Meyer lemon. A scintillating palate of concentrated peach and lemon flavors are supported by a bright acidity, focus and precision.

title: Bernard Rondeau Bugey Cerdon Methode Ancestral Rosé

paras.text: This is a delightful, slightly sweet sparkling rose wine from the tiny Cerdon de Bugey appellation in the Savoie region of France. It is made by a gentle, earnest hardworking husband and wife team who are raising their sweet children in their winery/home. Per the rules of the AOC, this sparkling rose Cerdon de Bugey is 100% Gamay Noir (Poulsard is also allowed to be blended with Gamay.) It is light in body and low in alcohol (7%) making it ideal to drink as an aperitif or with fruity desserts or beignets with powdered sugar (which we got to taste right out of the oven when we visited them).

As Charles Neal says, "this is literally like a strawberry parfait in a glass. At about 40 grams of residual sugar, the wine does have some perceptible sweetness; however, with the very delicate tannin of Gamay and the supporting acidity, the wine comes across as being less sweet than it actually is."

title: Maison Roy Incline Pinot Noir Dundee Hills

paras.text: Aromatically the Incline Dundee Pinot Noir shows cranberry, red rose, pie cherry and a slate-like minerality. The palate is broad, supple and concentrated, with lots of red and black fruit and a medium plus body. The wine has a great freshness and precision, framed by a low alcohol level. The tannins and bright acidity are integrated and soft allowing the prime drinking window to be around 2020-2028.

Beautiful depth and purity here, this is an elite pinot in all respects. Complex, spicy and meaty notes abound with ripe dark-cherry aromas holding court. The palate has a silky, long and succulent feel with impressively concentrated dark cherries.

title: Maison Roy Petite Incline Pinot Noir

paras.text: The Petite Incline is our “nod to nouveau”. It is a beautiful pop and pour wine that is early accessible with very aromatically intense red rose, strawberry and baking spice. The tannins and body are light, balanced and accessible. This wine is in its best drinking window now through 2021.

Vivid red. Fresh red berries and peppery spices on the nose, with a hint of rhubarb in the background. Taut, focused flavors of bitter cherry and redcurrant open slowly with air. Shows good energy and a slightly edgy quality on the youthfully tannic finish, with the redcurrant and spice notes echoing.

title: Domaine Saint-Rémy Gewurztraminer Grand Cru Hengst

paras.text: Golden color, superb. All in aromatic power, all in structure and aromas, on the nose of fresh berries, musk and nuts, full and persistent, really very racy, full on the nose and on the palate.

title: Domaine Saint-Rémy Gewurztraminer Vieilles Vignes

paras.text: Elegant nose of rose and cloves. Fruity, round and full-bodied supported by a pleasant freshness. To be served as an aperitif, with Asian dishes, strong cheeses, as well as fruit tarts.

title: Domaine Saint-Rémy Pinot Blanc

paras.text: This variety is tender and delicate, it combines freshness and suppleness to represent a happy medium in the range of Alsace wines. With great power and remarkable fruitiness, the wines of Val Saint Grégoire present a sumptuous balance.

In the mouth while being dry, it gives off a roundness, a subtlety and a reserve of good quality. It has an enveloping persistence in the mouth but which is never excessive. Suitable for terrines, pâtés, various salads.

title: Domaine Saint-Rémy Pinot Gris Grand Cru Brand

paras.text: Born on a hillside with warm granite soils overlooking Turckheim, this Pinot Gris blends scents of honey and candied citrus.

Southeast exposure, it rises to an altitude of 380m. Resting on a substrate of granite known as Turckheim, with two weathered mica, it offers a sandy and coarse soil. These aromas explode on the palate supported by a fairly fresh structure which gives the wine a dashing youthful appearance and which will allow it to wait two or three years. This mellow will go well with a pan-fried foie gras with mandarins or a cooked cheese.

title: Domaine Saint-Rémy Pinot Gris Reserve

paras.text: Beautiful bright yellow color, nose on fruity aromas of peach, pineapple and acacia flowers. The attack is supple with a good structure. The finish is persistent and aromatic. Balanced wine.

title: Domaine Saint-Rémy Riesling Grand Cru Schlossberg

paras.text: One can expect delicious fresh fruity flavours from this fantastic quality Riesling. Aromas of white stone fruits and citrus fruits. This is restrained and finely balanced. Its delicate stone fruit and citrus notes gain comlexity from a subtle, insistent stoniness, a character derived from the site's sandy, siliceous soil. The slight sweetness is managed well, and the flavors persist with length and poise. The acidic siliceous soil has excellent fertility and is mineral rich, thus determining the finesse and aromas in the wines from Domaine St Remy

title: Domaine Saint-Rémy Riesling Jade

paras.text: With notes of ripe yellow fruits, a tender and caressing impression: a wine of delicacy.
This Riesling is Mineral with a well marked and structured acidity, it will gain in complexity as it ages (between 5 and 8 years) it excels with fish and shellfish.

Alluvial soil of the Fecht alluvial fan located on the banks of Turckheim. The sandy alluviums are rich in clay (22%) and free from limestone. These alluvial-siliceous soils outcrop and are locally covered with deposits or loessic silt.

title: Domaine Séguinot Bordet Chablis

paras.text: Very pretty pale golden yellow in colour with light greenish glints. Bright, luminous and limpid. The Nose is reminiscent of the scented freshness of a lovely summer's morning. The taste is perfect harmony of maturity, mellowness and vivacity. The flowers and fruit reappear, enhanced by charming biscuity notes. The mineral touch, fine and airy, shows through well on the finish to accompany our thirst and pleasure right to the end.

title: Schoffit Riesling Harth Tradition

paras.text: Viticulture was reported around the town of Colmar as early as the 9th century and the name Harth is first mentioned in official documents in 1259. This vineyard enjoys maximum sunlight until late in the evening thanks to its location at the exit of a valley, and its very draining soil which heats very quickly induces a regular and homogeneous maturation of the grapes. Riesling grown here is particularly expressive and mineral, with about 6g/L residual sugar and 7g/L natural acidity depending on the vintage, and is always marked by opulent fruit and a very ripe acidity.

title: Domaine Séguinot Bordet Chablis Premier Cru Les Vaillons

paras.text: The nose is a tornado of fresh perfumed flowers, leading the way to a summer fruit platter of peaches, pears and melon.
Flowers and fruit compete in harmony with great balance achieved by fresh acidity.

title: Domaine Sérafin Père et Fils Bourgogne Rouge

paras.text: The Bourgogne Rouge vines all adjoin appellation Gevrey. Elevage 50% new oak, 50% one vintage used.

title: Domaine Sérafin Père et Fils Chambolle-Musigny Premier Cru Les Baudes

paras.text: Domaine Sérafin Père et Fils Chambolle-Musigny Premier Cru Les Baudes | Fine Vines
The Chambolle-Musigny 1er cru Les Baudes parcel lies directly below and is separated from Bonnes Mares only by the Route des Grand Crus. 40 year old vines. 100% new oak elevage.

title: Domaine Sérafin Père et Fils Charmes-Chambertin Grand Cru

paras.text: The Charmes-Chambertin Grand Cru is from two parcels, one in Charmes and one in Mazoyeres. Average age of the two parcels, both similar dates of planting is 75 years. 100% new oak elevage.

The Charmes Chambertin Grand Cru, from vines just under 80 years old, has an intense bouquet: macerated black cherries, boysenberry and bilberry fruit underneath a carapace of new oak. The palate is medium-bodied with quite rigid tannins for a Charmes-Chambertin. It feels long in the mouth, quite assertive and determined to make an impressive. Fortunately it pulls back toward the finish so that it is not overpowering.

title: Domaine Sérafin Père et Fils Gevrey-Chambertin AOC

paras.text: The Gevrey-Chambertin vines are from different areas of the appellation, both sides of the Route Nationale. Generally 70% new oak, though some years (2012 and 2013) 100%.

title: Domaine Sérafin Père et Fils Gevrey-Chambertin Premier Cru Les Corbeaux

paras.text: Domaine Sérafin Père et Fils Gevrey-Chambertin Premier Cru Les Corbeaux | Fine Vines

The Gevrey-Chambertin Les Corbeaux is rather exuberant in its up-front fruit, but that first impression dissipates a bit as the wine finds its sense of classicism with time in the glass. The Corbeaux possesses gorgeous mid-palate pliancy with an underpinning of firm tannin that will allow it to age gracefully for a number of years.
The Gevrey-Chambertin 1er Cru Les Corbeaux is one parcel near Mazis-Chambertin. Vines 48 years old. 100% new oak elevage.

title: Domaine Sérafin Père et Fils Gevrey-Chambertin Premier Cru Le Fonteny

paras.text: Domaine Sérafin Père et Fils Gevrey-Chambertin Premier Cru Le Fonteny | Fine Vines

The Gevrey-Chambertin 1er Cru Fonteny is a 55 year old parcel has the same exposition as Serafin's Grenad Cru and is located just to the north and almost adjoining Ruchottes Chambertin. 100% new oak elevage.

A gorgeous Gevrey, this exudes floral and sweet berry aromas that lead a beam of cherry flavor, with notes of blackberry, spice and mineral. This seems pretty for the appellation, yet there's density and grip to its tannins. Best from 2013 through 2027.

title: Domaine Sérafin Père et Fils Gevrey-Chambertin Premier Cru Les Cazetiers

paras.text: Domaine Sérafin Père et Fils Gevrey-Chambertin Premier Cru Les Cazetiers | Fine Vines

The Gevrey-Chambertin 1er Crus Les Cazetiers is "the Clos St. Jacques of Serafin" as it is on the same slope above the village of Gevrey and with an exposition similar to the Grands Crus. Vines are 60 years old. 100% new oak elevage.

A tart melange of fresh red and black raspberries joins with smoked meat and bitter dark chocolate in Serafin’s lean, long, bright, and multi-registered Gevrey-Chambertin Les Cazetiers. Here is an instance of more than enough stamina, refreshment, and fine tannic underpinnings allied to sufficient sweet, sappy primary fruit, a combination one finds too seldom. Hints of vanilla and licorice add allure to a long finish.

title: Domaine Sérafin Père et Fils Gevrey-Chambertin Vieilles Vignes

paras.text: The Gevrey-Chambertin V.V. is a selection of Serafin’s best-situated Gevrey parcels, all of which adjoin either 1er cru or Grand Cru vineyards. All over 50 years old, average age 65 years. 100% new oak elevage.

title: Domaine Sérafin Père et Fils Morey St Denis Premier Cru Les Millandes

paras.text: Domaine Sérafin Père et Fils Morey St Denis Premier Cru Les Millandes | Fine Vines
The Morey-St. Denis 1er Crus Les Millandes parcel is just below Clos de la Roche and adjoining, separated only by the Route des Grand Crus. Vines are 48 years old. 100% new oak elevage.

title: Domaine Sérol Côte Roannaise Rouge Chez Blondin

paras.text: Terroir: Middle of the Chez Blondin lieu-dit, steep, southwest-facing hillside, 8,500 vines per ha density
Vinification: 100% de-stemmed, indigenous yeast fermentation, 6 months maceration, all in amphora. Pressed by hand. Aged for6 months in amphora, no added sulfur.

title: Domaine Sérol Côte Roannaise Rouge Éclat De Granite

paras.text: Intense dark red colour. Aromas of red fruits (black currant raspberry) typical of Gamay. Mineral and spicy nose. Mouth with silky tannins which give suppleness, strength and length to the wine

This cuvée is similar to Les Originelles in that it is from a blend of different vineyards and that the amount produced and vineyards that it is sourced from vary from year to year. Its identity comes from the granitic soils in each terroir and the older vine ages: while the youngest vines may be only 10 years old, some of the domaine's oldest vines give their fruit to this cuvée as well. More entrenched vine root systems add complexity and the granite soils are the hallmark of the Sérol's terroir.

This terroir has a high plantation density: 8,500 vines/hectare. Soils are plowed and the vines are nourished with natural organic matter. Careful work in the vineyards is carried out to maintain yields including: pruning, de-budding, trellising, de-leafing.
Terroir: Mix of elevations and exposures, with soil of granite rocks and fine granite gravel
Vinification: 40% de-stemmed, indigenous yeast fermentation. Aged for 6 months in cement tank, light filtration.

title: Domaine Sérol Côte Roannaise Rouge Les Blondins

paras.text: Michel Troisgros (local Michelin-starred chef) and Stéphane Sérol cultivate and vinify this vineyard together as a separate wine from the Domaine Sérol range. It was originally planted by their fathers more than 20 years ago. The soil is perfectly adapted to the local grape variety (Gamay Saint-Romain). Vines are planted at a high density (8,500 per hectare). Grass and other cover-crop maintained with added natural organic matter and soil is worked with machine while other tasks (de-budding, de-leafing) are by hand.
Terroir: Steep, south-facing hill with a cow pasture below, fairly-shallow porphyry soil, hard granite bedrock with narrow fissures.
Vinification: 40% de-stemmed, indigenous yeast fermentation. Aged for 6 months in cement tank (70%) and barrel (30%), light filtration.

title: Domaine Sérol Turbullent Rosé Pétillant

paras.text: In mouth, the aromatic expression of Gamay is emphasized by the finesse of bubbles
Healthy soils are maintained by plowing under the rows, bringing in organic compost, and encouraging a limited cover crop. Bud and leaf removal is done by hand to limit yield and ensure quality.

Vinification: Pressed directly, cool settling, indigenous yeast alcoholic fermentation in tank at low temperature. Méthode ancestrale: bottling at 7% alc., fermentation continues, finishing at 9% alc. with 5 bars of pressure. Disgorged.

title: Domaine Servin Chablis Grand Cru Les Clos

paras.text: A .88 Ha parcel on the right side of the Serein River, South/South West facing, the Les Clos profits with perfect sun exposure. Often quoted as being the King of the Chablis Grands Crus. Complex and powerful with a perfect balance, this wine which is vinified in the traditional Burgundian style; 100% traditional oak fermentation and ageing in 3-9 year old oak casks. Entirely hand-harvested.

Description: Often quoted as being the King of the Chablis Grands Crus. This vineyard produces the best qualities of all the other Grand Crus vineyards. Complex and powerful with a perfect balance, this wine which is vinified in the traditional Burgundian style (100 % oak fermented and aged). A Grand Cru that will reward you with long term ageing.
Situation géographique: Right side of the Serein River. South/South West facing, the Les Clos profits with perfect sun exposure.

Terroir: Lime-clay soils are dominant here, but the geological originality of appellation Chablis resides in its sub-strata, often quite near the surface, of kimmeridgean limestone, formed by billions of tiny fossilised oyster shells called ostrea virgule.

title: Domaine Servin Chablis Grand Cru Les Preuses

paras.text: A .7ha parcel on the right side of the Serein River. A complex wine, striking a keen balance between mineral aromas and explosive flavours on the palate. Capable of being the best of the Chablis Grands Crus it is one of the most respected and offers exceptional ageing capacity. 100% hand-harvested. Static settling. All fermentations done in stainless steel tanks and 40% matured in oak barrels for 20 months.

Description: A complex wine, striking a keen balance between mineral aromas and explosive flavours on the palate. Capable of being the best of the Chablis Grands Crus it is one of the most respected. Les Preuses offers an exceptional ageing capacity.

Terroir: Lime-clay soils are dominant here, but the geological originality of appellation Chablis resides in its sub-strata, often quite near the surface, of kimmeridgean limestone, formed by billions of tiny fossilised oyster shells called ostrea virgule.

title: Domaine Servin Chablis Les Pargues

paras.text: Les Pargues sits between the official Premier Cru vineyards of Montmains and Vaillons. 50 year old vines deliver wine of impressive concentration. François Servin certainly lavishes Premier Cru attention on this wine, ensuring the honeyed minerality of great Chablis and years of pleasure ahead.

title: Domaine Servin Chablis Premier Cru Les Butteaux

paras.text: From the left side of the Serein, situated on a steep flank of the hill of Montmains, above and to the west of les Forets, lies the 1er cru Butteaux. Servin’s tiny parcel of Butteaux adjoins that of Raveneau.

Old vines, perfect exposition, and extremely rocky Kimmeridgian soil composition, make Butteaux a special wine, and one that is perhaps unsurpassed even by the Grand Cru for its expressiveness of character.

title: Domaine Servin Chablis Premier Cru Mont De Milieu

paras.text: From the right side of the Serein River. The “Mont de Milieu” vineyard is the hill after the “Montée de Tonnerre” vineyard and is near the village of Fyé. Situated with the same quality exposure as the Grands Crus, the Mont de Milieu vineyard produces ripe, rich and full bodied wines blended with floral and mineral notes. Regarded as one of the best Premiers Crus in Chablis. Lime-clay soils with Kimmeridgian fossils. Fermentation and maturing in stainless steel tanks.

title: Domaine Servin Chablis Premier Cru Montée de Tonnerre

paras.text: From the right side of the Serein River, situated right next to the Grand Cru Blanchot. A soft and elegant wine, the Montée de Tonnerre is situated in the same line as the Grand Crus. The notable white clay helps to develop intense fruit and floral aromas. The older vines add the depth and complexity in the mouth. Regarded by many as the best and most consistent Premier Cru in Chablis. Lime-clay soils with Kimmeridgian fossils. Fermentation and maturing in stainless steel tanks.

Description: A soft and elegant wine, the Montée de Tonnerre is situated in the same line as the Grand Crus. The notable white clay helps to develop intense fruit and floral aromas. The older vines add the depth and complexity in the mouth. Regarded by many as the best and most consistent Premier Cru in Chablis
Situation géographique: Right side of the Serein River. Situated right next to the Grand Cru Blanchot.

Terroir: Lime-clay soils are dominant here, but the geological originality of appellation Chablis resides in its sub-strata, often quite near the surface, of kimmeridgean limestone, formed by billions of tiny fossilised oyster shells called ostrea virgule.

title: Domaine Servin Chablis Premier Cru Vaillons

paras.text: From the left side of the Serein River, the Vaillons wine is made from the vineyards “Châtains”, “Côte Vaillons”, “Epinottes”, “Les Roncières” and “Sécher”. The Vaillons shows the classic Chablis style with dry mineral aromas. Vivid and intense, the vibrant energy is blended with ripe white fruit aromas. Lime-clay soils with Kimmeridgian fossils. Fermentation and maturing in stainless steel tanks.

Domaine Servin is a prominent estate with 32 hectares of vines across the unique terroir of Chablis, where the rich, old, limestone clay soils and the cool climate produce one of the world's finest Chardonnays. Seventh generation winemaker François Servin has crafted a classic Premier Cru in 2011 - a stylish, full-bodied wine to savour with fine cuisine from oysters to blanquette de veau.

title: Domaine Servin Chablis Premier Cru Vaucoupin

paras.text: From the right side of the Serein River, the “Vaucoupin” vineyard is the hill after the “Montée de Tonnerre” and “Mont de Milieu”, and is near the village of Chichee. Situated with the same quality exposure as the Grands Crus, the Vaucoupin produces rich, ripe fruit blended with soft mineral and stone aromas. Lime-clay soils with Kimmeridgian fossils. Fermentation and maturing in stainless steel tanks.

title: Domaine Sylvain Cathiard Chambolle-Musigny Les Clos de l’Orme

paras.text: Vinification: 100% de-stemmed, 20-30 days in tank, indigenous yeast fermentation. Aged for 15-18 months in barrel (50% new).

title: Domaine Sylvain Cathiard Romanée-Saint-Vivant Grand Cru

paras.text: Vinification: 100% de-stemmed, 20-30 days in tank, indigenous yeast fermentation. Aged for 15-18 months in barrel (67% new oak).

title: Domaine Sylvain Cathiard Nuits-Saint-Georges Premier Cru Aux Murgers

paras.text: Domaine Sylvain Cathiard Nuits-Saint-Georges Premier Cru Aux Murgers | Fine Vines
Vinification: 100% de-stemmed, 20-30 days in tank, indigenous yeast fermentation. Aged for 15-18 months in barrel (60% new oak).

title: Domaine Sylvain Cathiard Vosne-Romanée

paras.text: Vinification: 100% de-stemmed, 20-30 days in tank, indigenous yeast fermentation. Aged for 15-18 months in barrel (50% new).

title: Domaine Sylvain Cathiard Vosne-Romanée Premier Cru Aux Reignots

paras.text: Vinification: 100% de-stemmed, 20-30 days in tank, indigenous yeast fermentation. Aged for 15-18 months in barrel (50-60% new oak).

title: Domaine Sylvain Cathiard Vosne-Romanée Premier Cru Aux Malconsorts

paras.text: Vinification: 100% de-stemmed, indigenous yeast fermentation. Aged for 18 months in barrel (67% new oak).

title: Domaine Sylvain Cathiard Vosne-Romanée Premier Cru Les Suchots

paras.text: Terroir: Soil is shallow and rocky at top of slope, slightly richer and more humid at bottom
Vinification: 100% de-stemmed, 20-30 days in tank, indigenous yeast fermentation. Aged for 15-18 months in barrel (67% new oak).

title: Domaine Sylvain Langoureau Bourgogne Aligoté

paras.text: History : Domaine Sylvain LANGOUREAU is family domaine that was taken over by Sylvain in 1988. Mainly doing Chardonnay on the village of Saint Aubin, Chassagne Mt, Puligny Mt and Meursault. In total, 16 appellations are done.

paras.text: Domaine Sylvain Langoureau Puligny Montrachet Premier Cru La Garenne | Fine Vines

title: Domaine Sylvain Langoureau Saint Aubin Premier Cru En Remilly

title: Domaine Sylvain Pataille Bourgogne Aligoté

paras.text: Terroir: 60% from Champ Forey (limestone and gravel soil), 40% from Auvonnes (clay, marl soil with small stones)
Vinification: Directly pressed, indigenous yeast alcoholic fermentation 2/3 in older barrels, 1/3 in tank. 1 year aging, minimal sulfur, added only at bottling.

title: Domaine Sylvain Pataille Bourgogne Pinot Noir

paras.text: Vinification: 0-15% whole cluster, indigenous yeasts, gentle extraction. 10-12 months' aging in barrel (15% new), low sulfur additions.

title: Domaine Sylvain Pataille Marsannay

paras.text: Vinification: 30% whole-cluster, indigenous yeast fermentation. Aged for 18 months in older oak barrels, low sulfur additions at bottling.

title: Domaine Sylvain Pataille Marsannay Clos Du Roy

paras.text: Terroir: Approximately 280m altitude, east-facing, well-draining red soils with lots of iron, chalky limestone substrate
Vinification: 5 to 7 hours' pressing in vertical press, 6 months' indigenous yeast alcoholic fermentation and 24 months' aging in older 350L barrels, minimal sulfur added only at bottling.

title: Domaine Sylvain Pataille Marsannay La Montagne

paras.text: Terroir: Top of south-facing hill, 315m altitude, 3-12% slope, shallow soil with limestone rocks (Comblanchien; Prémeaux, oolite limestone substratum)
Vinification: 100% whole cluster, indigenous yeast alcoholic fermentation. 18 months' aging, minimal sulfur addition only at bottling.

title: Domaine Sylvain Pataille Marsannay En Clémengeots

paras.text: Terroir: Couchey, specifically in the lieu-dit Au Champ Salomon at 282-315m altitude, 2-8% slope, east/ southeast-facing, red clay soils.
Vinification: 100% de-stemmed, indigenous yeast alcoholic fermentation, 18 months' aging in barrel (15% new), low sulfur addition only at bottling.

Cle could come from the word Claie, which comes from the medieval Latin word for wood trellis, CLIDA. CLIDA designates an openwork fence structure with intertwined wood that consists of posts driven into the ground.
Mongeot could be a Burgundian diminutive of ancient French Monge (monk or solitary). Monge —from the imperial Latin word MONAHUS (monk, solitary).
Source: The Climats and Lieux-Dits of the Great Vineyards of Burgundy, Marie-Hélène Landrieu-Lussigny.

Site: En Clemengeot sits at the northern border of Couchey toward the bottom of the slope at 280-meters elevation. The slope is very gentle and faces east. A small combe to the northwest provides cool air.

title: Domaine Testut Chablis Grand Cru Grenouille

paras.text: Rich and powerful. A strong mineral palate balances the power of the ripe fruit. A wine that will show full potential in 5 to 8 years.

title: Domaine Testut Chablis Premier Cru Forêts

paras.text: Our oldest vine, on the left bank facing east, produces an impressive maturity with notes of acacia honey, grape and apricot that complements a long and beautiful minerality. A rich and fragrant wine to drink with a capon or a turbot.

title: Domaine Testut Chablis Premier Cru Montée de Tonnerre

paras.text: Powerful and complex. The Montee de Tonnerre is often quoted as the best 1er Crus in Chablis. Situated next to the Grand Crus its superior exposition gives the wine consistency each and every year.

title: Domaine Thomas & Fils Sancerre Le Pierrier

paras.text: A mineral-driven style of Sancerre with that classic flinty nose, this wine has broad appeal with a clean, refined character and balanced pyrazines (pyrazines give you those herbal grassy notes).
Perfect with white fish and fresh summer vegetables, this is also a classic pairing with creamy goat cheese.

Sauvignon Blanc is one of the most popular white grapes in the world, second only to Chardonnay. Without question, Sancerre is the most prestigious region for this grape due to the soil, climate, and history of the region. Naturally high in pyrazines, Sauvignon Blanc tends to exhibit herbaceous and green notes ranging from fresh cut grass to jalapenos and gooseberry. High in natural acidity the tart citrus fruits are also a major component to the wines flavor, especially when the grapes are grown in a cool climate like Sancerre.

title: Domaine Vacheron Sancerre
Domaine Vacheron Sancerre Belle Dame

paras.text: Hand harvested, natural yeast fermentation in French oak vats, pigeage, 30 day maceration

title: Domaine Vacheron Sancerre Guigne Chevres
Domaine Vacheron Sancerre Les Romains
Domaine Vacheron Sancerre Rouge
Domaine Violot-Guillemard Chassagne Montrachet

paras.text: In the southern part of the Côte de Beaune Chassagne-Montrachet is an appellation consisting of 350 ha (865 acres) of clayish limestone and shares with Puligny the uncontested title of the prince of the world's dry white wines.

title: Domaine José Dhondt Mes Vieilles Vignes Brut Blanc de Blancs

paras.text: Light gold. Intense, mineral-driven aromas of nectarine, honeydew, chalk and white flowers, with a spicy topnote. Sappy pit fruit flavors are enlivened by notes of ginger and orange zest, turning increasingly tangy with air. Finishes linear and firm, with lingering spiciness and excellent clarity. This is still a baby but holds real promise.

title: Virgile Lignier-Michelot Bourgogne Pinot Noir

paras.text: Lignier’s vineyard is located below Clos Vougeot. The wine was 100% de-stemmed, and aged on its fine lees for 12 months in mostly used wood, followed by 3 months in tank prior to bottling to both settle and focus the wine. The nose displays enticing, spicy, red and black fruits. On the palate there is good density and flesh, with tannins buried in the fruit.
Vinification: 20-25% whole-cluster, cold maceration, indigenous yeast fermentation. Aged for 12 months in barrel (20-30% new), unfiltered.

title: Virgile Lignier-Michelot Chambolle-Musigny Premier Cru Cuvée Jules

paras.text: Terroir: Central and southern parts of Chambolle: Les Sentiers (brown soil with small stones), Les Chabiots, Les Chatelots
Vinification: 80% whole-cluster, cold maceration. Aged for 12 months in barrel (20-30% new), gentle white earth filtration.

title: Virgile Lignier-Michelot Chambolle-Musigny Vieilles Vignes

paras.text: Pinot noir with heavy tastes of mineral and red fruits. The color is very bright and the nose has hints of flowers. The limestone soil that the wine is grown on is very prevelant on the palate along with the elegance of most Chambolle Musigny wines
Terroir: 2 parcels: Les Drazey (below Bonnes Mares with mostly limestone soils), Les Gamaires (deep clay soil)
Vinification: 50% whole-cluster, short cold maceration. Aged for 12 months in barrel (20% new), light white-earth filtration of bottom 2/3 of tank.

title: Virgile Lignier-Michelot Charmes-Chambertin Grand Cru

paras.text: Terroir: Red topsoil (oxidized iron), limestone pebbles, high active chalk in bedrock
Vinification: Whole-cluster pressing, cold maceration, rapid de-vatting. Aged for 12 months in barrel (80-100% new), 5 months settling in tank, unfiltered.

title: Virgile Lignier-Michelot Clos de la Roche Grand Cru

paras.text: For his own vines, he finds this parcel too dangerous to work with the typical Burgundian
, so soils are plowed by horse and any treatments are carried out with a lower caterpillar, which he borrows from a vigneron friend.
Terroir: Multiple small parcels bordering Les Monts Luisants, shallow soil (30cm) mostly limestone with large stones and some small rocks.
Vinification: 50% whole-cluster, short cold maceration before fermentation, rapid de-vatting. Aged for 12 months in barrel (80-100% new), 5 months settling in tank, unfined.

title: Virgile Lignier-Michelot Clos Saint-Denis Grand Cru

paras.text: The Clos St. Denis is gorgeous. Layers of dark fruit, minerals, spices and licorice take shape in this striking, multi-dimensional Burgundy. The Clos St. Denis is at once powerful yet also delicate, but ultimately it is the more refined side of the wine's personality that comes through most eloquently. The creamy, expansive finish is totally striking. The Clos St. Denis is made from equal parts estate and purchased grapes. This cuvée is made from purchased fruit.
Terroir: Bottom of slope, shallow brown rocky limestone soils, higher phosphorous and clay content
Vinification: 40-50% whole-cluster, short cold maceration before fermentation, rapid de-vatting. Aged for 12 months in barrel (80-100% new) 3 months settling in tank, unfiltered.

title: Virgile Lignier-Michelot Gevrey-Chambertin Cuvée Bertin

paras.text: Terroir: Early-ripening lieux-dits: Les Seuvrées (on the Morey side of the village, sandier soil), Les Murots (soils with many small chalky rocks)
Vinification: 50% whole-cluster, short cold maceration. Aged for 12 months in barrel (30% new), unfiltered.

title: Virgile Lignier-Michelot Morey-Saint-Denis Premier Cru Aux Chezeaux

paras.text: This Pinot Noir is a true treat! Has aromas of wood, and a slight mineral palate. The finish is very elegant and smooth. This wine will age very well.

Vinification: 60-80% whole-cluster, short cold maceration before fermentation, rapid de-vatting. Aged for 12 months on fine lees in barrel (20-30% new), 3 months settling in tank, gentle white earth filtration.
Guyot and Cordon pruning with high trellising and careful plowing. Since 2010, work in the vineyards and in the cellar follows the lunar calendar.
Unfortunately, 2016 is the last vintage that Virgile made this wine, because his purchasing contract ended in 2017.

title: Virgile Lignier-Michelot Morey-Saint-Denis Premier Cru Aux Charmes

paras.text: Vinification: 50% whole-cluster, cold maceration before fermentation. Aged for 12 months in barrel (30% new), 3 months settling in tank, gentle white earth filtration.
Cru is thus named because it is a small continuation of the Gevrey-Chambertin Grand Cru Les Mazoyères, which may also be called Charmes.
The vineyard is pruned to Guyot and Cordon, with higher trellising and careful plowing. Since 2010, viticultural and cellar work are carried out according to the lunar calendar.

title: Virgile Lignier-Michelot Morey-Saint-Denis Premier Cru Les Faconnières

paras.text: Virgile Lignier-Michelot Morey-Saint-Denis Premier Cru Les Faconnières | Fine Vines
For Virgile, this terroir, especially the soils, are worthy of Grand Cru status. "You just can't make bad wine here."
The name of this parcel refers to the falcons that circle around the vineyard. Work in all of Virgile's vines and the cellar has been carried out in function of the lunar cycle since 2010.
Vinification: 50% de-stemmed, cold pre-fermentation maceration, rapid de-vatting. Aged for 12 months on fine lees in barrel (30% new), 5 months settling in tank, unfiltered.

title: Virgile Lignier-Michelot Morey-Saint-Denis Vieilles Vignes

paras.text: This old vines blend is from 3 different lieux-dits in Morey-Saint-Denis. 50% of the fruit is from Les Cognées, 25% from Très Girard, 25% from Les Chenevery.
This comes from 3 plots with an average vine age of 40 years. This is a delicious village with pureed plum and spice fruit and fresh tangy personality. Good powdery tannins and length.
Terroir: Three vineyards with deep clay, sand, and gravel soils and clay-limestone bedrock from the Middle Jurassic
Vinification: 70% whole-cluster, short cold maceration, indigenous yeast fermentation. Aged for 12 months in oak barrel (30% new).

title: Virgile Lignier-Michelot Morey-Saint-Denis Premier Cru Les Chenevery

paras.text: Virgile Lignier-Michelot Morey-Saint-Denis Premier Cru Les Chenevery | Fine Vines
Guyot and Cordon pruning, with higher trellising and careful plowing. Since 2010, work in the vineyards and cellar is carried out in function of the lunar cycle.
An elegant wine with an extremely long and wonderful finish. 125 cases made on average on the .3 ha big vineyard known as les Chenevery. The vines are between 55 and 60 years old.
Terroir: Below Faconnières on the hill, soils with higher limestone content from the bedrock which resurfaces in some areas
Vinification: 20-50% de-stemmed, short cold pre-fermentation maceration, rapid de-vatting. Aged for 12 months in barrel (30% new), 3 months settling in tank, gentle white earth filtration.

title: Virgile Lignier-Michelot Nuits-Saint-Georges Premier Cru Les Murgers

paras.text: Virgile Lignier-Michelot Nuits-Saint-Georges Premier Cru Les Murgers | Fine Vines
Terroir: Northern Nuits-St-Georges, moderate slope, light-colored sand and gravel soil
Vinification: 50% whole-cluster, short cold maceration before fermentation, rapid de-vatting. Aged for 12 months in barrel (30% new), 5 months settling in tank, unfiltered.
Additional Info: This cuvée is made from purchased grapes. Work in the cellar is in function of the lunar cycle.

title: Domaine Vocoret Chablis

paras.text: Since 1867, the Vocorets have been growing vines on the clay-chalk hillsides of Chablis,
producing wines of pedigree, authenticity and consistency. Although challenging, the cool climate of the region gives the grape a signature high acidity, crisp balance, and bright mineral expression.

The nose is fresh and crisp with green apple, green pear, citrus (lemon), and sea shell/iodine minerality. Bright, cool citrus (lemon) and green apple and pear are echoed in the flavors. The wine structure is lean yet has a crisp, racy minerality with a persistent finish.

title: Domaine Vocoret Chablis Grand Cru Blanchot

paras.text: Very brilliant pale crystal colour, nose of lemons, buttered apples on layers of toasted oak and hazelnuts allied with a fabulous freshness and a mineral palate with notes of apricots. Full bodied.

title: Domaine Vocoret Chablis Grand Cru Les Clos

paras.text: The palate is well-balanced with good acidity and depth, plenty of fresh citrus fruit intermingling with pear and orange peel, and the oak nicely interwoven on the finish. Give this a year or two to allow the aromatics to fully integrate.

title: Domaine Vocoret Chablis Grand Cru Valmur

paras.text: Considered one of the finest grands crus in Chablis, Valmur hails from a small valley in the heart of Chablis’ grands crus vineyards, butting up to Les Clos on the east, with Vaudésir to the north and Grenouilles to the south. Kimmeridgian limestone with marl topsoil. Fermented entirely in oak puncheons for 8 to 10 months.

title: Domaine Vocoret Chablis Grand Cru Vaudésir

paras.text: Vaudesir's Grand Cru has a unique topography shaped like an ampitheater. Vocoret’s vines benefit from southern exposure and a slightly warmer micro-climate, ample sunlight providing full phenolic maturity, and the steep slopes allow protection from the northern winds.

title: Domaine Vocoret Chablis Premier Cru Les Forets Vieilles Vignes

paras.text: Named for a very small forest located at the top of the vineyards, La Forêt is considered the best portion of the larger Montsmains vineyard. A wine to enjoy in its youth or cellar for many years.

Pale yellow-gold color. Sexy aromas of fresh apricot, licorice, ginger and toast, with a note of exotic flowers emerging with air. Nicely sweet and penetrating, offering a distinctly tactile mouth-feel to the stone fruit, licorice and spicy oak flavors. A touch of rusticity here but has excellent material.
The premiers crus wines are fermented in a combination of stainless steel tanks and 500-liter puncheons for eight months.

title: Domaine Vocoret Chablis Premier Cru Vaillon

paras.text: Liberal ripe Meyer lemon, citrus blossoms and spice aromas are accented by notes of seaside
minerality. Flavors are layered with citrus, orchard fruit and clean oyster-shell minerality. A generous wine with great energy and vibrancy and will reward with additional cellaring.
Aging: The premiers crus wines are fermented in a combination of stainless steel and oak puncheons for seven months.

title: Domaine Vocoret Chablis Premier Cru Montée de Tonnerre

paras.text: Considered one of the very best 1er cru of Chablis. The vineyard is on the right bank of the Serein, just next to the grand cru hill. The vineyards face southwest and the soil is very similar to that of the grand cru sites. There is a sandy topsoil with a Kimmeridgian limestone subsoil.

title: Domaine Xavier Frissant Touraine Sauvignon Blanc

paras.text: Situation: Plot located at the south end of the vineyard on the place said "the slopes" Grape varieties: 100% Sauvignon Blanc Soil: stony hillside, with a clay soil, sand-sand Conduct of the vineyard: reasoned viticulture with heavy weed pressure natural. Size guyot Harvest, winemaking and farming: The yields of the harvest are of 55 hl/ha. After a destemming and crushing, we achieved a pressing tire of the grape harvest. The product are at low temperature, and last 30 days.

title: Dominique Mugneret Bourgogne Hautes-Côtes de Nuits
Dominique Mugneret Bourgogne Pinot Noir Vieilles Vignes

paras.text: From a selection of the best older vines from Vosne-Romanee and Morey-St.-Denis, Dominique crafts this rich Pinot Noir. Ruby in color, this wine has great texture with red and black fruits and hints of lavender.

title: Dominique Mugneret Echezeaux Grand Cru En Orveaux
Dominique Mugneret Gevrey-Chambertin Les Seuvrées

paras.text: A lovely bottle of Pinot Noir. Well balanced and with nice undertones of berries.

title: Dominique Mugneret Nuits-Saint-Georges Premier Cru Aux Boudots

paras.text: Light ruby, turning garnet. Blackcurrant, cassis, spices, liquorice. Med-full bodied, rich and concentrated, well integrated tannins, some sharpness, pepper, charcoal, dry long finish. Lovely!

title: Dominique Mugneret Romanée-Saint-Vivant Grand Cru

paras.text: Depth, concentration, and complex but with elegant ripe fruit and spice with a finish of moderate tannins and great minerality.

title: Dominique Mugneret Vosné-Romanée Alliance des Terroirs

paras.text: Spicy Pinot Noir with tastes of both red and dark fruit. Traditional Vosne Romanee texture with a laidback elegance to it.

title: Dominique Mugneret Vosne-Romanée
Dominique Mugneret Vosné-Romanée Premier Cru Au Dessus Des Malconsorts

paras.text: Dominique Mugneret Vosné-Romanée Premier Cru Au Dessus Des Malconsorts | Fine Vines
Vinification: 100% de-stemmed, 4 to 6 days cold maceration (13-14°C), alcoholic fermentation at 22°C, 12 to 16 days in tank total. 16 to 17 months aging in oak barrels (50% new).

title: Dominique Mugneret Vosné-Romanée Premier Cru Les Chaumes
Dr. Konstantin Frank Cabernet Franc

paras.text: Lighter in color and style. Medium intensity with cranberry, raspberry, cracked pepper, dark cherry, and slight toastiness from oak. Soft earthy tannins are balanced perfectly with vibrant acidity.

100% Cabernet Franc from two plots on our estate Keuka Lake property planted in the late 1980’s. The vineyards are characterized by shallow, shale based soils with high natural acidity and steep slopes. These vineyards influence the minerality and acid structure and the steep slopes provide excellent water and air drainage.

title: Dr. Konstantin Frank Dry Riesling

paras.text: A crisp acidity and characteristic Keuka Lake minerality enhance the lively lemon, green apple and floral notes of this wine.

title: Dr. Konstantin Frank Salmon Run Chardonnay

paras.text: The perfect marriage of Chardonnay and Riesling! Aromas of pear, stone fruits, and lemon are supported by light pine notes and finished with a mineral backbone.

title: Dr. Konstantin Frank Semi-Dry Riesling

paras.text: Medium intensity with dominant characters of apricot, honeysuckle, stone fruit and vibrant citrus finish. The light sweetness is well balanced by a soft acidity. A versatile refreshing wine to enjoy on its own or with a wide range of foods.

Dr. Konstantin Frank ignited the “Vinifera Revolution”, a movement that forever changed the course of wine growing in the Finger Lakes and the United States. Dr. Frank’s vision, knowledge and determination are credited with elevating the New York wine industry from a state of happy mediocrity to a level that today commands world attention. Located on Keuka lake in the Finger Lakes region, Dr. Konstantin Frank Wines features some of the oldest vinifera vines in the United States and continues to produce wines of distinction and quality.

The fruit is picked in the early morning to retain freshness and fermented at low temperatures in stainless steel tanks. The fermentation was stopped before dryness to preserve the fruity character of this wine.

title: Eyrie Chasselas Doré

paras.text: Chasselas Doré is an old grape variety born in the Jura and Alps mountain ranges of Switzerland. Fresh, tropical and savory, it is light on its feet while having a surprising amount of structure and body for a wine with just 10% alcohol. Serve chilled, it will pair nicely with creamy cheeses, fresh veggies and spicy foods.

This wine is made from two rows of organically grown, ungrafted vines in our Sisters Vineyard. The attentive vineyard practices we demand focus on rigorous training of the vines, minimal interference with the ecosystem, and on picking at the optimal time. Insecticides, herbicides, and systemic chemicals are never used in the vineyards. In the winery, we refrain from unnecessarily manipulating the wines during their fermentation and maturation, allowing them to reflect the vintage.

title: Eyrie Vineyard Pinot Noir Original Vines Reserve

paras.text: The Original Vines has a rich nose with dark fruit and plenty of earth. On the palate, the ripe fruit from the warm summer blends intriguingly with a bright acidity brought on by the cool-down at harvest, providing the best of both worlds!

Produced from the oldest Pinot Noir vines in the Willamette Valley, this extraordinary wine is history in a bottle. Glorious aromatics offer intense scents of citrus, pine needles, pepper and berry, with flavors following. There's a welcome kick of citrus in the natural acidity, and this promises a long cellar life, as proven over and over again by this founding Oregon Winery. Drink 2020 through 2040 and beyond. Cellar Selection -WE

title: Eyrie Vineyard Pinot Noir Roland Greens Vineyard

paras.text: Named for David Lett’s father Roland Green Lett, the 5 acres of Pinot here were planted in 1988 to Pommard and Wadenswil clones. This direct south-facing vineyard provides wines of great texture, depth and finesse from a nearly perfect site.

Light reddish purple color in the glass. Welcoming perfume of fresh black cherry and savory herbs. Delicious mid weight black cherry core framed by healthy tannins and lively acidity. Amazingly generous and long finish. A special wine.

title: Eyrie Vineyards Chardonnay Original Vines

paras.text: The Chardonnay Original Vines is a barrel selection. Since each barrel ferments with its own yeast and ages at its own rate, each barrel becomes very distinct. Before bottling, Jason tastes each barrel. Those barrels which speak to the longest aging potential become the Original Vines Reserve.

The Chardonnay Original Vines Reserve has a gorgeous bouquet with scents of honeycomb, citrus fruit, wet wool and minerals that for me demonstrate a little more precision than its 2014 counterpart, at least at the moment. The palate is medium-bodied with finely tuned acidity, hints of brioche, Conference pear, a dab of lemongrass and a poised, tensile finish. This is an outstanding Chardonnay from winemaker Jason Lett. --WA

title: Eyrie Vineyards Chardonnay Estate

paras.text: The Chardonnay estate is a barrel selection. Since each barrel ferments with its own yeast and ages at its own rate, each barrel becomes very distinct. Before bottling, Jason tastes each barrel. Those barrels which speak to the longest aging potential become the Original Vines Reserve. This estate, on the other hand, is blended from those barrels which offer the most immediate pleasure.

Vivid straw. Pungent Meyer lemon and yellow apple scents show very good clarity and complicating hints of tarragon and smoky lees. Minerally and precise on the palate, offeing zesty pear and lime flavors and deeper suggestions of buttered toast and honey that build on the back half. Shows very good energy and finishes silky and long, with a subtle floral nuance hanging on. --Vinous

title: Eyrie Vineyards Dundee Hills Pinot Gris

paras.text: The Pinot Gris presents concentrated aromatics of pear, citrus, and spring greens. The palate unfolds a spectrum of pome fruits and crushed fennel. The racy natural acidity is complemented by a texture that is round while still being dry and light. Refreshing, direct, with the focused acidity and lingering finish that define Eyrie Pinot gris.
Eyrie pioneered the variety in the New World and the New World’s oldest vines contribute to this cuvée.

We take a slow approach—our Pinot gris ages 3-4 times longer than most commercial versions, on its natural yeast lees and in the company of full malolactic. The result is textural suppleness to complement the acidity, and a surprising ability to age. (Recent tastings of 1977, 1983, 1989, and 1991 all continue to show amazing freshness.)

title: Eyrie Vineyards The Eyrie Pinot Noir
